सामिधेन्य: सामिधेन्य सामिधेन्य, अस्, m. (fr. सम्-इन्ध् or सम्-इध्), a particular Mantra or mystical prayer.
सामिधेनी: सामिधेनी, f. a particular prayer or verse recited whilst the sacrificial fire is being kindled or on add-ing fuel to it (= धाय्या); fuel.
सामीप्य: सामीप्य सामीप्य, अम्, n. (fr. समीप), near-ness, vicinity, proximity, contiguity, nearness to the deity (as one of the four or five states or grades of beatitude); (अस्), m. a neighbour.
सामुदायिक: सामुदायिक सामुदायिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सम्-उदाय), belonging to a multitude or assemblage, collective.
सामुद्र: सामुद्र 1. सामुद्र, अम्, n. (fr. 1. स-मुद्र), an impression or mark on the body, spot.

सामुद्र 2. सामुद्र, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. 2. सम्-उद्र), oceanic, marine, sea-born; declared or re-lated by Samudra; (अस्), m. a mariner, voyager, sailor; (ई), f., N. of the daughter of Samudra and wife of Prācīna-barhis; (अम्), n. sea-salt; a cuttle-fish bone.
सामुद्रक: 1. सामुद्रक, अम्, n., N. of a work describing the various marks on the bodies of men and women, (so called, according to one account, because com-posed by Samudra; see 2. सामुद्र below.) —सामु-द्रक-विद्या, f. the art of interpreting the marks of the body, palmistry.
सामुद्रिक: 1. सामुद्रिक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to marks on the body, (सामुद्रिका गुनाः, qualities denoted by marks on the body); connected with good or bad fortune supposed to be indicated by marks or spots on the body; (अस्), m. an interpreter or describer of marks or spots on the body; a fortune-teller; (अम्), n. palmistry, N. of a work on this subject; [cf. 1. सामुद्रक above.] —सामुद्रिकाचार्य (°क-आच्°), अस्, m. a proper N.
2. सामुद्रिक, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to the sea or ocean, oceanic.
सामोद: सामोद सामोद, अस्, आ, अम्, (fr. स-आम्°), joy-ful, pleased; possessing fragrance, fragrant, odori-ferous.
सामोद्भव: सामोद्भव सामोद्भव, &c. See under सा-मन्, p. 1107.
साम्पराय: साम्पराय साम्पराय, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सम्-पराय), relating to war or battle, warlike; relating to the other world or a future state, belonging to the future; (अस्, अम्), m. n. contention, conflict; the future, future life; means of attaining a future world; inquiry into the future; investigation (in general); uncertainty.
साम्परायिक: साम्परायिक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to war, military, strategic; warlike; calamitous; relating to the other world or a future state, belonging to future time, future; (अस्), m. a war-chariot; (अम्), n. war, battle. —साम्परायिक-कल्प, अस्, m. military form, strategic array.
साम्पश्य: साम्पश्य साम्पश्य, अस्, &c. (fr. rt. 1. पश् with सम्), Ved. causing mutual looks (of love), forcing mutual glances (of affection; said of a herb used in charms or philters).
साम्प्रतम्: साम्प्रतम् साम्प्रतम्, ind. (fr. सम्-प्रति), now, at this time; seasonably, fitly, properly; [cf. अ-स्°।]
साम्प्रतिक: साम्प्रतिक, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to the present time, present (not future), suitable to the present occasion, suitable.
साम्प्रदायिक: साम्प्रदायिक साम्प्रदायिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सम्-प्रदाय), traditional, belonging to traditional doctrine, handed down by tradition.
साम्प्रयोगिक: साम्प्रयोगिक साम्प्रयोगिक, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सम्-प्रयोग), relating to sexual union.
साम्ब्: साम्ब् साम्ब् (= rt. सम्ब्), cl. 10. P. साम्-बयति, -यितुम्, to accumulate, collect.
साम्ब: साम्ब साम्ब (स-अम्°), अस्, m. attended by Ambā (said of Śiva). —सांब-शिव, अस्, m. Śiva along with Ambā.
साम्बन्धिक: साम्बन्धिक साम्बन्धिक, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सम्-बन्ध), belonging to or proceeding from relation-ship; (अम्), n. (probably) alliance.
साम्बर: साम्बर 1. साम्बर, अम्, n. (fr. सम्बर, q. v.), a kind of salt (= गड-लवण).
साम्बर 2. साम्बर (स-अम्°), अस्, आ, अम्, hav-ing clothes, clothed.
साम्बरी: साम्बरी साम्बरी, f. (also written शाम्बरी, q. v.), a female juggler, sorceress.
साम्बवती: साम्बवती साम्बवती, f., N. of a woman.
साम्बेश्वर: साम्बेश्वर (°ब-ईश्°), अस्, m., N. of a particular idol or of a temple built by Sāmbavatī.
साम्भवी: साम्भवी साम्भवी, f. (fr. सम्-भव), pos-sibility, probability; the red Lodhra tree.
साम्भस्: साम्भस् साम्भस् (स-अम्°), आस्, आस्, अस्, hav-ing water, containing water, watery.
साम्मद: साम्मद साम्मद, अस्, m. (fr. सम्-मद), a patronymic of the Vedic Ṛṣi Matsya (the author of a hymn in the Ṛg-veda, according to some).
साम्मातुर: साम्मातुर साम्मातुर, अस्, m. (fr. सम्-मातृ), a patronymic.
साम्मुख्य: साम्मुख्य साम्मुख्य, अम्, n. (fr. सम्-मुख), the state of being present face to face or in front, presence, favour, countenance.
साम्य: साम्य साम्य, अम्, n. (fr. 1. सम), even-ness, equality, parity, sameness, equipoise; likeness, similarity; harmony; equability; impartiality, indif-ference. —साम्य-ता, f. or साम्य-त्व, अम्, n. equality, sameness. —साम्य-बोधक, अस्, इका, अम्, expressive of similarity. —साम्यावस्था (°य-अव्°), f. equal state, equipoise.
साम्राज्य: साम्राज्य साम्राज्य, अम्, n. (fr. सम्-राज्), complete or universal sovereignty, empire, dominion; (अस्), m. the descendant of a king or Kṣatriya. —साम्राज्य-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, one who exercises im-perial sway, obtaining complete sovereignty. —सा-म्राज्य-दीक्षित, अस्, आ, अम्, consecrated to universal empire.
साम्राणिकर्दम: साम्राणिकर्दम साम्राणि-कर्दम, अम्, n. (ac-cording to Śabda-k.) a kind of perfume or mixture of fragrant substances (= जवादि-नामक-गन्ध-द्रव्य).
साम्राणिज: साम्राणि-ज, अम्, n. a kind of tree (= महा-पारेवत).
साय: साय साय, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 1. सो, cf. अव-सो, 1. अव-साय, दिवसावसान), end, close, termina-tion; the close of day, evening; an arrow; (अम्), ind. the evening; Evening personified as a son of Puṣpārṇa and Prabhā [cf. प्रातर्, मध्यन्-दिन]; in the evening; (ए), ind. in the evening, at the close of day; [cf. according to some, Lat. serus, but recent authorities refer serus to rt. सृ।] —सायं-सन्ध्या, f. the evening twilight; the goddess to be worshipped at the evening twilight or the time at which she is worshipped. —सायं-सन्ध्या-देवता, f. ‘the deity of the evening twi-light,’ epithet of Sarasvatī. —सायङ्-काल, अस्, m. evening, eventide. —सायङ्कालीन, अस्, आ, अम्, be-longing to evening, vespertine. —सायङ्-गृह, अस्, m., N. of a Muni. —सायन्-धृति, इस्, f. the even-ing Homa or oblation. —सायन्-निवास, अस्, m. evening abode, evening resting-place. —साय-मण्-डन, अम्, n. ‘evening-ornament,’ sunset. —सायम्-अधिवास, अस्, m. ‘evening-decoration,’ N. of the ceremony of decorating an image of Durgā on the fifth day of the month Āśvina. —सायाह्न (°य-अह्°), अस्, m. the evening, eventide.
साय, अस्, m. end, close, &c. See p. 1109, col. 1.
सायक: सायक, अस्, इका, अम्, Ved. destroying; (अस्), m. an arrow [cf. 2. शायक]; a sword, any weapon, a thunderbolt, (enumerated among the वज्र-नामानि in Naigh. II. 20); (इका), f. the being or standing in regular order, = क्रम-स्थिति; (अम्), n., Ved. an arrow. —सायक-पुङ्खा, f. the feathered end of an arrow. —सायक-प्रणुत्त, अस्, आ, अम्, driven away by arrows, put to flight by arrows. —सायक-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of arrows.
सायकायन: सायकायन, अस्, m. a proper N.
सायन्तन: सायन्तन, अस्, ई, अम् [cf. चिरन्तन], belonging to evening, vespertine.
सायम्प्रातिक: सायम्प्रातिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सायम्-प्रातर्; cf. पौनःपुनिक), belonging to evening and morning.
सायण: सायण सायण or सायणाचार्य (°ण-आच्°), अस्, m., N. of a learned Brāhman (thought to have flourished about A. D. 1370, and celebrated as a well-known commentator on the Ṛg-veda, Śata-patha-Brāhmaṇa, Tāṇḍya-Brāhmaṇa, and other works; he was associated in many of his writings with his elder brother Mādhava, also called Vidyā-raṇya, who became prime minister to two kings, Bukka-rāya and Harihara, after having aided them to found a new capital, called Vijaya-nagara, in the native kingdom of Karnāṭa about A. D. 1344).
सायणीय: सायणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to or composed by Sāyaṇa.
सायन: सायन सायन (स-अय्°), अम्, n. the longi-tude of a planet reckoned from the vernal equi-noctial point.
सायवस: सायवस सायवस, अस्, m. a proper N.
सायिन्: सायिन् सायिन्, ई, m. (according to some) a horseman (= अश्वारोह; cf. सादिन्).
सायुज्य: सायुज्य सायुज्य, अम्, n. (fr. स-युज्), inti-mate union, identification, absorption (especially into the divine essence; this is one of the four or five grades or states into which Mukti is distinguished; cf. ब्रह्म-स्°); similarity, likeness; [cf. राज-स्°।]
सायुध: सायुध सायुध (स-आय्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having weapons, armed. —सायुध-प्रग्रह, अस्, आ, अम्, holding weapons in the hand.
सार्: सार् सार् = rt. शार्, q. v.
सार: सार सार, अस्, m. (fr. rt. सृ, ‘to go, pervade,’ apparently involving in some of its deriva-tives a meaning ‘to be strong, to be whole or entire,’ cf. सर्व), essence, substance; the substantial or essential part of anything; the best or choicest part; the quintessence; the heart; the matter (of a book, speech, &c.; also अम्, n., according to some); real meaning, main point, real truth, (also अम्, n.); marrow; pith; the sap of trees and plants, (also अम्, n.); cream, curds; nectar; the matter formed in a boil or ulcer, pus; strength, power, vigour, force, courage, prowess, valour, heroism; firmness, hardness; worth, excellence, highest degree of per-fection; wealth, goods, riches; a compendium, sum-mary, epitome; impure carbonate of soda; sickness, disease [cf. सारण ]; air, wind; (अस्, ई), m. f. a chess-man, piece at chess or backgammon [cf. शार, शारि]; (आ), f. a kind of plant (= कृष्ण-त्रिवृता); Dūrvā grass; Kuśa grass; (ई), f. a kind of bird (= सारिका); a kind of plant, = सप्तला; (अम्), n. pith; sap; water; fresh butter; wealth; propriety, fitness; steel; a wood, thicket, = विपिन; (in rhe-toric) a climax; (अस्, आ, अम्), essential, substantial; vigorous, strong, hard; excellent; good, sound, best; real, true, genuine; sound (as an argument), thoroughly proved; [cf. Lat. serum.] —सार-खदि-र, अस्, m. ‘hard Khadira,’ a kind of Acacia Catechu (= दुष्-खदिर). —सार-गन्ध, अस्, m. ‘hav-ing the perfection of scent,’ sandal-wood. —सार-गीता, f., N. of a short work on Yoga. —सार-ग्रा-हिन्, ई, इणी, इ, extracting the essence or best part of anything. —सार-ग्रीव, अस्, m. ‘strong-necked,’ epi-thet of Śiva. —सार-ज, अम्, n. ‘produced from cream,’ fresh butter; [cf. सर-ज।] —सार-तरु, उस्, m. ‘pith tree, sap tree,’ the plantain tree (= कदल, q. v.; so called as containing no hard wood in the stem). —सार-तस्, ind. essentially, from strength, by or with vigour, vigorously, according to wealth, with regard to riches. —सार-ता, f. or सार-त्व, अम्, n. essence, substance; strength; highest degree. —सार-दा, f. ‘force-giver,’ epithet of Sarasvatī (goddess of speech); of Durgā. —सार-द्रुम, अस्, m. ‘hard. tree,’ the Khadira tree. —सार-पादप, अस्, m. a particular plant or tree, (probably = धामनी।) —सार-फल्गुत्व, अम्, n. substance and emptiness, importance and insignifi-cance. —सार-भङ्ग, अस्, अम्, m. n. destruction or loss of vigour; (अस्, आ, अम्), deprived of substance or strength. —सार-भट्टारक, अस्, m., N. of an author. —सार-भाण्ड, अम्, n. a natural vessel (as the bag or skin containing the musk of the musk-deer); a bale of goods; implements. —सार-भुज्, क्, क्, क्, eating the essence or best part of anything. —सार-मञ्जरी, f., N. of a commentary by Śrī-nātha-śarman on the Pariśiṣṭa-prakāśa. —सार-मिति, इस्, m. ‘truth-measuring, truth-determining,’ the Veda. —सार-मूषिका, f. a kind of plant (= देव-दाली). —सार-योग, अस्, m. possession of the essence or substance of anything. —सार-लहरी, f., N. of a grammatical work by Kavi-candra. —सार-लोह, अम्, n. ‘the essence of iron,’ steel. —सार-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having substance, substantial; hav-ing pith or sap; fertile. —सारवत्-ता, f. substanti-ality, hardness, force, strength. —सार-वर्जित, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘devoid of substance,’ pithless, sapless. —सार-सङ्ग्रह, अस्, m. concentration of essence; N. of a philosophical work by Varada-rāja; of a work on the proper seasons for performing ceremonies or for commencing other undertakings. —सार-समुच्-चय, अस्, m., N. of a work. —सार-सिद्धान्त-कौमुदी, f., N. of a work by Varada-rāja-bhaṭṭa. —सारापराध-तस् (°र-अप्°), ind. in accordance with proved offences or crimes. —सारावली (°र-आव्°), f., N. of a work [cf. स्मृति-स्°]; of a work on astronomy. —सारासार (°र-अस्°), अस्, आ, अम्, substantial and unsubstantial, valuable and worthless, real and vain; (अम्), n. substance and emptiness; strength and weakness; worth and worthlessness. —सारासार-ता, f. the state of being substantial and unsubstantial or of having strong or weak points, &c. —सारासार-विचार, अस्, m. the considering or weighing of strong and weak points. —सारी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, -कर्तुम्, to make hard. —सारोद्-धार (°र-उद्°), N. of a work on music.
सारक: सारक, अस्, इका, अम् (fr. Caus. of rt. सृ), causing to go; cathartic, laxative; (अस्), m. a particular plant (= जय-पाल).
सारण: सारण, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. Caus. of rt. सृ), caus-ing to go or flow; (अस्), m. dysentery, diarrhœa [cf. अति-सार]; the hog-plum, Spondias Mangifera; another plant (= भद्र-बला); N. of one of Rā-vaṇa's ministers (sent as ambassador to Rāma); (अम्), n. a kind of perfume.
सारणा: सारणा, f. a particular process to which mineral substances (especially quicksilver) are subjected, (two others are given, called ऋतु-स्° and प्रति-स्°।) —सा-रणा-त्रय, अम्, n. the three Sāraṇā processes.
सारणि: सारणि, इस्, f. a canal, drain, channel, water-pipe; a small river; the plant Pæderia Fetida; [cf. सा-रणी।]
सारणिक: सारणिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सरणि), travelling, wayfaring, journeying; (अस्), m. a traveller, way-farer. —सारणिक-घ्न, अस्, m. ‘killing travellers,’ a robber, highwayman, murderer.
सारणिका: सारणिका, f., N. of a short treatise on astrology.
सारि: सारि, इस्, f. a chess-man, &c. (= सार, सारी). —सारि-फलक, अस्, m. a chess-board, draught-board; a table for playing chess or backgammon; [cf. शारि-फ्°।] —सारिम्-एजय, अस्, m., N. of a chieftain.
सारि सारि, सारिन्, &c. See p. 1109, col. 3.
सारिका: सारिका, f. a kind of bird (= शारिका, श्यामा); N. of a Rākṣasī.
सारिन्: सारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, going, resorting to, &c. (gene-rally at the end of a comp., e. g. ओकः-सारिन्, going home); having the essence or substance of; (इणी), f., N. of various plants (= सह-देवी; = कार्पासी; = दुर्-आलभा; = कपिल-शिंशपा; = प्र-सारिणी; = रक्त-पुनर्नवा).
सारिवा: सारिवा, f. a kind of plant (= शारिवा).
सारी: सारी, f. See under सार, col. 2.
सारघ: सारघ सारघ, अम्, n. (fr. सरघा), honey.
सारङ्ग: सारङ्ग सारङ्ग, अस्, ई, अम्, (probably fr. अ-रङ्ग, ‘having colour, &c.;’ but cf. शार, शारङ्ग; according to Uṇādi-s. I. 121. fr. rt. सृ), of a variegated colour, variegated, spotted [cf. कृष्-ण-स्°, लोहित-स्°]; (अस्), m. a variegated colour; the spotted antelope; a deer; a lion; an elephant; the Cātaka bird, Cuculus Melanoleucus; the Indian cuckoo; a kind of large crane, Ardea Sarunga; a peacock; the Rāja-haṃsa; a large bee; a cloud; a tree; an umbrella, parasol; a garment, cloth, cloths; hair; a lotus; a flower; a conch-shell; a sort of musical instrument; an ornament, jewel; gold; a bow; epithet of Śiva; of Kāma-deva; sandal; camphor; the earth; night; light; (ई), f. a kind of spotted doe or antelope; a sort of violin. —सारङ्ग-देव, अस्, m., N. of a king. —सारङ्ग-रङ्ग-दा, f., N. of a commentary on the Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta.
सारङ्गिक: सारङ्गिक, अस्, m. a bird-catcher, fowler, hunter, deer-catcher, &c.
सारण्ड: सारण्ड सारण्ड, अस्, m. = सर्पाण्ड, a snake's egg.
सारण्यक: सारण्यक सारण्यक (स-आर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, hav-ing the Āraṇyakas, together with the Āraṇyakas.
सारथि: सारथि सारथि, इस्, m. (fr. स-रथ), the son of a Sa-ratha (see स-रथ); a charioteer, driver of a car, coachman, (forming a mixed caste, com-monly called Sārthī, and supposed to have sprung from a Kṣatriya father and Brāhman mother); the ocean (= 1. सम्-उद्र।)
सारथिन्: सारथिन्, ई, m., Ved. a charioteer, (Atharva-veda XV. 2, 1.)
सारथ्य: सारथ्य, अम्, n. the office of a charioteer, coach-manship, charioteering, driving; conveyance.
सारमेय: सारमेय सारमेय, अस्, m. (fr. सरम, q. v.), a dog; (औ), m. du. the two children of Saramā, i. e. the two four-eyed brindled watch-dogs of Yama (conjectured by some to have been origin-ally Indra and Agni); (ई), f. a female dog, bitch; [cf. probably Gr. Ἑρμείας.] —सारमेय-वाक्य, अम्, n. ‘Sārameya's speech,’ N. of the fifty-sixth chapter of the Uttara-kāṇḍa of the Rāmāyaṇa.
सारयत्: सारयत् सारयत्, &c. See under rt. सृ।
सारयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, causing to go, putting in the proper place, fixing, adjusting, replacing; causing to go away, removing.
सारल्य: सारल्य सारल्य, अम्, n. straightness, recti-tude, sincerity, uprightness, honesty, artlessness.
सारव: सारव सारव, अस्, ई, अम्, (anomalously fr. सरयु), being on or belonging to the Sarayu river.
सारशन: सारशन सारशन, अम्, n. (fr. स-रशन), a woman's zone or girdle (said to be formed of twenty-five strings); a military belt or girdle.
सारस: सारस सारस, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सरस्), relating or belonging to a lake or pond, coming from a lake; (अस्), m. the Indian or Siberian crane, Ardea Sibirica; a bird in general [cf. राज-स्°]; the moon; (अम्), n. a lotus; a woman's zone or girdle; [cf. सारशन।] —सारस-द्वितीय, अस्, आ, अम्, accom-panied by a Sārasa or Indian crane.
सारसी: सारसी, f. a female Indian crane.
सारस्वत: सारस्वत सारस्वत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सरस्-वती), relating or belonging to the river Sarasvatī; relating to the goddess Sarasvatī; being in the form of Sarasvatī; eloquent, learned; belonging to the Sārasvata country; (अस्), m., N. of the country about the Sarasvatī river (i. e. the north-west part of the province of Delhi including part of the Pañjāb); N. of a Muni or saint (fabled to have sprung from the personified Sarasvatī river); N. of a particular tribe of Brāhmans (so called as coming from the above country or as supposed to be de-scended from the above Muni; they are said to be subdivided into ten classes, and to be often cultivators of literature); a staff of the Vilva tree; a particular ceremonial used in the worship of Sarasvatī; = सारस्-वत-प्रक्रिया below; (आस्), m. pl. the people of the Sārasvata country; (ई), f., scil. प्रक्रिया = सारस्-वत-प्रक्रिया. —सारस्वत-कल्प, अस्, m. the ceremonial used in the worship of Sarasvatī. —सा-रस्वत-कोष and सारस्वत-तन्त्र, N. of two works. —सारस्वत-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —सारस्वत-प्रक्रिया, f., N. of a grammatical work by Anubhūti-svarūpācārya. —सारस्वत-व्रत, अस्, अम्, m. n. a particular religious observance in honour of Sarasvatī. —सारस्वतालङ्कार (°त-अल्°), अस्, m., N. of a work. —सारस्वतोत्सव (°त-उत्°), अस्, m. the festival in honour of Sarasvatī.
सारस्वत्य: सारस्वत्य, अस्, &c., belonging to the Sārasvata family or tribe, (सारस्वत्यो गणः, the descendants or family of Sārasvata.)
साराल: साराल साराल, अस्, m. sesamum (= तिल).
सारिसृक्त: सारिसृक्त सारिसृक्त, अस्, m. (probably ano-mal. fr. the Intens. of rt. 1. सृज्), N. of the author of Ṛg-veda X. 142, 5, 6 (having the patronymic Śāṅga).
सारु: सारु सारु (doubtful), a kind of metre.
सारुन्धतीक: सारुन्धतीक सारुन्धतीक (स-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, together with Arundhatī, accompanied by Arun-dhatī.
सारूप्य: सारूप्य सारूप्य, अम्, n. (fr. स-रूप), same-ness or similarity of form, conformity, resemblance; assimilation to or conformity with the deity (one of the states or grades of Mukti, = सरूप-ता, q. v.); (in the drama) surprise at seeing an object or its likeness previously seen elsewhere. —सारूप्य-तस्, ind. in consequence of similarity of form.
सारोप: सारोप सारोप (स-आर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, super-imponent.
सारोष्ट्रिक: सारोष्ट्रिक सारोष्ट्रिक, अस्, m. (corrupted fr. सौराष्ट्रिक, q. v.), a kind of poison.
सारोह: सारोह सारोह (स-आर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having elevation, rising.
सार्क: सार्क सार्क (स-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, with the sun, sunny.
सार्गल: सार्गल सार्गल (स-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having a bar or obstacle, barred, impeded, prevented, (Raghu-v. I. 79.)
सार्ञ्जय: सार्ञ्जय सार्ञ्जय, अस्, m. (fr. सृञ्जय), Ved. the son of Sṛñjaya.
सार्थ: सार्थ सार्थ (स-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having an object; having meaning, full of meaning or purport, significant, important; serving a purpose, useful, ser-viceable; of like meaning or purport; having pro-perty, opulent, wealthy; (अस्), m. a wealthy man; a company of traders, caravan; a multitude of similar animals; a troop; a collection or multitude (in general); one of a company of pilgrims. —सार्थ-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, born or reared in a caravan. —सार्-थ-भ्रंश-समुद्भव, अस्, आ, अम्, arising from the loss of a caravan. —सार्थ-मण्डल, अम्, n. the circle or collected body of a caravan. —सार्थ-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a meaning or purpose, signifi-cant, intending; having a numerous company. —सार्-थ-वाह, the leader or conductor of a caravan, a merchant, trader. —सार्थवाह-वचस्, अस्, n. the speech or proclamation of the captain of a caravan. —सार्थ-हन्, हा, घ्नी, ह, ‘caravan-destroyer,’ a robber who attacks a caravan.
सार्थक: सार्थक (स-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having meaning, full of meaning, important; serviceable, useful, ad-vantageous. —सार्थक-ता, f. the being adapted to any purpose, serviceableness.
सार्थिक: सार्थिक, अस्, m. a merchant, trader.
सार्द्र: सार्द्र सार्द्र (स-आर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, wet, moist, damp.
सार्ध: सार्ध सार्ध (स-अर्°), अस्, ई, अम्, joined with a half, plus one half, increased by one half, having a half over (e. g. द्वे शते सार्धे, two hundred toge-ther with a half, i. e. two hundred and fifty, Manu VIII. 138; used chiefly in comps., see below); (अम्), ind. with, along with, together with (with inst.). —सारध-शत, अम्, n. ‘a hundred + a half,’ 150. —सार्ध-संवत्सर, अस्, m. a year and a half.
सार्धमात्र: सार्धमात्र (स-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having a half Mātrā.
सार्प: सार्प सार्प, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to snakes or serpents; (अस्), m., N. of the Nakṣatra Āśleṣā.
सार्पराज्ञी: सार्पराज्ञी, f., N. of the authoress of the hymn Ṛg-veda X. 189.
सार्प्य: सार्प्य, अस्, -पी, अम्, relating to a snake; (अस्, पी), m. f., N. of the Nakṣatra Āśleṣā (over which the serpents are said to preside).
सार्पिष: सार्पिष सार्पिष, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सर्पिस्), con-taining clarified butter, cooked with ghee, dressed with clarified butter.
सार्पिष्क: सार्पिष्क, अस्, ई, अम्, = सार्पिष above.
सार्व: सार्व सार्व, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सर्व), relating to all, general, universal; fit for all; (अस्), m. a Buddha; a Jina or Jaina deified saint.
सार्वकामिक: सार्वकामिक, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सर्व-काम), ful-filling all desires, gratifying every wish.
सार्वकाल: सार्वकाल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सर्व-काल), taking place at all times, suitable for all seasons.
सार्वकालिक: सार्वकालिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सर्व-काल), belong-ing to all times, suited to all seasons, everlasting.
सार्वगुणिक: सार्वगुणिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सर्व-गुण), endued with every good quality or excellence.
सार्वजनिक: सार्वजनिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सर्व-जन), relating or belonging or suited to all men, universal, public.
सार्वजनीन: सार्वजनीन, अस्, ई, अम्, = सार्वजनिक above.
सार्वत्रिक: सार्वत्रिक, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सर्वत्र), belonging to every place, general, suited to all places or cir-cumstances.
सार्वदैवत्य: सार्वदैवत्य, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सर्व + देवता), presided over by or sacred to all the gods.
सार्वधातुक: सार्वधातुक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सर्व-धातु), applicable to the whole of a radical term or to the complete form of the verbal base after the conju-gational characteristics or Vikaraṇas are affixed, i. e. to the four conjugational or special tenses, &c. (see below; cf. आर्धधातुक); (अम्), n., N. of the verbal terminations of the four conjugational or special tenses (present, imperfect, potential, and imperative) and of all the root affixes (such as शानच् and शतृ) which have a servile or indicatory श्।
सार्वभौतिक: सार्वभौतिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सर्व-भूत), belonging or relating to all elements or beings, &c.; comprising all animated beings.
सार्वभौम: सार्वभौम, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सर्व-भूमि), relating to or consisting of the whole earth, com-prising the whole world, known throughout the world; (अस्), m. an emperor, universal monarch; N. of the elephant of Kuvera (regent of the north); N. of a king; of a poet. —सार्वभौम-भट्टा-चार्य, अस्, m., N. of a preceptor.
सार्वलौकिक: सार्वलौकिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सर्व-लोक), pre-vailing throughout the whole world, common to all the world, known by every one, universal.
सार्ववर्णिक: सार्ववर्णिक, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सर्व-वर्ण), of every kind or sort; belonging or relating to every tribe.
सार्ववर्मिक: सार्ववर्मिक, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सर्व-वर्मन्), composed or written by Sarva-varman; (अम्), n. any thing written by Sarva-varman.
सार्वविभक्तिक: सार्वविभक्तिक, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सर्व-विभक्ति), applicable or belonging to all the cases of a noun, &c.
सार्ववेदस: सार्ववेदस, अस्, m. (fr. सर्व-वेदस्, q. v.), one who gives away all his wealth at a sacred rite.
सार्ववेद्य: सार्ववेद्य, अस्, m. (fr. सर्व-वेद), a Brāhman conversant with all the Vedas.
सार्षप: सार्षप सार्षप, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सर्षप), made of mustard; (अम्), n. mustard oil.
सार्ष्टि: सार्ष्टि सार्ष्टि, इस्, इस्, इ (perhaps fr. स + आ + ऋष्टि; cf. ऋष्व), possessing the same rank or condition or station, having the same power or sub-limity; (अयस्), m. pl., N. of a Gotra.
सार्ष्टिता: सार्ष्टि-ता, f. equality in rank or condition, equality in power, &c. (according to Kullūka on Manu IV. 232 = समान-गति-ता, तुल्य-ता; in a passage of the Mahā-nārāyaṇa Upaniṣad, Sāy. explains सार्ष्टि-ता by समानैश्वर्य-त्व, which is said to mean here equality with the Supreme Being in power and all the divine attributes; it is regarded as the fourth grade or division of Mukti or final beatitude).
सार्ष्ट्य: सार्ष्ट्य, अम्, n. the fourth state of Mukti, = सार्-ष्टि-ता above.
साल: साल साल, अस्, m. (= शाल, q. v.), the Śāl tree or its resin; any tree; a fence or wall surround-ing a building; any wall; a kind of fish, Ophio-cephalus Wrahl; (आ), f. a house (more usually written शाला). —साल-ग्राम, अस्, m., N. of a sacred place; the Śāla-grāma stone, (see शाल-ग्राम।) —साल-ग्राम-क्षेत्र, अम्, n., N. of a district. —साल-ज्य, अम्, n., N. of a place. —साल-निर्यास, see शाल-निर्यास. —साल-पर्णी, see शाल-पर्णी। —साल-पुष्प, अम्, n. a flower of the Sāl tree; the shrub Hibiscus Mutabilis. —साल-भञ्जिका, see शाल-भञ्जिका. —साल-रस, अस्, m. the resin of the Sāl or Śāl tree. —साल-वाहन, incorrect for शालि-वाहन. —साल-वेष्ट, see शाल-वेष्ट. —सा-ल-शृङ्ग, अम्, n. ‘wall-pinnacle,’ the coping of a wall. —साल-सार, see शाल-सार. —साला-करी, f. (according to some) ‘house-worker,’ a female cap-tive (especially one won in battle). —साला-वृक, अस्, m. (see शाला-वृक), a dog; a jackal; a hyena; a wolf; a wolf-like or cruel man.
सालन: सालन, अस्, m. the resin of the Sāl or Śāl tree; resin (in general).
सालार: सालार, अम्, n. a pin or peg projecting from a wall, a bracket, shelf.
सालकि: सालकि सालकि, इस्, m., N. of a Muni.
सालङ्ग: सालङ्ग सालङ्ग, अस्, m. a kind of Rāga or musical mode.
सालम्ब: सालम्ब सालम्ब (स-आल्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having a support or prop, supported.
सालम्बन: सालम्बन (स-आल्°), अस्, आ, अम्, = सालम्ब above.
सालस: सालस सालस (स-अल्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having languor, languid, languishing.
सालातुरीय: सालातुरीय सालातुरीय, अस्, m. (for शालातु-रीय, q. v.), N. of Pāṇini.
सालिमञ्जरि: सालिमञ्जरि सालिमञ्जरि, इस्, m., N. of a Muni.
सालूर: सालूर सालूर, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. सल्), a frog (= शालूर).
सालेय: सालेय सालेय, अस्, m. a sort of fennel or dill (= शालेय).
सालोक्य: सालोक्य सालोक्य, अम्, n. (fr. स-लोक), the being in the same sphere or world (with another), residence in the same heaven with any particular deity (= सलोक-ता, q. v.). —सालोक्य-ता, f. = सालोक्य above.
साल्व: साल्व साल्व, अस्, m., N. of a demon-king who was slain by Viṣṇu, (according to the Śabda-k. he was king of the country of Saubha); N. of a country (more usually written शाल्व); (आस्), m. pl. the inhabitants of Sālva; (अस्, ई, अम्), belonging to the country Sālva. —साल्व-हन्, आ, m. ‘slayer of Sālva,’ N. of Viṣṇu.
साल्विक: साल्विक साल्विक, अस्, m. (probably a cor-ruption of सारिका, q. v.), the Sārikā bird.
साव: साव साव, अस्, m. (fr. 1. सव), a libation, in प्रातः-साव, q. v.
सावन: सावन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. 1. सवन), relating to or comprising the three Savanas; (अस्), m. an institutor of a sacrifice or employer of priests at a sacrifice (= यजमान); the conclusion of a sacrifice or the ceremonies by which it is terminated; N. of Varuṇa; a month of thirty solar days; a particular kind of day; a natural or civil day from sunrise to sunset; a particular kind of year (as distinguished from the solar year); a particular ceremony performed during the Sāvana month.
सावक: सावक सावक, अस्, इका, अम् (fr. the Caus. of rt. 4. सु), generative, productive, causing birth, &c., obstetric, parturient; the young of any animal (in this sense for शावक); (इका), f. a midwife.
सावकाश: सावकाश सावकाश (स-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, hav-ing leisure, at leisure; (अम्), ind. leisurely.
सावग्रह: सावग्रह सावग्रह (स-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, hav-ing the grammatical mark called Ava-graha, q. v.
सावज्ञ: सावज्ञ सावज्ञ (स-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, feeling contempt, despising, disdainful.
सावद्य: सावद्य सावद्य (स-अव्°), अम्, n., scil. ऐश्वर्-य, one of the three kinds of power attainable by an ascetic, (the other two are called निर्-अवद्य and सूक्ष्म।)
सावधान: सावधान सावधान (स-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having or bestowing attention, attentive, heedful, careful, cautious; diligent; (अम्), ind. cautiously. —सावधान-ता, f. attention, carefulness.
सावधानीकृ: सावधानी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to make careful, caution, put on one's guard.
सावधानीकृत: सावधानी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, cautioned, apprized, made aware.
सावधारण: सावधारण सावधारण (स-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, (in argumentative writings) having a limitation.
सावधि: सावधि सावधि (स-अव्°), इस्, इस्, इ, together with a limit or termination, having a bound or limit, limited (in time), finite, defined, circumscribed.
सावन्तमिश्र: सावन्तमिश्र सावन्त-मिश्र, अस्, m. a pro-per N.
सावयव: सावयव सावयव (स-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, com-posed of parts (in the Vaiśeṣika phil. said of all things except the eternal substances).
सावर: सावर सावर, अस्, m. (= शावर), fault, of-fence; sin, wickedness, crime; the Lodhra tree.
सावरण: सावरण सावरण (स-आव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, hav-ing concealment or secrecy, clandestine.
सावर्ण: सावर्ण सावर्ण, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. स-वर्ण), re-lating or belonging to one of the same colour or tribe or caste; (अस्), m. (fr. स-वर्णा), a metronymic of the eighth Manu, (see below.) —सावर्ण-लक्-ष्य, अम्, n. ‘mark of sameness of colour or caste,’ the skin.
सावर्णि: सावर्णि, इस्, m. a metronymic of the eighth Manu (son of the Sun by Sa-varṇā, q. v., and therefore younger brother of the seventh Manu or Vaivasvata; the succeeding Manus to the twelfth, or according to other authorities to the fourteenth, inclusive are also called Sāvarṇi; cf. दक्ष-स्°, ब्रह्म-स्°, धर्म-स्°); (अयस्), m. pl., N. of a Gotra.
सावर्णिक: सावर्णिक, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to Sāvarṇi, ar-ranged by Sāvarṇi (said of a Saṃhitā).
सावर्ण्य: सावर्ण्य, अम्, n. sameness or similarity of colour; identity of caste or class; the Manv-antara presided over by the eighth Manu (in this sense fr. सावर्णि); (अस्), m., Ved. the eighth Manu (= सावर्णि).
सावलम्ब: सावलम्ब सावलम्ब (स-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having a support or prop, supported, leaning for sup-port (on the arm of another).
सावलेप: सावलेप सावलेप (स-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, full of pride, proud; (अम्), ind. insolently, arrogantly, haughtily.
सावशेष: सावशेष सावशेष (स-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, hav-ing a remainder, leaving a residue or remainder, re-maining; imperfect, incomplete, unfinished. —सा-वशेष-बन्धन, अस्, आ, अम्, having bonds still remaining, still bound.
सावष्टम्भ: सावष्टम्भ सावष्टम्भ (स-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, possessing self-dependence, full of self-confidence; (अम्), ind. resolutely, courageously.
सावहेल: सावहेल सावहेल (स-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, dis-dainful, disdaining, despising; (अम्), ind. disdain-fully, contemptuously.
सावित्र: सावित्र सावित्र, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सवितृ), re-lating or belonging to the sun; descended from the sun, belonging to the solar dynasty; accompanied by the Gāyatrī (or sacred verse described below); (अस्), m. the sun; an embryo or fetus; a Brāhman; N. of Śiva; of Karṇa (as child of the Sun); of a Vasu, q. v.; of the tenth Kalpa (according to the Vāyu-Purāṇa); of one of the Nakṣatras or lunar aste-risms; (ई), f. a beam or ray of light, a cluster of solar rays; N. of a celebrated verse of the Ṛg-veda (III. 62, 10. regarded as the most sacred verse of the Veda, and called Sāvitrī as addressed to the sun; it is repeated by every Brāhman at his morning and evening devotions, and is also called गायत्री, see under गायत्र, p. 288); N. of a wife of Brahmā (sometimes regarded as the above verse or prayer deified and represented as mystical mother of the first three twice-born classes; sometimes identified with the daughter of Savitṛ by his wife Pṛśni); the ceremony of investiture with the sacred thread, (see उप-नय, p. 164, col. 3); a kind of metre; epithet of Sūryā (daughter of Savitṛ); of Umā (wife of Śiva); of a daughter of Dakṣa (wife of Dharma); of the wife of Kaśyapa; of the wife of Satya-vat (king of Śālva; she was daughter of Aśva-pati, king of Madra); (अम्), n. the sacred sacrificial thread worn only by Brāhmans and members of the first three classes, (see यज्ञोपवीत; it was called Sā-vitra because the repetition of the Gāyatrī forms part of the ceremony of investiture.) —सावित्री-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —सावित्री-पतित or सावित्री-परिभ्रष्ट, अस्, m. ‘fallen from the Sāvitrī,’ a man of one of the first three classes not invested at the proper time with the sacrificial cord. —सावित्री-महानाम्य, (according to some) the ceremony of investiture accompanied by repetition of the Gāyatrī. —सावित्री-व्रत, अम्, n. a particular fast (kept by Hindū women on the fourteenth day of the second half of the month Vaiśākha, or of the dark half of Jyaiṣṭha, to preserve them from widowhood). —सावित्री-सूत्र, अम्, n. the sacred cord or thread worn by men of the three twice-born classes, (see above.) —सावित्र्य्-अवरजा, f. the younger daughter of Sāvitrī.
साविष्कार: साविष्कार साविष्कार (स-आव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having manifestation, manifest; showing off or making an exhibition of any power or talent, proud, haughty, arrogant (= साहङ्कार).
सावेतस: सावेतस सावेतस, अस्, m., a proper N.
साशंस: साशंस साशंस (स-आश्°), अस्, आ, अम्, full of desire or strong passion, desirous, hopeful; (अम्), ind. wishfully.
साशङ्क: साशङ्क साशङ्क (स-आश्°), अस्, आ, अम्, feeling fear, apprehensive, disheartened, afraid. —साशङ्क-ता, f. the state of being afraid or apprehensive, fear, terror.
साशन: साशन साशन (स-अश्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having food, consisting of nourishment.
साशनार: साशनार साशनार, अस्, m., N. of a parti-cular Agra-hāra or royal grant to Brāhmans.
साशयन्दक: साशयन्दक साशयन्दक, अस्, m. a small house-lizard (= ज्येष्ठी).
साशूक: साशूक साशूक, अस्, m. a blanket (= कम्-बल).
साश्चर्य: साश्चर्य साश्चर्य (स-आश्°), अस्, आ, अम्, won-derful, marvellous, astonishing; (अम्), ind. with astonishment, with surprise. —साश्चर्य-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, wonderful, full of marvels.
साश्र: साश्र 1. साश्र (स-अश्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having angles or corners, cornered, angular.
साश्र 2. साश्र (स-अश्°), अस्, आ, अम्, tearful, weeping.
साश्रु: साश्रु (स-अश्°), उस्, उस्, उ, accompanied by tears, tearful, shedding tears. —साश्रु-नयन, अस्, आ, अम्, having the eyes filled with tears.
साश्रुधी: साश्रुधी साश्रुधी, f. a wife's or husband's mother, a mother-in-law.
साश्व: साश्व साश्व (स-अश्°), अस्, आ, अम्, possessing horses, with horses.
साष्टाङ्गम्: साष्टाङ्गम् साष्टाङ्गम् (स-अष्°), ind. with eight limbs or members (viz. the hands, breast, fore-head, knees, and feet); with humble prostration of the body (i. e. touching the earth with the eight members; cf. अष्टाङ्ग).
साष्ट्रक: साष्ट्रक साष्ट्रक (स-अष्°), अस्, इका, अम्, possessing goads, (see अष्ट्रा।)
सास: सास सास (स-आस), अस्, आ, अम्, having a bow.
सासार: सासार सासार (स-आस्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having showers, rainy.
सासि: सासि सासि (स-असि), इस्, इस्, इ, having a sword, armed with a sword.
सासुसू: सासुसू सासु-सू (स-अस्°), ऊस्, ऊस्, उ, having arrows, (see Kirāt. XV. 5, where, according to Malli-nātha, असु-सू = वाण।)
सासूय: सासूय सासूय (स-असूया), अस्, आ, अम्, envious, disdainful, scornful; (अम्), ind. disdainfully, scorn-fully, angrily.
सास्थिताम्रार्ध: सास्थिताम्रार्ध सास्थि-ताम्रार्ध, अम्, n. (fr. स + अस्थि + ताम्र + अर्ध), a kind of amalgam of zinc and copper, bell-metal (= कांस्य).
सास्ना: सास्ना सास्ना, f. (in Uṇādi-s. III. 15. said to be fr. rt. सस्), the dewlap of an ox (= गो-गल-कम्बल).
सास्र: सास्र 1. सास्र (स-अस्°), अस्, आ, अम् (for 1. साश्र, q. v.), having angles or corners, cornered, angular.
सास्र 2. सास्र (स-अस्°), अस्, आ, अम् (for 2. साश्र, q. v.), weeping, in tears.
सास्वादन: सास्वादन सास्वादन (स-आस्°), अम्, n., scil. स्थान, one of the steps towards supreme happiness (according to the Jainas).
साहङ्कार: साहङ्कार साहङ्कार (स-अह्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having egotism or arrogance, proud, arrogant.
साहचर्य: साहचर्य साहचर्य, अम्, n. (fr. सह-चर), companionship, fellowship, company, association, society.
साहञ्जि: साहञ्जि साहञ्जि, इस्, m., N. of a king.
साहदेव: साहदेव साहदेव, आस्, m. pl. (fr. सह-देव), the descendants of Saha-deva.
साहदेव्य: साहदेव्य, अस्, m., Ved. a patronymic of Somaka.
साहय: साहय, अस्, आ, अम्, causing or enabling to endure.
साहस: साहस साहस, अम्, n. (in Manu VIII. 138. also अस्, m.; fr. सहस्), violence, force, rapine, robbery, rape, felony, suicide; any act of aggression or oppression or hatred; cruelty; punishment, chas-tisement, fine (regarded as of three kinds, the highest being called Uttama; half of that, Madh-yama; and half of that, Adhama; see उत्तम-स्°, मध्यम-स्°); boldness, daring, courage, fool-hardiness, rashness, temerity, inconsiderate hastiness’ impetuosity; a particular sacred fire in which an oblation is made (in this sense अस्, m.), or the obla-tion itself (according to some). —साहसाङ्क (°स-अङ्°), अस्, m. ‘marked or characterized by daring,’ epithet of king Vikramāditya; of a poet; of a lexi-cographer. —साहसाध्यवसायिन् (°स-अध्°), ई, इनी, इ, acting with inconsiderate haste. —साहसैक-रसिक (°स-एक्°), अस्, ई, अम्, one whose only feeling or passion is cruelty, wholly intent on violence, brutal, ferocious. —साहसैकान्त-रसानुवर्तिन् (°स-एक्°, °स-अन्°), ई, इनी, इ, one who follows or yields to the one passion of cruelty or rashness.
साहसिक: साहसिक, अस्, ई, अम्, using great force or violence, violent, perpetrated with violence, cruel, brutal, fero-cious, felonious, rapacious; bold, daring, impetuous, rash; punitive, castigatory; (अस्), m. a robber, free-booter. —साहसिक-ता, f. cruelty, ferocity, impetu-osity, temerity, boldness.
साहसिन्: साहसिन्, ई, इनी, इ, violent, ferocious; foolhardy, bold, daring, impetuous, rash.
साहस्र: साहस्र साहस्र, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सहस्र), relating or belonging to a thousand; consisting of a thousand; bought with a thousand; paid per thou-sand (as interest, duty); a thousandfold, a thousand times better; (अस्), m. an army or detachment con-sisting of a thousand men; (अम्), n. the aggregate of a thousand; an aggregate of many thousands.
साहायक: साहायक साहायक, अम्, n. (fr. सहाय), assistance, fellowship, association; a number of asso-ciates or companions; auxiliary troops.
साहाय्य: साहाय्य, अम्, n. friendship, fellowship, alliance, confederation; help, succour; helping another in danger (regarded as a branch of dramatic action). —साहाय्यार्थ (°य-अर्°), अस्, m. the use or ad-vantage of assistance.
साहिड: साहिड साहिड, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
साहिती: साहिती साहिती, f. (fr. 2. सहित) = साहित्य below.
साहित्य: साहित्य, अम्, n. association, connection, combi-nation, union, society, fellowship; literary compo-sition, rhetorical composition, rhetoric, poetry; (ac-cording to some) a collection of materials or means or rules for the production or performance of any-thing. —साहित्य-दर्पण, अम्, n. ‘mirror of com-position,’ N. of a treatise on rhetorical composition by Viśva-nātha-kavi-rāja (a kind of Ars Poetica, giving rules and canons of literary composition, especially dramatic). —साहित्य-मीमांसा, f., N. of a work on rhetorical composition. —साहित्य-शास्त्र, अम्, n. any rhetorical treatise (i. e. any work explaining and applying the figures of rhetoric, setting forth the various passions and affections, and giving rules for dramatic or poetical composition). —साहित्य-सर्-वस्व, अम्, n., N. of a commentary by Māheśvara on the Kāvyālaṅkāra-vṛtti. —साहित्य-सुधा-स-मुद्र, अस्, m., N. of a work on medicine.
साह्य: साह्य, अम्, n. (fr. 2. सह), conjunction, union, society, association, companionship. —साह्य-कृत्, त्, m. a companion, associate.
साहिदेव: साहिदेव साहिदेव, अस्, m. a proper N.
साहिवीचि: साहिवीचि साहि-वीचि (स-अह्°), इस्, इस्, इ, hav-ing waves of serpents.
साहुडियान: साहुडियान साहुडियान, अस्, m., N. of the author Śūla-pāṇi.
साह्वय: साह्वय साह्वय (स-आह्°), अस्, m. gambling with fighting animals, setting animals to fight for sport, &c. (= सम्-आह्वय).
सि: सि सि, cl. 5. 9. P. A. सिनोति, सिनुते, सि-नाति, सिनीते, सिषाय, सिष्ये, सेष्यति, -ते, असैषीत्, असेष्ट, सेतुम्, to bind, tie, fasten; to ensnare: Caus. साययति, -यितुम्, Aor. असीषयत्: Desid. सिसीषति, -ते: Intens. सेषीयते, सेषयीति, सेषेति; [cf. Zend hi-ta, ‘bound:’ Gr. σει-ρά, ἱ-μά-ς, ἱ-μον-ιά, ἱμάσσ-ω, ἱμάσ-θλη: Old Germ. sei-l, sei-d, ‘a noose;’ sai-to: Goth. in-sailjan: Old Sax. si-mo, ‘a bond:’ Angl. Sax. sal, sœl, sœlan, sieran, syrwan: Slav. si-lo, se-ti, si-tije: Lett. see-t, ‘to bind;’ sai-te, ‘a bond, rope.’]
सित: 1. सित, अस्, आ, अम्, (for 2. see p. 1113, col. 2; for 3. see under rt. 1. सो), bound, tied, fastened; sur-rounded.

सित 2. सित, अस्, आ or ई, अम् (thought by some to be fr. 2. असित, q. v.; apparently connected with शिति, p. 1005, cf. श्वित, श्वेत, p. 1031, and see सिन; for 1. see under rt. सि, for 3. see under rt. 1. सो), white; (अस्), m. the colour white; the light half of the month from new to full moon; the planet Venus or its regent, = शुक्र; (आ), f. candied sugar, sugar; moonlight; a handsome woman; spirituous liquor; white Dūrvā grass; Arabian jas-mine; a sort of Clitoria; a kind of Aparājitā plant (growing on mountains); various other plants or trees, = श्वेत-कण्टकारी; = वाकुची; = विदारी; = कुटुम्बिनी; = पिङ्गा; = त्रायमाणा; = तेजनी; (अम्), n. silver; sandal; a radish (= मूलक)। —सित-कण्टा or सित-कण्टारिका, f. a kind of plant (= श्वेत-कण्टकारी). —सित-कण्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, white-throated, having a white neck; (अस्), m. a gallinule. —सित-कर, अस्, m. ‘white-rayed,’ the moon; camphor. —सित-कर्णी, f. a kind of plant (= वासक). —सित-कर्मन्, आ, आ, अ, pure in deeds or actions. —सित-कुञ्जर, अस्, m. a white elephant; N. of Indra's elephant; ‘having a white elephant,’ epithet of Indra. —सित-गुञ्जा, f. a kind of plant (= श्वेत-गुञ्जा). —सित-चिह्न, अस्, m. ‘white-marked,’ a sort of fish (= बालुका-गड). —सित-च्छत्त्र, अम्, n. a white umbrella (especially as one of the emblems of royalty); (आ or ई), f. a sort of fennel (= शत-पुष्पा). —सित-च्छत्रित, अस्, m. having a white umbrella, possessed of all the insignia of royalty, (according to the Scholiast on Naiṣadha I. 1. = श्वेतातपत्री-कृत, made into a white um-brella.) —सित-च्छद, अस्, m. ‘white-feathered,’ a goose; (आ), f. white Dūrvā grass. —सित-तुरग, अस्, m. ‘white-horsed,’ epithet of Arjuna. —सित-दर्भ, अस्, m. white Kuśa grass. —सित-दीधिति, इस्, m. ‘white-rayed,’ the moon. —सित-दीप्य, अस्, m. white cumin. —सित-दूर्वा, f. white Dūrvā grass. —सित-द्रु, उस्, m. ‘white tree,’ a species of Moraṭa plant. —सित-धातु, उस्, m. a white mineral; chalk. —सित-पक्ष, अस्, m. a white wing; the light half of a lunar month; ‘white-winged,’ a goose; [cf. धवल-पक्ष।] —सित-पर्णी, f. ‘white-leafed,’ a kind of plant (= अर्क-पुष्पिका)। —सित-पाटलिका, f. the white Pāṭalā tree. —सित-पुङ्खा, f. the white Śara-puṅkhā plant. —सित-पुष्प, अस्, m. the Tagara tree; a kind of grass (= काश); a kind of tree, = श्वेत-रोहित; (आ), f. Arabian jasmine; (ई), f. a kind of white Aparājitā plant; (अम्), n. a sort of grass, Cyperus Rotundus. —सित-मणि, इस्, m. a white precious stone, a crystal. —सितमणि-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of crystals or jewels, made of crystal. —सित-मरिच, अम्, n. white pepper. —सित-माष, अस्, m. a sort of bean (= राज-माष). —सित-रक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, white and red. —सित-रञ्जन, अस्, m. ‘white-tinged,’ yellow (the colour). —सित-रश्मि, इस्, m. ‘white-rayed,’ the moon. —सित-वर्षाभू, ऊस्, m. a kind of plant (= पुनर्-णवा). —सित-वाजिन्, ई, m. ‘having white horses,’ epithet of Arjuna. —सित-शर्करा, f. candied sugar. —सित-शायका, f. the white Śara-puṅkhā plant. —सित-शिंशपा, f. the white Śiṃśapā tree. —सित-शिम्बिक, अस्, m. ‘white-awned,’ wheat, (also read शिति-शिम्बिक।) —सित-शिव, अम्, n. rock-salt, (also read शित-शिव, सित-सिव, शीत-शिव, शीत-सिव।) —सित-शूक, अस्, m. ‘white-awned,’ barley; [cf. शित-शूक।] —सित-शू-रण, अस्, m. the plant Vana-śūraṇa. —सित-श्म-श्रु, उस्, उस्, उ, having a white beard, silvery-bearded. —सित-सप्ति, इस्, m. ‘having white horses,’ epithet of Arjuna. —सित-सर्षप, अस्, m. white mustard. —सित-सार or सित-सारक, अस्, m. ‘having white pith,’ the Śāliñca plant. —सित-सिंही, f. the white Kaṇṭakārī plant. —सित-सिन्धु, उस्, f. ‘white river,’ the Ganges. —सित-सिव, see सित-शिव. —सि-तांशु (°त-अं°), उस्, m. ‘white-rayed,’ the moon; camphor. —सितांशुक (°त-अं°), अस्, आ, अम्, dressed in a white mantle or garment. —सितांशु-तैल, अम्, n. camphor oil or ointment. —सिता-खण्ड, अस्, m. a kind of clayed or refined sugar (said to be prepared from honey). —सिताग्र (°त-अग्°), अस्, m. = शिताग्र, a thorn. —सिताङ्क (°त-अङ्°), अस्, m. ‘white-marked,’ the Bālukā-gaḍa fish. —सिताङ्ग (°त-अङ्°), अस्, m. the Śveta-rohita tree. —सिताङ्ग-राग (°त-अङ्°), अस्, m. a white cosmetic or deco-ration for the limbs or body. —सिताजाजी (°त-अज्°), f. white cumin. —सितातप-वारण (°त-आत्°), अम्, n. a white umbrella (especially as a symbol of royalty). —सितादि (°त-आदि?), इस्, m. treacle, mo-lasses (= गुड). —सितानन (°त-आन्°), अस्, ई, अम्, white-faced; (अस्), m. epithet of Garuḍa. —सिता-पाङ्ग (°त-अप्°), अस्, m. ‘having white eye-corners,’ a peacock. —सिताब्ज (°त-अब्°), अम्, n. a white lotus. —सिताभ (°त-आभ्°), अस्, m. ‘white-looking,’ camphor; (आ), f. = तक्राह्वा (according to Śabda-k.). —सिताभ्र (°त-अभ्°), अस्, अम्, m. n. or सिता-भ्रक, अम्, n. (see अभ्र), camphor; (incorrectly written शिताभ्र।) —सिताम्बर (°त-अम्°), अस्, आ, अम्, clothed in white garments; (अस्), m. an ascetic wearing white garments. —सिताम्बुज (°त-अम्°) or सिताम्भोज (°त-अम्°), अम्, n. a white lotus. —सितार्जक (°त-अर्°), अस्, m. white basil. —सिता-लक (°त-अल्°), अस्, m. the white Mandāraka tree. —सिता-लता, f. white Dūrvā grass. —सितालि (°त-आलि), इस्, इस्, इ, having white lines. —सितालि-कटभी, f. the white Kiṇihī tree. —सितालिका (°त-आल्°), f. ‘white-lined,’ a cockle. —सितावर (°त- or °ता-अव्°), अस्, m. a species of culinary plant (commonly called Susunī, = मेधा-कृत्); (ई), f. the plant Vākucī. —सिताश्व (°त-अश्°), अस्, m. ‘having white horses,’ epithet of Arjuna. —सितासित (°त-अस्°), अस्, आ, अम्, white and black; (अस्), m., N. of Bala-rāma; (औ), m. du. Venus and Saturn. —सिताह्वय (°त-आह्°), अस्, m. the white Śigru tree; the Śveta-rohita tree. —सितेक्षु (°त-इक्°), उस्, m. white sugar-cane. —सितेतर (°त-इत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, other than white, black; (अस्), m. a kind of dark-coloured rice; a kind of pulse (= कुलत्थ). —सितेतर-गति, इस्, m. ‘having a black course,’ epithet of fire; [cf. कृष्ण-वर्त्मन्।] —सितोत्पल (°त-उत्°), अम्, n. a white water-lily. —सितोदर (°त-उद्°), अस्, m. ‘white-bellied,’ epithet of the god Kuvera (who is described as deformed and whitened by a leprous taint). —सि-तोद्भव (°त-उद्°), अस्, आ, अम्, produced from sugar; (अम्), n. white sandal. —सितोपल (°त-उप्°), अस्, m. ‘white stone,’ crystal; (आ), f. refined or candied sugar; (अम्), n. chalk (or a similar substance considered as a variety). —सितोष्ण-वारण (°त-उष्°), अम्, n. ‘white heat-repeller,’ a white um-brella.

3. सित, अस्, आ, अम्, (for 1. see under rt. सि; for 2. see p. 1113, col. 2), destroyed, brought to an end, finished, completed, concluded; ascertained, known; (अस्), m. an arrow (probably for शित, cf. सायक, शायक). —सिताग्र (°त-अग्°), अस्, m. = शिताग्र, a thorn.
सिति: 1. सिति, इस्, f. binding, fastening; [cf. 1. प्र-सिति।]

2. सिति, इस्, इस्, इ (connected with शिति, p. 1005; for 1. see p. 1112, col. 3; for 3. see under rt. 1. सो), white; black. —सिति-कण्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, having a white throat; dark-necked; (अस्), m. Śiva; [cf. शिति-कण्ठ।] —सिति-वार, अस्, m. a kind of culinary plant (= सु-निषण्णक). —सिति-वासस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, clad in black; (आस्), m. epithet of Bala-rāma (= नीलाम्बर).
सेतु: सेतु, सेतृ, सेत्र, &c. See under सेतु, p. 1134.

सेतु सेतु, उस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. I. 70. fr. rt. सि, ‘to bind’), a ridge of earth, mound, bank, causeway, dike, dam, any raised piece of ground separating fields (serving as a boundary or as a pas-sage during inundations); a landmark; a bridge; a pass, defile, mountain road or track; a boundary, limit; a barrier or obstruction of any kind; an estab-lished institution, fixed rule or law; epithet of the Praṇava or sacred syllable Om (which is said to be मन्त्राणां सेतुः); the tree Cratæva Roxburghii or Tapia Cratæva (= वरण, वरुण); N. of a king; of a place. —सेतु-खण्ड, N. of a book of the Skanda-Purāṇa. —सेतु-बन्ध, अस्, m. the forming of a causeway or bridge; the ridge of rocks extending from the south extremity of the Coro-mandel coast towards the island of Ceylon (supposed to have been formed by Hanumat as a bridge for the passage of Rāma's forces against Rāvaṇa); any causeway, bridge, dike, &c.; N. of a poem. —सेतु-भेदिन्, ई, इनी, इ, breaking down barriers; removing obstructions; (ई), m. the medicinal plant Dantī, q. v. —सेतु-मङ्गल-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a Tantra work. —सेतु-वृक्ष, अस्, m. the tree Cratæva Rox-burghii.

demonstrated conclusion of an argument, the esta-blished line of reasoning or view of any question, the true logical conclusion (following on the refuta-tion of the पूर्व-पक्ष or first objection), esta-blished truth, proved fact, settled opinion or doc-trine, dogma, axiom, received or admitted truth (regarded as of four kinds, viz. सर्व-तन्त्र-स्°, प्रति-तन्त्र-स्°, अधिकरण-स्°, अभ्युपगम-स्°, q. q. v. v.); any fixed or established text-book resting on conclusive arguments, (often used at the end of comps. to denote certain received treatises by high authorities on astronomy, mathematics, and other sciences; nine astronomical works being espe-cially so designated, viz. the Brahma-s°, Sūrya-s°, Soma-s°, Vṛhaspati-s°, Garaga-s°, Nārada-s°, Parā-śara-s°, Pulastya-s°, Vasiṣṭha-s°; five principal astro-nomical Siddhāntas are enumerated by others, viz. Pauliśa-s°, Romaka-s°, Vāsiṣṭha-s°, Śaura-s°, and Paitāmaha-s°.) —सिद्धान्त-कोटि, इस्, f. the point in an argument which is regarded as a logical conclu-sion. —सिद्धान्त-कौमुदी, f., N. of a celebrated grammar by Bhaṭṭoji-dīkṣita (intended to furnish a practical arrangement of Pāṇini's Sūtras with a commentary). —सिद्धान्त-गर्भ, अस्, m., N. of a work by Madana-pāla. —सिद्धान्त-चन्द्रिका, f. a commentary on the Sarasvatī-sūtra by Rāma-candrāśrama; another on the Śāstra-dīpikā by Rāma-kṛṣṇa-bhaṭṭa; N. of Rāma-saṃyamin's Ve-dānta precepts. —सिद्धान्तचन्द्रिका-टीका, f. a commentary by Gaṅgādhara-yati on Rāma-saṃya-min's work. —सिद्धान्त-चन्द्रोदय (°र-उद्°), अस्, m. a commentary by Kṛṣṇa-dhūrjaṭi-dīkṣita on the Tarka-saṅgraha. —सिद्धान्त-चिन्तामणि, इस्, m., N. of a work on astronomy. —सिद्धान्त-तत्त्व, अम्, n., N. of a work on the principles of the Vaiśeṣika doctrines, (also called Padārtha-viveka.) —सिद्धान्ततत्त्व-बिन्दु, a commentary by Ma-dhu-sūdana-sarasvatī on Śaṅkarācārya's Daśa-ślokī. —सिद्धान्ततत्त्वबिन्दु-सन्दीपन or बिन्दु-सन्दीपन, अम्, n. a commentary by Puruṣottama Sarasvatī on the preceding. —सिद्धान्ततत्त्व-सर्-वस्व, अम्, n. a commentary on the Siddhānta-tattva by Gopīnātha-maunin. —सिद्धान्त-दीपिका, f. a commentary on the Siddhānta-muktāvalī by Nānā-dīkṣita. —सिद्धान्त-पक्ष, अस्, m. the logically correct side of an argument. —सिद्धान्त-बिन्दु = सिद्धान्ततत्त्व-बिन्दु, q. v. —सिद्धान्-तबिन्दु-व्याख्या, f. a commentary by Nārāyaṇa-yati on the preceding. —सिद्धान्त-मुक्तावली, f. ‘string of pearls of dogmatic precepts,’ N. of a com-mentary by Viśva-nātha Pañcānana Bhaṭṭācārya Tarkālaṅkāra on the Bhāṣā-pariccheda (a text-book of the Nyāya, also called मुक्तावली); of a metrical Vedānta treatise with a prose interpretation by Prakāśānanda; of a metrical exposition of the theory of Vallabhācārya. —सिद्धान्तमुक्तावली-प्रकाश, अस्, m., N. of a commentary on the Sid-dhānta-muktāvalī. —सिद्धान्त-रत्न, N. of a summary of the Vedānta system by Nimbārka (= दश-श्लोकी). —सिद्धान्त-रहस्य, अम्, n., N. of a work on astronomy. —सिद्धान्त-लेश, अस्, m., N. of a metrical work by Apya-dīkṣita on the Vedānta and other systems of philosophy. —सिद्-धान्त-वागीश, अस्, m., N. of the preceptor of Rāghavendra. —सिद्धान्त-शिरोमणि, N. of an astronomical work by Bhāskara. —सिद्धान्त-सङ्-ग्रह, अस्, m., N. of an epitome of Vijñāneśvara's Mitākṣarā. —सिद्धान्त-सन्दर्भ, अस्, m., N. of an astronomical work. —सिद्धान्त-सुन्दर, N. of a work on astronomy by Jñāna-rāja. —सिद्-धान्त-सूक्ति-मञ्जरी, f., N. of a metrical abridg-ment of the Siddhānta-leśa by Gaṅgā-dhara-sarasvatī. —सिद्धान्ताचार (°त-आच्°), अस्, m. a perfect rule of action (with the Tāntrikas); one who practises this rule (said to consist in purity, quietism, and complete mental absorption in Durgā). —सिद्धान्-तित, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. सिद्धान्त), logically demon-strated or proved, established as true. —सिद्धान्तिन्, ई, m. one who establishes or proves his conclusions; one learned in scientific text-books; a follower of the Mīmāṃsā philosophy. —सिद्धान्न (°ध-अन्°), अम्, n. dressed food, cooked victuals. —सिद्धापगा (°ध-अप्°), f. ‘divine river,’ epithet of the Ganges. —सिद्धारि (°ध-अरि), इस्, m. a particular Mantra. —सिद्धार्थ (°ध-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, one who has accomplished an aim or object, successful, prosperous; (अस्), m. epithet of the great Buddha (or Śākya-muni, founder of the Buddhist religion); N. of the father of the last and most celebrated Arhat of the present Ava-sarpiṇī; epithet of Śiva; white mustard; (आ), f., N. of the mother of the fourth of the twenty-four Arhats. —सिद्धार्थक, अम्, n. white mustard. —सिद्धार्थ-कारिन्, ई, m. epithet of Śiva. —सिद्धार्थिन् (°ध-अर्°), ई, m., N. of the fifty-third (or twenty-seventh) year of Jupiter's cycle of sixty years. —सिद्धाश्रम (°ध-आश्°), N. of a hermitage in the Himālaya (where Viṣṇu performed penance before his dwarf incarnation). —सिद्धा-श्रम-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —सिद्धा-सन (°ध-आस्°), अम्, n. a particular posture in religious meditation (described as placing the left heel under the body and the right heel in front of it, fixing the sight between the eyebrows, and medi-tating upon the syllable ॐ). —सिद्धेश्वर-तन्त्र (°ध-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a Tantra work. —सिद्-धेश्वर-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —सिद्-धेश्वरी (°ध-ईश्°), f., N. of a particular goddess. —सिद्धौघ (°ध-ओघ), अस्, m., N. of a par-ticular class of Gurus worshipped or revered by the Tāntrikas, (their names are said to be Nārada, Kāśyapa, Śambhu, Bhārgava, Kula-kauśika.)
सिद्धिली: सिद्धिली सिद्धिली, f. (according to some) a small ant.
सिध्: सिध् 1. सिध् (according to Vopa-deva VIII. 41. the स् of this rt. is not changed to ष् after prepositions; cf. परि-सिध्), cl. 1. P. सेधति, सिषेध, सेधिष्यति, असेधीत्, सेधि-तुम्, to go, (in Naigh. II. 14. सेधति is enume-rated among the गति-कर्माणः); to go towards, reach, strike, hit (Ved.).

सिध् 2. सिध् (this rt. allows the change of स् to ष् after prepositions, cf. प्रति-षिध्), cl. 1. P. (ep. also A.) सेधति (-ते), सि-षेध, सेत्स्यति or सेधिष्यति, असैत्सीत् or असे-धीत्, सेद्धुम् or सेधितुम्, to drive off, ward off, keep off, restrain, hinder; to interdict; to ordain, instruct; to turn out well or auspiciously: Caus. सेधयति, -यितुम्: Desid. of Caus. सिषेधयि-षति: Desid. सिसेधिषति, सिसिधिषति, सिषित्-सति: Intens. सेषिध्यते, सेषेद्धि।

सिध् 3. सिध् (connected with rt. साध्), cl. 4. P. सिध्यति (ep. also A. -ते), सि-षेध, सेत्स्यति, असिधत्, सेद्धुम्, to be accom-plished, be fulfilled, be effected; to be successful, succeed; to be settled or established; to be valid; to be proved or demonstrated; to be thoroughly prepared or cooked; to attain an object, hit an aim, fall true (with loc., e. g. इषुः सिध्यति लक्ष्ये, the arrow falls true on the mark): Pass. सिध्यते, Aor. असेधि, to be completed or concluded, &c.: Caus. सेधयति, with reference to sacred things; साधयति, -यितुम्, with reference to secular things, (Pāṇ. VI. 1, 49; see rt. साध्); to accomplish, complete, effect, settle, perform: Desid. सिषित्सति: Intens. सेषिध्यते, सेषेद्धि।
सेध: 1. सेध, अस्, m. going, reaching [cf. उत्-स्°]; a tail (according to some; cf. गो-ष्°); (आ), f. a porcupine.
2. सेध, अस्, m. restraint, restraining, hindering; [cf. नि-षेध under नि-षिध्।]
सेधन: 1. सेधन, अम्, n. the act of going.
2. सेधन, अम्, n. the act of restraining or keep-ing off.
सेधित्वा: 2. सेधित्वा, ind. (according to some) = सिद्ध्वा, col. 2; [cf. 1. सेधित्वा under rt. 1. सिध्। ]
सेद्धव्य: सेद्धव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be kept off, to be pre-vented, &c.
सेधक: सेधक, अस्, आ, अम्, driving off, preventing.
सेधनीय: सेधनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, = सेद्धव्य, col. 1.
सिद्धक: सिद्धक, अस्, m. a kind of tree (= सिन्धु-वार); the Śāl tree; a species of metre.
सिद्धा: सिद्धा। See under सिद्ध, p. 1114, col. 2.
सिद्धायिका: सिद्धायिका, f., N. of one of the twenty-four goddesses, called Śāsana-devatās, who execute the commands of the twenty-four Arhats.
सिद्धि: सिद्धि, इस्, f. accomplishment, fulfilment, com-pletion, perfection, complete attainment (of any object), performance; success, prosperity, well-being; settlement, establishment, substantiation, demonstra-tion, proof, indisputable conclusion; validity (of a rule or law); certainty, truth, accuracy, correctness; decision, adjudication, determination (of a lawsuit); payment, liquidation (of a debt), acquittance; the solution of a problem; preparation, cooking, matur-ing, maturity; readiness; complete knowledge; complete perfection or sanctification (by penance &c.); final emancipation, supreme felicity, beati-tude; the acquisition of supernatural powers by magical means or the supernatural faculty so ac-quired, (eight are usually enumerated, e. g. अणिमन्, महिमन्, लघिमन्, गरिमन्, प्राप्ति, प्रा-काम्य, ईशि-त्व, वशि-त्व, q. q. v. v., to which is sometimes added कामावसायि-त्व and many others, e. g. सिद्धिः खेचरी, the magical power of flying through the air; रसोल्लास, q. v., वि-शोका, q. v., see also under सिद्ध, p. 1114); any marvellous skill or capability; a magical shoe or slipper (supposed to have the power of conveying the wearer wherever he likes); good effect or result, use, advantage; un-derstanding, intellect; concealment, vanishing, mak-ing one's self invisible; a particular Yoga (either the sixteenth of the astronomical periods or the nine-teenth of the twenty-eight astrological Yogas); a kind of medicinal root (= ऋद्धि); Perfection (per-sonified as a daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Dharma); N. of a Yoginī; of Durgā; of Śiva, (in this sense masc.) —सिद्धि-कारण, अम्, n. a cause of beatitude, means of obtaining felicity. —सिद्धि-चामुण्डा-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —सिद्धि-द, अस्, आ, अम्, conferring felicity or beatitude; (अस्), m. epithet of a form of Bhairava or Śiva (= वटुक-भैरव). —सिद्धि-दात्री, f. ‘giver of perfection,’ epithet of Durgā. —सिद्धि-भैरव, अम्, n., N. of a Tantra work. —सिद्धि-योग, अस्, m. a parti-cular auspicious conjunction of the planets. —सिद्-धि-योगिनी, f. a kind of Yoginī. —सिद्धि-लाभ, अस्, m. acquirement of success or perfection. —सिद्-धि-सोपान, ‘ladder of success,’ N. of a work. —सिद्धि-स्थान, अम्, n. ‘place of felicity,’ N. of any sacred spot where final beatitude is obtained by religious worship (such as particular places on the Ganges or Sarasvatī). —सिद्ध्य्-अर्थम्, ind. for the sake of accomplishing or obtaining.
सिद्ध्वा: सिद्ध्वा, ind. having accomplished or effected, having completed.
सिधित्वा: सिधित्वा, ind. (according to some) = सिद्ध्वा above.
सिध्म: सिध्म, अम्, or सिध्मन्, अ, n. a blotch, pustule, scab; pock-mark, leprous spot; leprosy or a kind of leprosy (one of the seven kinds). —सिध्म-पुष्-पिका, f. a particular kind of cutaneous disease or leprosy. —सिध्म-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, scabby, pock-marked, covered with pustules or blotches; leprous, tainted with leprosy.
सिध्मल: सिध्मल, अस्, आ, अम्, = सिध्म-वत्; (आ), f. a scab, blotch, leprous spot; a sort of leprosy; dried fish, salt fish (= मत्स्य-विकृति).
सिध्मा: सिध्मा, f. a blotch, scab, leprous spot; leprosy.
सिध्य: सिध्य, अस्, m. ‘auspicious,’ N. of the asterism Puṣya.
सिध्र: सिध्र, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. obtaining, effecting, (Sāy. = साधक); perfect, good; protecting; (अस्), m. a pious or virtuous man; a tree.
सिध्रका: सिध्रका, f. a kind of plant or tree. —सिध्रका-वण, अम्, n. ‘Sidhrakā-grove,’ N. of one of the celestial gardens.
सिन: सिन सिन, अस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. III. 2. fr. rt. सि, ‘to bind;’ see also Nirukta V. 5), ‘a quantity of anything bound or collected together,’ a lump of food, &c., mouthful; (अम्), n. the body; food (Ved.; Sāy. = अन्न); (अस्, ई, अम्), white, white-coloured (according to Śabda-k.); blind with one eye, one-eyed, = काण; (ई), f. white, (perhaps an old fem. of 2. सित; cf. श्येनी under श्येन।) —सिन-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. having food.
सिनीवाली: सिनीवाली, f. (said to be connected with सिनी, ‘white;’ but in Nirukta XI. 31. सिनी is connected with rt. सि and वाली with rt. वल्, ‘to surround,’ or with बाल, ‘young;’ the real meaning may be ‘a white ring’), the day preceding that of new moon or the day on which the moon rises with a thin crescent of light scarcely visible; N. of a Vedic god-dess; of the goddess Durgā.
सिन्दुक: सिन्दुक सिन्दुक, अस्, m. (probably fr. rt. स्यन्द्, see below), the small tree or shrub Vitex Negundo.
सिन्दुवार: सिन्दु-वार, अस्, m. (probably for स्यन्द-वार, the plant being used medicinally to prevent flow of the humors and laxity), = सिन्दुक above; [cf. सिन्धु-वार।]
सिन्दूर: सिन्दूर सिन्दूर, अस्, m. (in Uṇādi-s. I. 69. said to be fr. rt. स्यन्द्), a sort of tree; (ई), f., N. of a plant (= रोचनी); the plant Grislea Tomentosa (= धातकी); the plant Lythrum Fruticosum; red cloth or clothes; (अम्), n. red lead, minium, ver-milion; = राज-लेख (according to some). —सिन्-दूर-कारण, अम्, n. ‘origin of minium,’ lead. —सिन्दूर-तिलक, अस्, m. ‘marked with red lead,’ an elephant; (आ), f. a woman whose forehead is marked with red lead (and therefore whose husband is living). —सिन्दूर-निर्गम, अस्, m., N. of the 137th chapter of the Krīḍā-khaṇḍa or second part of the Gaṇeśa-Purāṇa. —सिन्दूर-पुष्पी, f. a kind of plant (= वीर-पुष्पी).
सिन्दूरित: सिन्दूरित, अस्, आ, अम्, reddened, made red.
सिन्धु: सिन्धु सिन्धु, उस्, m. (probably connected with rt. स्यन्द्, ‘to flow’), the ocean, sea, (कृपा-सिन्धु, ‘ocean of mercy,’ a term for an exceedingly merciful person); N. of Varuṇa (as god of the ocean); the river Indus; the Indus personified (as one of the male rivers, cf. नद); the country around the Indus (commonly called Sindh); the water into which the Soma drops; water ejected from the mouth or from an elephant's trunk (= वमथु); the juice that exudes from an elephant's temples; an elephant; a particular Rāga or musical mode (re-garded as son of the Rāga Mālakauśa); the tree Vitex Negundo [cf. सिन्दुक]; white or refined borax, = श्वेत-टङ्कण; (अवस्), m. pl. the in-habitants of Sindh; (उस्), f. the river Sindhu, (Ni-rukta IX. 26); a river or stream of water in general. —सिन्धु-कफ, अस्, m. ‘sea-foam,’ cuttle-fish bone. —सिन्धु-कर, अम्, n. a kind of white borax (= श्वेत-टङ्कण). —सिन्धु-क्षित्, त्, m., N. of the author of the hymn Ṛg-veda X. 75 (having the patronymic Praiyamedha). —सिन्धु-खेल, अस्, m. ‘sported or flowed over by the Indus,’ the country Sindh. —सिन्धु-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, ocean-born, sea-born, marine; river-born, aquatic; born or produced in the country Sindh; (आ), f. epithet of the goddess Lakṣmī (as produced at the churning of the ocean); (अम्), n. rock-salt. —सिन्धु-जन्मन्, आ, आ, अ, ocean-born, sea-born; produced in Sindh; (आ), m. the moon; (अ), n. rock-salt. —सिन्धु-डा, f., N. of the wife of the Rāga Mālava. —सिन्धु-देश, अस्, m. the country of Sindh. —सिन्धु-द्वीप, अस्, m., N. of a king; of the author of the hymn Ṛg-veda X. 9 (having the patronymic Āmbarīṣa). —सिन्धु-नद, N. of a river. —सिन्धु-नन्दन, अस्, m. ‘son of the ocean,’ the moon (fabled to have been one of the fourteen precious things recovered at the churn-ing of the ocean, see मन्दर, p. 746). —सिन्धु-नाथ, अस्, m. ‘lord of rivers,’ the ocean. —सिन्धु-पति, इस्, m. ‘lord of Sindh,’ epithet of Jayad-ratha. —सिन्धु-पार-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, born or produced on the further bank of the Indus. —सिन्धु-पुत्र, अस्, m. ‘son of the ocean,’ the moon; a sort of ebony. —सिन्धु-पुलिन्द, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people. —सिन्धु-पुष्प, अस्, m. ‘sea-flower,’ a conch-shell. —सिन्धु-मध्य, N. of a district. —सिन्धु-मन्थ, अस्, m. the churning of the ocean, (see मन्दर, p. 746); ‘ocean churning-stick,’ a mountain (according to some). —सिन्धु-मन्थ-ज, अम्, n. rock-salt. —सिन्धु-मातृ, ता, त्री, तृ, Ved. having the sea as mother (said of the Soma, also of the Maruts and of the Aśvins); (ता), f. ‘mother of streams,’ epithet of the river Sarasvatī (Ved.). —सिन्धु-मुख, अम्, n. the mouth of a river. —सिन्धु-मुखागत (°ख-आग्°), अस्, आ, अम्, arrived at the mouth of a river. —सिन्धु-राज, अस्, m. ‘king of Sindh,’ epithet of Jayad-ratha. —सिन्धु-लवण, अम्, n. ‘Sindh-salt,’ rock-salt. —सिन्धु-वार, अस्, m. a good horse or one of a particularly good breed (brought probably from Sindh or the borders of Persia); the small tree Vitex Negundo (= सिन्दु-वार). —सिन्धु-वारक, अस्, m.
