स्थावर: स्थावर, अस्, आ, अम्, standing still, not moving, not having the power of motion, not locomotive, fixed to one spot, fixed, stationary, firm, stable, immov-able, (opposed to जङ्गम, q. v.); inert, inactive, slow (said of poison); regular, established; (अस्), m. a mountain; (अम्), n. any stationary or inanimate object (as a plant, mineral, &c.; these stationary objects constituted the seventh creation of Brahmā or तस्थुषां सर्ग, see under सर्ग; cf. Manu I. 41); a bow-string; immovable property, real estate (such as land or houses); a heir-loom, family possession (such as jewels &c. which have been long preserved in a family and ought not to be sold). —स्थावर-ता, f. fixedness, stability, the quality of being stationary, immobility; the state of a vegetable or mineral, (Manu XII. 9.) —स्थावर-जङ्गम, अम्, n. or आनि, n. pl. things stationary and movable or inanimate and animate, (Manu I. 41.) —स्थाव-रादि (°र-आदि), n. the poison called Vatsa-nābha, q. v. —स्थावरास्थावर (°र-अस्°), अम्, n. things stationary and movable, immovable and movable property.
स्थाविर: स्थाविर, अस्, आ or ई, अम् (fr. स्थविर), thick, firm (Ved.); (अम्), n. old age (described as commencing after seventy in men and after fifty in women, and ending at ninety, after which period a man is called वर्षीयस्).
स्थासक: स्थासक, अस्, m. perfuming or smearing the body with fragrant unguents (of sandal &c.); a bubble of water or any fluid.
स्थासु: स्थासु, उ, n. bodily strength or stamina.
स्थास्नु: स्थास्नु, उस्, उस्, उ, disposed to stand, firm, stationary, immovable, fixed, stable; durable, per-manent, eternal; a tree or plant (= वृक्ष; cf. स्थावर). —स्थास्नु-ता, f. firmness, stability, dura-bility.
स्थित: स्थित, अस्, आ, अम्, stood, stayed, remained, stopped; standing; standing up, risen; staying, resting, abiding, (उच्चावचेषु स्थित, abiding in all things high and low); being, situated, existing, living; stood still, standing still, desisted, stopped; fixed, permanent, settled, steady, firm, immovable; steadfast, determined, resolved, decreed, established; steady or steadfast in conduct; faithful to a promise or agreement; upright, virtuous; agreed, engaged, contracted, promised; being close at hand, ready; (अम्), n. (in Vedic grammar), scil. पद, a word standing by itself (i. e. without the particle इति in the Pada text; opposed to उप-स्थित). —स्थित-धी, ईस्, ईस्, इ, steady-minded, firm-minded, firm, unmoved, calm. —स्थित-पाठ्य, (in the drama) recitation in Prākṛt by a woman standing. —स्थित-प्रज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, firm in judgment or wisdom, free from fancies or hallucinations, calm, contented. —स्थित-प्रेमन्, आ, m. ‘firm in affection,’ a firm or faithful friend. —स्थितोपस्थित (°त-उप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, (a word) with and without the particle इति (in the Pada text; see स्थित above).
स्थित स्थित, स्थिति, &c. See p. 1147, col. 1.
स्थितवत्: स्थितवत्, आन्, अती, अत्, one who has stood or stayed or abided.
स्थिति: स्थिति, इस्, f. standing, staying, remaining, con-tinuing, living, residing, abiding; stay, residence; standing still, stopping, continuance in one state; remaining stationary, stability, duration, fixedness, fixity, a firm position; stop, cessation; pause; any situation, state, position; posture, condition, natural state, state of a case; good condition, well-doing, welfare; station, high station, rank, dignity; per-manence; continuance or steadfastness in the path of duty, steadiness, correctness of conduct, propriety, good manners; consistency; establishment of good order (in a government); settled rule, sure or fixed decision, ordinance, decree, axiom, maxim; settled determination; term, limit, boundary; (in philo-sophy) inertia, resistance to motion; one of the three states through which the system of created things and every individual being passes, (these three states are, 1. उत्पत्ति, arising into being; 2. स्थिति, continuance in life; 3. लय, dissolution); (in astronomy) duration of an eclipse; (in Vedic grammar) the standing of a word by itself (i. e. without the particle इति, see स्थित). —स्थिति-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing firmness or stability, firm, stable; steady (in purpose or conduct), upright, firm, virtuous. —स्थिति-स्थापक, अस्, आ, अम्, fixing in a (former or original) state or condition, capable of placing in or restoring to a (previous) form or position, having elastic properties; (अस्), m. (ac-cording to some also अम्, n.), the capability of placing in or recovering a (previous) position or condition, elasticity.
स्थित्वा: स्थित्वा, ind. having stood or stayed or stopped, &c.
स्थिर: स्थिर, अस्, आ, अम्, firm, fixed, steady, steadfast; unfluctuating, permanent, enduring, durable, settled, lasting; not moving, immovable, still, placid, calm, quiescent, cool, composed, collected, free from pas-sion; steadfast or steady in conduct; constant, faithful, determined; certain, sure, convinced; firm, hard, solid, strong; (अस्), m. a deity, immortal; epithet of Śiva; of Kārttikeya; a mountain; a tree; a bull; final emancipation from existence; the planet Saturn; a particular plant (= 1. धव); N. of a particular astronomical Yoga; of certain zodiacal signs (viz. Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius; so called because any work done under these signs is supposed to be lasting); (आ), f. a strong-minded woman; the earth; the shrub Śāla-parṇī; a medi-cinal root (= काकोली); the silk-cotton tree; [cf. Gr. στερεό-ς, στεῤῤό-ς, στέρι-φο-ς, στερίφη, στεῖρα, στήρ-ιγξ, στηρίζ-ω, στελεόν: Lat. steri-li-s, stīr-ia, stilla, stolidus, stultus: Goth. stairo: Old Germ. staren, storren, stornen, ga-starken, starh-jan, &c.: Angl. Sax. starian, starc: Lith. styr-u, ‘to be stiff or benumbed;’ ster-va, ‘a carcass.’] —स्थिर-कुट्टक, अस्, m. (in algebra) a steady pulverizer, constant multiplier, common divisor (ap-plied to a particular kind of common divisor). —स्थिर-गन्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, having durable per-fume, strong-scented; (अस्), m. the Campaka tree, Michelia Champaca; (आ), f. Pandanus Odoratissimus (= केतकी); the trumpet-flower (= पाटला). —स्थि-र-चक्र, अस्, m. a particular Jina or Bodhi-sattva (= मञ्जु-श्री). —स्थिर-चित्त, अस्, आ, अम्, or स्थिर-चेतस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, firm-minded, firm, resolute, constant, steady. —स्थिर-च्छद, अस्, m. ‘firm-leafed,’ the birch tree (= भूर्ज-पत्त्र). —स्थिर-च्छाय, अस्, m. ‘having deep shade,’ a tree which gives shelter to travellers; any tree. —स्थिर-जिह्व, अस्, m. ‘firm-tongued,’ a fish. —स्थिर-जीविता, f. ‘firm-lived,’ the silk-cotton tree. —स्थिर-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, more firm, fixed, stationary; very firm or permanent, durable, eternal. —स्थिर-ता, f. or स्थिर-त्व, अम्, n. firmness, stability, steadiness, steadfastness; moral firmness, fortitude; fearlessness. —स्थिर-दंष्ट्र, अस्, m. ‘strong-toothed,’ a snake; N. of Viṣṇu in the boar-Avatāra; = ध्वनि (according to Śabda-k.). —स्थिर-धन्वन्, आ, आ, अ, having or armed with a strong bow (said of Rudra, Ṛg-veda VII. 46, 1). —स्थिर-धी, ईस्, ईस्, इ, firm-minded, resolute, per-severing. —स्थिर-पत्त्र, अस्, m. ‘firm-leafed,’ the marshy date tree. —स्थिर-पुष्प, अस्, m. ‘firm-flowered,’ the Campaka tree; the Vakula tree. —स्थिर-पुष्पिन्, ई, m. ‘strong-flowered,’ the Tilaka tree. —स्थिर-प्रतिज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, persist-ing in an assertion, pertinacious; faithful to a promise. —स्थिर-प्रतिबन्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, firm in resist-ance, pertinacious, obstinate. —स्थिर-प्रतिष्ठा, f. a firm resting-place, fixed residence. —स्थिर-प्रेमन्, आ, आ, अ, firm or steady in affection, a firm friend. —स्थिर-प्स्नु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. having con-stant food; [cf. विश्व-प्स्न्य।] —स्थिर-फला, f. ‘having firm fruit,’ a kind of gourd (= कुष्-माण्डी). —स्थिर-बुद्धि, इस्, इस्, इ, steady-minded, resolute, calm, dispassionate. —स्थिर-मति, इस्, f. a firm mind, fixed resolution; (इस्, इस्, इ), firm-minded, firm, steady, resolute. —स्थिर-मनस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, firm-minded, resolute, determined, faithful. —स्थिर-योनि, इस्, m. ‘having a firm receptacle,’ a large tree which gives shade and shelter. —स्थिर-यौवन, अस्, आ, अम्, possessing constant youth, ever youthful; (अस्), m. a kind of good or evil genius, a fairy (= विद्या-धर). —स्थिर-रङ्गा, f. ‘having a durable colour,’ indigo; a sort of Curcuma. —स्थिर-रागा, f. a kind of Curcuma (= दारु-हरिद्रा). —स्थिर-लोचन, अस्, आ, अम्, steady-eyed; (one) whose gaze is fixed. —स्थिर-श्री, ईस्, ईस्, इ, having fixed or en-during prosperity. —स्थिर-सङ्गर, अस्, आ, अम्, faithful to an agreement or promise, true, veracious. —स्थिर-साधनक, अस्, m. the Sindu-vāra tree. —स्थिर-सार, अस्, m. ‘having firm sap,’ a kind of tree (= शाक). —स्थिर-सौहृद, अस्, आ, अम्, firm in friendship; (अम्), n. firmness in friendship. —स्थिर-स्थायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, remaining firm or steady, keeping perfectly still (as in meditation). —स्थिरांह्रिप (°र-अं°), अस्, m. ‘durable tree,’ the marshy date tree. —स्थिरात्मन् (°र-आत्°), आ, आ, अ, firm-minded, resolute, unmoved, stable, steady. —स्थिरानुराग (°र-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, constant in affection or love. —स्थिरायुस् (°र-आय्°), उस्, उस्, उस्, long-lived, long-lasting; (उस्), m. the silk-cotton tree, (also स्थिरायु according to some.) —स्थिरा-रम्भ (°र-आर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, firm in undertakings, persevering. —स्थिरी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to make firm, confirm, strengthen, corroborate; to bring to a standstill, stop, make fast. —स्थिरी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, &c., to become firm or steady; to become calm.
स्थिरक: स्थिरक, अस्, m., N. of a preceptor.
स्थिराय: स्थिराय, Nom. P. स्थिरायति, &c., to remain firm or constant.
स्थुल: 1. स्थुल in अप-ष्ठ्°, वि-संष्ठ्°, q. q. v. v.
स्थुल 2. स्थुल, अम्, n. (perhaps for स्थुड, fr. rt. स्थुड्, but cf. 1. स्थुल at p. 1147, col. 3), a sort of long tent.
स्थूर: स्थूर, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. = स्थूल, स्थविर, strong, firm; wide, extended, (Sāy. = विस्तृत, Ṛg-veda VI. 29, 2); (अस्), m. a bull (Ved.); a man.
स्थूरिका: स्थूरिका, f. (probably) a barren cow, (according to some this is the more correct reading for छूरिका in Manu VIII. 325.)
स्थूरिन्: स्थूरिन्, ई, m. (also written स्थुरिन्, cf. स्थौ-रिन्), a pack-horse, one carrying loads on his back; a pack-bullock; (इ), n., Ved. a cart drawn by one bull or draught animal, (Sāy. = एकेन धुर्येण युक्तम् अनः, Ṛg-veda X. 131, 3); [cf. Zend staora, ‘a beast of burden:’ Gr. ταῦρο-ς: Lat. tauru-s: Umbr. turu: Old Germ. stiuri, ‘strong;’ stur, ‘large:’ Goth. stiur: Angl. Sax. steor, stor: Engl. steer: Slav. turu, ‘a bull:’ Lith. taura-s, ‘a wild ox.’]
स्थेमन्: स्थेमन्, आ, m. (according to some), firmness, stability, fixedness.
स्थेय: स्थेय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be placed or fixed, to be settled or determined; (अस्), m. a person chosen to settle a dispute between two parties, an arbitrator, umpire, judge; a domestic priest; (आस्), f. pl., scil. आपः, standing water (i. e. water standing in a pot used in certain nuptial ceremonies).
स्थेय स्थेय, स्थेयस्, स्थेष्ठ। See p. 1147.
स्थेयस्: स्थेयस्, आन्, असी, अस् (compar. of स्थिर), more fixed or firm, firmer; very firm or stable; eternal, permanent; very resolute.
स्थेष्ठ: स्थेष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, (superl. of स्थिर), most fixed, very firm or stable, durable.
स्थैर्य: स्थैर्य, अम्, n. (fr. स्थिर), firmness, stability, fixedness, steadiness; continuance; firmness of mind, resolution, constancy, calmness; patience; hardness, solidity.
स्थोरिन्: स्थोरिन्, ई, m. a pack-horse or animal carrying burdens, (see स्थौरिन्।)
स्थौर: स्थौर, अम्, n. (fr. स्थूर = स्थूल), firmness, strength, power; a sufficient load for a horse or ass; (अस्), m. a patronymic of the Vedic Ṛṣi Agni-yuta or Agni-yūpa (author of the hymn Ṛg-veda X. 116).
स्थौरिन्: स्थौरिन्, ई, m. (see स्थूरिन्, स्थोरिन्, स्थुरिन्), a horse carrying burdens on his back, a pack-horse; a strong horse.
स्थागर: स्थागर स्थागर, Ved. probably connected with स्थगर, q. v.
स्थाण्डिल: स्थाण्डिल स्थाण्डिल, अस्, m. (fr. स्थण्डिल), a devotee who sleeps on the bare ground or on ground prepared for a sacrifice (= स्थण्डिल-शायिन्); a mendicant, religious beggar.
स्थिक: स्थिक स्थिक, अस्, m. (according to some fr. rt. 1. स्था), the buttocks (= कटि-प्रोथ).
स्थिर्: स्थिर् स्थिर्, cl. 1. P. स्थिरति, &c., (see Nirukta IX. 11.)
स्थिवि: स्थिवि स्थिवि, see Ṛg-veda X. 68, 3, (ac-cording to Sāy. स्थिविभ्यः apparently = कुसीदे-भ्यः, but the MS. is doubtful.)
स्थुड्: स्थुड् स्थुड् = rt. थुड्, cl. 6. P. स्थुडति, &c., to cover.
स्थूणा: स्थूणा स्थूणा, f. (according to Uṇādi-s. III. 15. fr. rt. 1. स्था), the post or pillar of a house; any post or pillar; an iron image, statue; an anvil; a disease (according to some).
स्थूम: स्थूम स्थूम, अस्, m. (according to Śabda-k.) light; the moon; [cf. स्यूम।]
स्थूल्: स्थूल् स्थूल् (rather a Nom. derived fr. स्थूल below), cl. 10. A. स्थूलयते (also P. स्थूलयति according to some), अतुस्थूलत्, त, to become big or stout, to become bulky, in-crease, grow fat.
स्थूल: स्थूल, अस्, आ, अम्, (probably a later form of स्थूर for स्थावर, see p. 1147, col. 3), strong, powerful; stout, bulky, big, huge; fat, corpulent; great, large, thick; clumsy, coarse, gross, rough, (opposed to सूक्ष्म); not exact; doltish, stolid, thick-headed; stupid, dull, ignorant; (अस्), m. the jack tree; (आ), f. a sort of pepper (= गज-पिप्पली); a kind of gourd or cucumber (= एर्वारु); large cardamoms; (अम्), n. a heap, quantity; = कूट (according to Śabda-k.); a tent, (probably for 2. स्थुल।) —स्थूल-कङ्गु, उस्, m. a sort of wild and coarse kidney-bean (= वरक). —स्थूल-कणा, f. the plant Nigella Indica. —स्थूल-कण्टक, अस्, m. ‘large-thorned,’ a kind of plant, = जाल-वर्वूरक; (इका), f. the silk-cotton tree. —स्थूल-कण्टा, f. a kind of plant (= बृहती). —स्थूल-कन्द, अस्, m. ‘having a large bulb,’ a kind of esculent root or plant with such a root (= सूरण; = माणक; = हस्ति-कन्द); a kind of garlic (= रक्त-लशुन)। —स्थूल-काय, अस्, आ, अम्, large-bodied, corpulent. —स्थूल-काष्ठ-दह्, -धक्, or स्थूल-काष्-ठाग्नि (°ठ-अग्°), इस्, m. the trunk of a tree or any thick piece of timber on fire. —स्थूल-क्षेड or स्थूल-क्ष्वेड, अस्, m. (see क्ष्वेड), an arrow. —स्थूल-ग्रीव, अस्, आ, अम्, thick-necked. —स्थू-लङ्-करण, अस्, ई, अम्, making big or large. —स्थूल-चञ्चु, उस्, m. a kind of culinary plant (= महा-चञ्चु). —स्थूल-चाप, अस्, m. (for तूल-चाप), a large bow-like instrument used in cleaning cotton. —स्थूल-जीरक, अस्, m. the plant Nigella Indica (called Kaloñjī in Hindī). —स्थूल-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, more bulky, bigger, stouter, very large, larger. —स्थूल-ता, f. or स्थूल-त्व, अम्, n. big-ness, stoutness, bulkiness, coarseness; dulness, stu-pidity. —स्थूल-ताल, अस्, m. the marshy date tree (= हिन्ताल). —स्थूल-त्वचा, f. ‘thick-barked,’ a kind of plant (= काश्मरी). —स्थूल-दण्ड, अस्, m. a sort of large reed (= देव-नल). —स्थूल-दर्भ, अस्, m. a kind of grass, Saccharum Munja. —स्थूल-दला, f. the plant Aloe Perfoliata. —स्थू-ल-देह, अस्, अम्, m. n. = स्थूल-शरीर below. —स्थूल-धी, ईस्, ईस्, इ, dull-witted, stupid, ignorant. —स्थूल-नाल, अस्, m. a kind of large reed (= देव-नल). —स्थूल-नास or स्थूल-नासिक, अस्, आ, अम्, large-nosed, thick-nosed; (अस्), m. a hog, boar. —स्थूल-पट, अस्, अम्, m. n. coarse cloth; (अस्, आ, अम्), having coarse cloth or clothes. —स्थूल-पट्ट, अस्, m. cotton; (अम्), n. coarse cloth (accord-ing to some). —स्थूल-पट्टाक, अस्, m. coarse cloth. —स्थूल-पाद, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, large-footed, club-footed, having swelled legs; (अस्), m. an elephant; a man with elephantiasis. —स्थूल-पुष्प, अस्, m. ‘large-flowered,’ the tree Æschynomene Grandiflora; (आ), f. a sort of mountain Clitorea; (ई), f. a kind of plant (= यव-तिक्ता). —स्थूल-फल, अम्, n. the gross result of a calculation or measurement; (अस्), m. ‘having large fruit,’ the silk-cotton tree; (आ), f. the Crotolaria (= शण-पुष्पी). —स्थूल-बाहू, ऊस्, f., N. of a woman. —स्थूल-बुद्धि, इस्, इस्, इ, dull-witted, dull, stupid. —स्थूल-भद्र, अस्, m., N. of one of the six Jaina Śruta-kevalins. —स्थूल-भूत, आनि, n. pl. the five grosser ele-ments (according to the Sāṅkhya phil., see साङ्ख्य). —स्थूल-मरिच, अम्, n. a particular fragrant berry (= कक्कोल). —स्थूल-मान, अम्, n. gross or rough measure, rough computation. —स्थूल-मूल, अम्, n. a large root; a kind of radish (= चाणक्य-मूलक). —स्थूलम्-भविष्णु, उस्, उस्, उ, or स्थूलम्-भावुक, अस्, आ, अम्, becoming large or stout. —स्थूल-लक्ष or स्थूल-लक्ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘having large aims or attributes,’ munificent, liberal, generous; wise, learned; disposed to recol-lect both benefits and injuries; taking careless aim. —स्थूललक्ष्य-त्व, अम्, n. munificence, libe-rality; aiming carelessly. —स्थूल-वर्त्म-कृत्, त्, m. a kind of shrub (= ब्राह्मण-यष्टिका)। —स्थूल-वल्कल, अस्, m. ‘thick-barked,’ the red Lodhra (or Lodh tree, the bark of which is used in tanning, &c.). —स्थूल-वृक्ष-फल, अस्, m. a kind of plant or tree (= स्निग्ध-पिण्डीतक)। —स्थूल-वैदेही, f. a particular plant (= गज-पिप्पली). —स्थूल-शङ्खा, f. a woman having a large vulva. —स्थूल-शर, अस्, m. a kind of large reed. —स्थूल-शरीर, अम्, n. the grosser or material and perishable body with which a soul clad in its subtile body is invested, (opposed to सूक्ष्म-शरीर and लिङ्ग-शरीर, q. q. v. v.); (अस्, आ, अम्), large-bodied, huge. —स्थूल-शाटक, अस्, अका or इका, m. f. or स्थूल-शाटि, इस्, m. thick or coarse cloth. —स्थूल-शालि, इस्, m. a kind of large rice. —स्थूल-शिरस्, अस्, n. a large head or summit; (आस्, आस्, अस्), large-headed. —स्थूल-शीर्षक, अस्, इका, अम्, large-headed; (इका), f. a small ant having a large head in proportion to its size. —स्थूल-षट्-पद, अस्, m. a large bee; wasp. —स्थूल-ष्ठीवि, इस्, m., N. of the father of a grammarian. —स्थूल-सूक्ष्म, अस्, आ, अम्, mighty and subtile (as God who sustains the universe and an atom). —स्थूल-स्कन्ध, अस्, m. ‘having a thick stem,’ the Lakuca tree. —स्थूल-हस्त, अस्, m. a large hand; the thick trunk of an elephant; (अम्), n. an elephant's trunk; (अस्, आ, अम्), having large hands. —स्थू-लांशा (°ल-अं°), f. a kind of Curcuma (= गन्ध-पत्त्रा). —स्थूलान्त्र (°ल-अन्°), अम्, n. the larger intestine near the anus. —स्थूलाम्र (°ल-आम्°), अस्, m. the large Mango tree (= महाराज-चूत)। —स्थूलास्य (°ल-आस्°), अस्, आ, अम्, large-faced, large-mouthed; (अस्), m. a snake. —स्थूली-करण, अम्, n. the act of making large or bulky, enlarging, fattening. —स्थूली-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, made large, enlarged, fattened. —स्थूली-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, be-come large or thick, become bulky, fattened. —स्थू-लैरण्ड (°ल-एर्°), अस्, m. the large castor-oil plant. —स्थूलैला (°ल-एला), f. large cardamoms. —स्थूलोच्चय (°ल-उच्°), अस्, m. ‘rough aggre-gation,’ a large fragment of rock or crag fallen from a mountain and forming an irregular mound or hillock; incompleteness, deficiency, defect; the middle pace of elephants (neither quick nor slow); an eruption of pimples on the face; a hollow at the root of an elephant's tusks.
स्थूलक: स्थूलक, अस्, आ, अम्, large, bulky; (अस्), m. a sort of grass or reed (Saccharum Cylindricum, com-monly called Ulu).
स्थूलिन्: स्थूलिन्, ई, m. a camel; [cf. स्थूरिन्।]
स्थौल: स्थौल, अस्, आ, or ई, अम्, stout, robust (= स्थूल, Ṛg-veda VI. 44, 7).
स्थौललक्ष्य: स्थौललक्ष्य, अम्, n. (fr. स्थूल-लक्ष), the having great aims, munificence, liberality, (Manu VII. 211.)
स्थौलशीर्ष: स्थौलशीर्ष, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. स्थूल-शीर्ष), having a large head or summit, large-headed.
स्थौलाष्ठीवि: स्थौलाष्ठीवि, इस्, m. (sometimes written स्थौ-लष्ठीवि), N. of an ancient grammarian.
स्थौल्य: स्थौल्य, अम्, n. stoutness, bigness, largeness, bulk, size, thickness, coarseness, grossness, denseness, (opposed to सौक्ष्म्य); doltishness, density of intellect.
स्थौणेय: स्थौणेय स्थौणेय, अम्, n. (said to be fr. स्थूणा), a sort of perfume (= ग्रन्थि-पर्ण; commonly called Gāṇṭhiāla).
स्थौणेयक: स्थौणेयक, अम्, n. a kind of perfume.
स्नपन: स्नपन, अस्, आ, अम्, causing to bathe; used for bathing (as water &c.); (अम्), n. causing to bathe, bathing, ablution; washing, sprinkling, wetting.
स्नव: स्नव स्नव। See under rt. 1. स्नु।
स्नव, अस्, m. oozing, drizzling, dripping, trickling.
स्नस्: स्नस् स्नस्, cl. 1. 4. P. स्नसति, स्नस्यति, सस्नास, &c., (according to some) to eject, eject from the mouth, reject (निरासे); to inhabit (निवासे, according to others); to eat (?); [cf. rt. स्नुस्]: Caus. स्नसयति or स्नासयति, &c.
स्नसा: स्नसा स्नसा, f. a tendon, muscle, = स्नाव; [cf. perhaps, according to some, Old Germ. snor, snuor.]
स्ना: स्ना स्ना (probably connected with rt. 1. स्नु), cl. 2. P. (ep. also A.) स्नाति (-ते), Pot. P. स्नायात् (Manu IV. 82; A. anomalous, स्ना-यीत, Mahā-bh. Vana-p. 7072), सस्नौ, स्नास्यति, अस्नासीत्, Prec. स्नायात् or स्नेयात्, स्नातुम् (perhaps originally ‘to float or swim,’ cf. rt. 1. स्नु, 3. नौ, p. 518), to bathe, perform ablution; to perform the ceremony of bathing when leaving the house of a spiritual preceptor: Caus. स्नापयति or स्नप-यति (with preps. the form स्नापयति is more correct), to cause to bathe, wash, cleanse, bathe, wet; to bathe with tears, weep for (?): Desid. सि-स्नासति: Intens. सास्नायते, सास्नाति, सास्नेति; [cf. Gr. νά-ω, νᾶ-μα, να-ρό-ς, νη-ρό-ς, νῆ-αο-ς, νίπτω, νή-χ-ω for ανή-χ-ω; Lat. nâ-re, nâ-s (= Sans. स्नासि), na-ta-re, na-su-s; Goth. nadr; Angl. Sax. nœd-dre, nedre; Old Germ. nacho; Hib. snamhaim, ‘I swim.’]
स्नपित: स्नपित, अस्, आ, अम्, bathed, washed, sprinkled, wetted, moistened.
स्नात्: स्नात्, आन्, आती or आन्ती, आत्, bathing, performing ablution.
स्नात: स्नात, अस्, आ, अम्, bathed, washed, purified by ab-lution, pure; (अस्), m. one whose spiritual instruc-tion is finished; an initiated householder. —स्नाता-नुलिप्त (°त-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, one who is both bathed and anointed.
स्नातक: स्नातक, अस्, m. a Brāhman who has performed the ceremony of ablution (cf. आ-प्लव) required on his finishing his first Āśrama or period of studentship as a Brahma-cārin (and on becoming initiated into the second Āśrama or order of a Gṛha-stha, q. v.); a Brāhman just returned from the house of his pre-ceptor and become a married man or initiated house-holder, (three kinds of Snātakas are enumerated, 1. the Vidyā-snātaka or Brahma-cārin, who, at the end of his period of studentship, has completed a course of study of the Vedas only; 2. the Vrata-snātaka, who has completed the prescribed Vratas or vowed observances, such as fasting, continence, &c., without becoming perfect in the Vedas; 3. the Vidyā-vrata-snātaka or Ubhaya-snātaka, who has com-pleted both the Vedas and the Vratas; this last is of course regarded as the highest kind, see Kullūka on Manu III. 2); a Brāhman who is a Bhikṣu or asker of alms for any religious object or legitimate purpose, (nine kinds are enumerated in Manu XI. 1); any man of the first three classes who is an initiated householder.
स्नातृ: स्नातृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who bathes or washes, a bather.
स्नात्व: स्नात्व, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. fit for ablutions, capable of being used for bathing, (Sāy. स्नात्वाः = स्नानार्-हाः, Ṛg-veda X. 71, 7.)
स्नात्वा: स्नात्वा (Ved. also स्नात्वी), ind. having bathed or washed, having performed ablutions.
स्नान: स्नान, अम्, n. bathing, washing, ablution, dipping in water, wetting, purification by bathing, religious or ceremonial ablution, bathing in sacred waters (considered as a daily observance or as an essential part of some ceremonial); the ceremony of bathing or anointing an idol; anything used in ablution (e. g. water, perfumed powder for the body, &c.). —स्ना-न-तृण, अम्, n. ‘bathing-grass,’ Kuśa grass. —स्ना-न-दीपिका, f., N. of a commentary by Gopī-nātha on the Snāna-sūtra. —स्नान-द्रोणी, f. a bathing-tub. —स्नान-यात्रा, f. ‘bathing procession,’ the festival held on the day of full moon in the month Jyeṣṭha (when images of Kṛṣṇa as Jagan-nātha are carried out and bathed; in Orissa this festival is called Ratha-yātrā). —स्नानयात्रिक, अस्, आ, अम्, attend-ing the above procession at the bathing of Jagan-nātha. —स्नान-वस्त्र, अम्, n. a cloth put on for bathing, a bathing-dress, wet cloth. —स्नान-विधि, इस्, m. the rules of ablution, proper manner of bathing; N. of a Pariśiṣṭa of the Sāma-veda. —स्नान-शील, अस्, आ, अम्, fond of bathing, observing or performing ablution (especially in sacred waters). —स्नान-सूत्र, अम्, n., N. of a Sūtra work (ascribed to Kātyāyana). —स्नानसूत्र-पद्धति, इस्, f., N. of a summary of a commentary by Hari-jīvana-miśra on the Snāna-sūtra. —स्नानागार (°न-आग्°), अम्, n. a bath-room. —स्नानोत्तीर्ण (°न-उत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, rising up from a bath, one who has just completed his ablutions.
स्नानीय: स्नानीय, अस्, आ, अम्, fit for bathing or ablution, suitable for bathing; (अम्), n. water or any article (such as unguents, perfumed powders, &c.) proper for bathing. —स्नानीय-वस्त्र, अम्, n. a cloth tied round the waist for bathing, a bathing dress.
स्नापक: स्नापक, अस्, m. (fr. the Caus.), a servant who bathes his master or attends him while bathing (bringing water and pouring it over his person).
स्नापन: स्नापन, अम्, n. the act of causing to bathe or attending a person while bathing, (Manu II. 209.) —स्नापनोच्छिष्ट-भोजन (°न-उच्°), ए, n. du. the act of bathing another person and eating his leavings, (Manu II. 209.)
स्नापित: स्नापित, अस्, आ, अम्, caused to bathe, attended on while bathing, immersed.
स्नायिन्: स्नायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, bathing; (ई), m. a bather, per-former of ablutions.
स्नास्यत्: स्नास्यत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत्, about to bathe or perform an initiatory ceremonial ablution; (अन्), m. a religious student about to become a Snātaka, (Manu II. 245.)
स्नायु: स्नायु स्नायु, उस्, f. (according to some उस्, m.; said in Uṇādi-s. I. 1. to be fr. rt. स्ना), a sinew, tendon, muscle (described as वायु-वाहिनी-नाडी, ‘a tubular vessel conveying vital air’); the string of a bow; [cf. probably Gr. νεῦρο-ν, νευρ-ά; Lat. ner-vu-s, nerviœ, nervosus; Old Germ. snar-a, snar-ahha, snuor, narwa; Old Sax. naru; Lith. nar-a-s, ner-u.] —स्नायु-बन्धन, अम्, n. a sinew-string. —स्नायु-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made of tendons. —स्नायु-युत, अस्, आ, अम्, possessed of tendons, (Manu VI. 76.) —स्नायु-रज्जु, उस्, उस्, उ, having tendons for cords (said of the body). —स्नाय्व्-अर्मन्, अ, n. a kind of disease of the eyes.
स्नाव: स्नाव, अस्, m. (the form स्नावानि, neut. pl., occurs), a tendon, muscle; (according to some) the vascular membrane investing the bones; [cf. probably Old Germ. senwa; Angl. Sax. sinu, sinw, senw.]
स्नावन्: स्नावन्, आ, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. IV. 112. fr. rt. स्ना), a muscle, sinew (Ved.); = रसिक, a lover (?).
स्निग्ध: स्निग्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, oily, oleaginous, unctuous, greasy, fat, sticky, viscid, cohesive, adhesive; emol-lient, smooth; glossy, shining, resplendent; moist, wet; cooling; bland, kind, amiable; attached, lov-ing, tender, affectionate, friendly, well affected; lovely, agreeable; coarse, thick, dense; (अस्), m. a friend; a sort of pine, (see स्निग्ध-दारु below); the red castor-oil plant; scil. गण्डूष, a particular mode of rinsing the mouth; (आ), f. marrow, = मेदा; (अम्), n. oil; bees'-wax; light, lustre; thickness, coarseness. —स्निग्ध-जन, अस्, m. an affectionate or friendly person, a friend. —स्निग्ध-तण्डुल, अस्, m. a kind of rice of quick growth (= षष्टिक)। —स्निग्ध-ता, f. or स्निग्ध-त्व, अम्, n. unctuous-ness, oiliness; blandness; tenderness, kindness, affec-tion, love. —स्निग्ध-दारु, उ, n. a sort of pine, Pinus Longifolia (= सरल); another kind, Pinus Devadaru. —स्निग्ध-पत्त्र, अस्, आ, अम्, having smooth or glossy leaves; (अस्, आ), m. f. the jujube, Zizyphus Jujuba; (आ), f. a kind of plant (= काश्-मरी); another kind (= पालक्या). —स्निग्ध-पत्त्रक, अस्, m. ‘having smooth leaves,’ a kind of grass; other plants (= घृत-करञ्ज; = गुच्छ-करञ्ज). —स्निग्ध-पिण्डीतक, अस्, m. a kind of Madana tree. —स्निग्ध-फल, अस्, आ, अम्, having unctuous fruit, having glossy fruit; (आ), f. the ich-neumon plant (= नाकुली). —स्निग्ध-वर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, having a glossy or bright colour; having a soft or agreeable complexion.
स्निट्: स्निट् स्निट्, cl. 10. P. स्नेटयति, to go; to love, be in love; [cf. rt. 1. स्निह् below.]
स्निह्: स्निह् 1. स्निह्, cl. 4. P. स्निह्यति, सिष्णेह, स्नेहिष्यति or स्नेक्ष्यति, अस्निहत्, स्नेहितुम् or स्नेग्धुम् or स्नेढुम्, (probably originally) to be adhesive or sticky or viscid; to be bland; to be easily attached; to have affection for, love, regard; to be fond of (with gen.); to be kind to or pleased with; cl. 10. P. स्नेहयति, &c., to be unctuous or greasy: Pass. स्निह्यते, Aor. अस्नेहि: Caus. स्नेहयति, &c., Aor. असिष्णिहत्, to make unctuous, anoint, lubricate; to cause to love, &c.; to dissolve, destroy, kill, slay, (in Naigh. II. 19. स्नेह-यति and [according to some readings] स्नेहति are enumerated amongst the वध-कर्माणः): Desid. सिस्नेहिषति, सिस्निहिषति, सिस्निक्षति: Intens. सेष्णिह्यते, सेष्णेग्धि or सेष्णेढि।
2. स्निह्, ट्, ट्, ट्, or क्, क्, क्, loving, affectionate; one who loves.
स्निग्ध्वा: स्निग्ध्वा or स्निहित्वा, ind. becoming unctuous, becoming bland or affectionate.
स्नीढ: स्नीढ, अस्, आ, अम्, attached, bland, tender, loving.
स्नीहिति: स्नीहिति, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. killing, slaying.
स्नीहिती: स्नीहिती, f., Ved. killing, slaying; malevolent, (Sāy. = वध-कारिणी, Ṛg-veda I. 74, 2.)
स्नेह: स्नेह, अस्, m. oiliness, unctuousness, fattiness, greasiness, lubricity, viscidity (as one of the twenty-four Guṇas of the Vaiśeṣika branch of the Nyāya phil.); moisture; blandness, tenderness, love, affec-tion, kindness; filial love or affection; any unctuous or oleaginous substance, oil, grease, fat, an unguent; a fluid of the body; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a caste (cor-responding to the Vaiśyas). —स्नेह-गुणित, अस्, आ, अम्, endowed with love or affection. —स्नेह-च्छेद, अस्, m. interruption of friendship, cessation or loss of regard. —स्नेह-पक्व, अस्, आ, अम्, cooked or dressed with oil. —स्नेह-पात्र, अम्, n. a worthy object of affection. —स्नेह-पूर्वम्, ind. preceded by affection, affectionately, tenderly, fondly. —स्नेह-प्रवृत्ति, इस्, f. ‘course of friendship,’ affection, love. —स्नेह-प्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, fond of oil; (अस्), m. a lamp. —स्नेह-भाण्ड, अम्, n. an oil-vessel, pot of oil. —स्नेहभाण्ड-जीविन्, ई, m. living by oil-vessels, an oilman. —स्नेह-भू, ऊस्, m. phlegm, rheum, the phlegmatic humor. —स्नेह-भूमि, इस्, f. ‘oil-ground, oil-source,’ any substance yielding oil or grease; any object of affection, one worthy of love. —स्नेह-रङ्ग, अस्, m. ‘oil-coloured,’ se-samum. —स्नेह-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, unctuous, oily; possessed of affection, affectionate; (अती), f. = मेदा (according to Śabda-k.). —स्नेह-वस्ति, इस्, f. a clyster or injection of oil, oily enema. —स्नेह-विद्-ध, अस्, m. ‘pierced or impregnated with oil,’ a sort of pine, Pinus Devadaru (according to Śabda-k. अम्, n.). —स्नेह-विमर्दित, अस्, आ, अम्, rubbed or anointed with oil. —स्नेह-वीज, अस्, आ, अम्, having oily seeds, causing unctuousness, &c.; (अस्), m. the Piyāla tree. —स्नेह-व्यक्ति, इस्, f. manifestation or display of friendship. —स्नेह-संयुक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, mixed with oil, dressed with ghee, (Manu V. 24.) —स्नेह-सम्भाष, अस्, m. kind conversation. —स्नेहाक्त (°ह-अक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, anointed with oil, oiled, greased, lubricated. —स्नेहानुवृत्ति (°ह-अन्°), इस्, f. continuance of affection, affectionate or friendly intercourse. —स्नेहाश (°ह-आश), अस्, m. ‘oil-consumer,’ a lamp.
स्नेह स्नेह, स्नेहिन्। See p. 1149, col. 3.
स्नेहन्: स्नेहन्, आ, m. a friend; the moon; a kind of disease.
स्नेहन: स्नेहन, अस्, ई, अम्, anointing, lubricating; de-stroying; (अस्), m. epithet of Śiva; (अम्), n. the act of anointing, unction, lubrication, rubbing or smear-ing with oil or unguents; unctuousness, being or becoming oily, &c.; an emollient, unguent, lini-ment.
स्नेहनीय: स्नेहनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be anointed or lubri-cated; to be loved.
स्नेहयत्: स्नेहयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, Ved. destroying, killing, murdering.
स्नेहित: स्नेहित, अस्, आ, अम्, anointed, smeared with oil; loved, beloved; kind, affectionate; (अस्), m. a loved one, friend.
स्नेहितव्य: स्नेहितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, = स्नेहनीय above.
स्नेहिती: स्नेहिती, f., Ved. destroying, killing; [cf. स्नीहिती above.]
स्नेहिन्: स्नेहिन्, ई, इनी, इ, oily, unctuous, fat; attached, af-fectionate, friendly; (ई), m. an anointer, smearer; a painter; a friend.
स्नेहु: स्नेहु, उस्, m. the moon; a kind of disease; [cf. स्नेहन्।]
स्नैग्ध्य: स्नैग्ध्य, अम्, n. (fr. स्निग्ध), unctuousness, oiliness, smoothness, lubricity, blandness; tenderness, fondness; affectionateness.
स्नु: स्नु 1. स्नु (probably connected with rt. स्ना), cl. 2. P. स्नौति, सुष्णाव, स्नविष्-यति, अस्नावीत्, स्नवितुम्, to drip, trickle, distil, fall in drops, drop, ooze, run out, leak; to flow, stream; cl. 2. A. (Pass. reflex.) स्नुते, अस्नोष्ट or अस्ना-विष्ट: Pass. स्नूयते, स्नोता or स्नाविता, स्नोष्-यते or स्नाविष्यते, Aor. अस्नावि, to be distilled, &c.: Caus. स्नावयति, &c., Aor. असुष्णवत्: Desid. of Caus. सिस्नावयिषति or सुस्नावयिषति (according to Vopa-deva): Desid. सुस्नूषति: In-tens. सोष्णूयते, सोष्णवीति, सोष्णोति; [cf. Gr. νέ-ω (for σνεϝ-ω), νεύ-σω (for σνεύ-σω), νεῦ-σι-ς, νευ-σ-τήρ, νά-ω (for σναϝ-ω), ἀένα-ο-ς, νᾶ-μα, νᾱ-ρό-ς, νη-ρό-ς, Νη-ρ-εύ-ς, Νη-ιά-(δ)-ς; (probably also ναῦ-ς, ναύ-τη-ς, &c., see under 3. नौ, p. 518): Goth. snu, ‘to go;’ sniva, snau, snivum (for snu-um), snaivs, ‘snow:’ Old Germ. sniutan, sniumi, sneo, snê: Angl. Sax. sniwan, snytan, sneome: Lith. snega-s (w being changed to g): Slav. snêg: Hib. snuadhaim, ‘I flow;’ snuadh, ‘blood;’ sneachd, ‘snow.’]

स्नु 2. स्नु, उस्, उ, m. n. (a defective word optionally substituted for सानु, q. v., in certain cases; according to some fr. rt. 1. सो), the level summit or edge of a mountain, table-land; any top, surface; anything fixed or stationary (as the firmament; Sāy. = स्थित, Ṛg-veda IV. 28, 2).
स्नु 3. स्नु, उस्, f. = स्नायु, a sinew, tendon, muscle. —स्नु-तस्, ind. from the sinews or muscles.
स्नु 4. स्नु, a Kṛd-anta affix to roots form-ing adjectives expressive of an aptitude to be what is implied by the root; [cf. स्थास्नु।]
स्नवन: स्नवन, अम्, n. the act of oozing, trickling; distillation.
स्नुत: स्नुत, अस्, आ, अम्, trickled, distilled, dropped, trickling, flowing, dropping, oozing.
स्नुति: स्नुति, इस्, f. trickling, distilling, oozing, stream, flow.
स्नुत्वा: स्नुत्वा, ind. having trickled or oozed or flowed.
स्नुच्: स्नुच् स्नुच्, cl. 1. A. स्नोचते, &c., to be bright or clear (probably for rt. स्तुच्, but according to Śabda-k., under ष्णुच्, the meaning is सेचने).
स्नुषा: स्नुषा स्नुषा, f. (said to be fr. rt. 1. स्नु), a daughter-in-law; the milk-hedge plant (= 2. स्नुह्); [cf. Gr. νυό-ς; Lat. nuru-s (for snusu-s); Old Germ. snur; Angl. Sax. snoru; Slav. snochâ.]
स्नुस्: स्नुस् स्नुस्, cl. 4. P. स्नुस्यति, सुस्नोष, स्नोसितुम्, to eat; to disappear or become invisible; to take.
स्नुह्: स्नुह् 1. स्नुह्, cl. 4. P. स्नुह्यति, सुष्णोह, स्नोहितुम् or स्नोग्धुम् or स्नोढुम्, to vomit; = rt. 1. स्निह्।

2. स्नुह्, ट्, ट्, ट्, or क्, क्, क्, vomiting, one who vomits; (क्), f. the milk-hedge plant, Euphorbia Antiquorum (its milky juice has various medicinal pro-perties, and is used as an emetic; seventeen synonyms of this plant are enumerated, cf. सीहुण्ड). —स्नुक्-छद, अस्, m. a kind of reed (= क्षीर-कञ्चुकिन्).
स्नुहि: स्नुहि, इस्, or स्नुही, f. = 2. स्नुह् above.
स्नै: स्नै स्नै (also written स्तै, q. v.), cl. 1. P. स्नायति, &c., to dress, wrap round, envelope, adorn.
स्पन्द्: स्पन्द् स्पन्द् (sometimes incorrectly con-founded with rt. स्यन्द्), cl. 1. A. स्पन्-दते, पस्पन्दे, अस्पन्दिष्ट, स्पन्दितुम्, to quiver, throb, tremble, quake, shake, palpitate, beat, to go, move (= rt. स्यन्द्): Pass. स्पद्यते (accord-ing to some), Aor. अस्पन्दि: Caus. स्पन्दयति, Aor. अपस्पन्दत्।
स्पन्द: स्पन्द, अस्, m. throbbing, throb, pulse, tremor, vibration, motion; [cf. वि-ष्पन्द।] —स्पन्द-कारिका, f., N. of a metrical version of the Spanda-sūtra. —स्पन्द-शास्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a work. —स्पन्द-सूत्र, अम्, n., N. of the aphorisms of the Śaiva philosophy (= शिव-सूत्र).
स्पन्दन: स्पन्दन, अम्, n. throbbing, pulsation, palpita-tion, quivering, (throbbings and quiverings of the limbs and different parts of the body are supposed by the Hindūs to indicate good or bad luck; they are therefore minutely described in certain works); tremor, vibration, agitation; the quickening of a child in the womb; rapid motion, going; (according to some) a car, chariot (Sāy. explains स्पन्दने by रथस्य गमने सति, Ṛg-veda III. 53, 19); (अस्), m. a sort of tree.
स्पन्दमान: स्पन्दमान, अस्, आ, अम्, throbbing, quivering, palpitating, beating; going.
स्पन्दित: स्पन्दित, अस्, आ, अम्, throbbed, quivered, agitated, throbbing, beating; gone; (अम्), n. a pulsation, throb.
स्पन्दिन्: स्पन्दिन्, ई, इनी, इ, quivering, throbbing, palpitat-ing, beating, tremulous.
स्परिश: स्परिश, अस्, m. touch (= स्पर्श below; Śab-da-k.).
स्पर्ध्: स्पर्ध् स्पर्ध् (connected with rt. स्पृह्, q. v.; the older form seems to have been स्पृध्, q. v.), cl. 1. A. (ep. also P.) स्पर्धते (-ति), पस्पर्धे, स्पर्धिष्यते, अस्पर्धिष्ट, स्पर्धितुम्, to contend or compete with, contest, vie with, emulate, rival, be equal with; to envy; to challenge, defy, bid defiance to: Pass. स्पर्धते, Aor. अस्पर्धि: Caus. स्पर्धयति, Aor. अप-स्पर्धत्, &c.: Desid. पिस्पर्धिषते: Intens. पा-स्पर्ध्यते, पास्पर्द्धि; [cf. Goth. spauards; Old Germ. spurt; Angl. Sax. spyrd.]
स्पर्ध: स्पर्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, emulous, envious; (आ), f. emulation, rivalry, competition, the successive eleva-tion of rivals; envy, jealousy; defiance; equality with. —स्पर्ध-ता, f. rivalry, emulation, envious-ness.
स्पर्धन: स्पर्धन, अम्, n. competition, emulation; envy.
स्पर्धमान: स्पर्धमान, अस्, आ, अम्, vying, emulating, com-peting, contending with, envying, challenging, de-fying.
स्पर्धित: स्पर्धित, अस्, आ, अम्, contended with, emulated, envied; defied.
स्पर्धित्वा: स्पर्धित्वा, ind. having contended or competed or vied with.
स्पर्धिन्: स्पर्धिन्, ई, इनी, इ, rivalling, emulating, compet-ing; emulous, envious; proud, superb.
स्पर्धिष्यमाण: स्पर्धिष्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, about to contend or compete.
स्पूर्धस्: स्पूर्धस् (probably to be connected with rt. स्पर्ध्), Ved. envy, (Sāy. स्पूर्धसे = स्पर्ध-नाय, Ṛg-veda V. 64, 4.)
स्पर्श्: स्पर्श् स्पर्श् (also written स्पश्, see rt. 5. स्पश्; cf. rt. 1. स्पृश्), cl. 10. A. स्पर्-शयते, अपस्पर्शत, &c., to take, take hold of, touch (= rt. 1. स्पृश्); to unite, join, embrace.
स्पर्श: स्पर्श, अस्, m. touching, touch, perception by touch, handling, contact; sexual union; collision, con-flict, encounter (= सम्-पराय); the quality of tangi-bility (which is the Viṣaya for the skin; see साङ्-ख्य); feeling, sensation; anything which touches or comes in contact, (eleven such Sparśas are enume-rated, viz. 1. उष्ण, hot; 2. शीत, cold; 3. सुख, pleasant; 4. दुःख, painful; 5. स्निग्ध, greasy; 6. विशद, clean; 7. खर, hard; 8. मृदु, soft; 9. श्लक्ष्ण, smooth; 10. लघु, light; 11. गुरु, heavy); who or what affects or acts upon or in-fluences; affection, morbid affection or influence, any-thing the contact or influence of which causes pain or disease, disorder, sickness, fever; air, wind; a consonant of any of the five classes of Gutturals, Palatals, Cerebrals, Dentals, and Labials (so called be-cause the first four are pronounced by the contact of the tongue with the four places of utterance [see स्थान, स्पृष्ट], throat, palate, top of palate, and teeth; the fifth class or labials being formed by contact of the lips); contact (in astron.); presentation, gift, donation, offering, (काक-स्पर्श, a particular cere-mony on the tenth day after a death, putting out a lump of rice as an offering for the crows); a spy (probably for स्पश, q. v.); (आ), f. a wanton or unchaste wo-man. —स्पर्श-तन्मात्र, अम्, n. the subtile ele-ment of tangibility, (see साङ्ख्य।) —स्पर्श-ता, f. a state of contact, touching. —स्पर्श-मणि, इस्, m. ‘touch-stone,’ a kind of stone (supposed to turn everything it touches to gold), the philo-sopher's stone. —स्पर्शमणि-प्रभव, अम्, n. ‘touchstone-production,’ gold. —स्पर्श-लज्जा, f. ‘shrinking from touch,’ the sensitive plant, Mimosa Pudica. —स्पर्श-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having tangi-bility, palpable; agreeable to the touch, smooth, soft. —स्पर्श-वर्ग, अस्, m. a class of consonants, (see under स्पर्श). —स्पर्श-वेद्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be known or apprehended by the sense of touch. —स्पर्श-शुद्धा, f. ‘pure to the touch,’ the plant Asparagus Racemosus. —स्पर्श-सुख, अम्, n. the pleasure of touch. —स्पर्श-स्नान, अम्, n. ablution at the ingress of the sun or moon into an eclipse. —स्पर्श-स्यन्द, अस्, m. a frog (also written स्पर्श-स्पन्द). —स्पर्शानन्दा (°श-आन्°), f. ‘touch-delighting,’ N. of an Apsaras. —स्पर्शोदय (°श-उद्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having a consonant succeed-ing, followed by a consonant.
स्पर्ष्: स्पर्ष् स्पर्ष् (= rt. पर्ष्, q. v.), cl. 1. A. स्पर्षते, &c., to become wet or moist.
स्पश्: स्पश् 1. स्पश् (= rt. 1. पश्, q. v.), cl. 1. P. A. स्पशति, -ते, पस्पाश, पस्पशे, स्पशिष्यति, -ते, अस्पाशीत्, अस्पशिष्ट, स्पशितुम्, to see, behold, perceive clearly, spy out, espy: Caus. स्पाशयति, -ते, -यितुम्, Aor. अपस्पशत्, to destroy; Desid. पिस्पशिषति, -ते: Intens. पास्पश्यते, पा-स्पष्टि; [cf. Zend śpaś; Gr. σκέπ-τ-ο-μαι, σκοπ-ή, σκοπιά, σκοπ-ό-ς, ἐπι-σκοπος, σκώψ; Lat. spec-i-o, con-spic-i-o, specula, speculum, spec-to; Old Germ. speh-o-m, spāh-i, ‘circumspect, prudent.’]

2. स्पश्, ट्, ट्, ट्, Ved. seeing, spying out, perceiving; (ट्), m. one who espies, a spy, messenger, (in the Ṛg-veda especially applied to the messengers (of Varuṇa); a guardian, protector, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda V. 59, 1. स्पल् or स्पट् = स्प्रष्टा = होता, a priest; in Ṛg-veda VIII. 61, 15. स्पट् = सर्वस्य ज्ञाता, ‘omniscient,’ applied to Indra); a ray or rein, (ac-cording to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VI. 67, 5. स्पशः = रश्मयः or चराः।)

स्पश् 3. स्पश्, = rt. 3. पश्, ‘to bind,’ q. v. This rt. is said to have the follow-ing additional meanings — to obstruct, oppose, hinder; to string together; to touch, undertake, perform, (Sāy. पस्पशे = स्पृष्टवान् = अनुतिष्ठति, Ṛg-veda I. 22, 19; अस्पष्ट = उपक्रान्तवान्, I. 10, 2.)
4. स्पश्, ट्, ट्, ट्, Ved. binding.
स्पश् 5. स्पश् (= rt. स्पर्श्), cl. 10. A. स्पाशयते, &c., to take, &c. See rt. स्पर्श्।
स्पश: स्पश, अस्, m. a spy [cf. Old Germ. spëhon, ‘to look;’ spëhu, ‘a spy’]; any secret messenger or emissary; a fight, war, battle; a kind of gladiator who fights with a savage animal for a reward.
स्पष्ट: स्पष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, clearly perceived or discerned, distinctly visible, distinct, clear, evident, manifest, plain, apparent, intelligible; true, real; one who sees clearly; (अम्), ind. clearly, distinctly; openly, boldly, (न स्पष्टम् उद्वीक्षते, he does not look [at me] straight in the face.) —स्पष्ट-गर्भा, f. a woman evidently pregnant. —स्पष्ट-तारक, अस्, आ, अम्, (the sky) which has its stars distinctly seen or clearly displayed. —स्पष्ट-प्रतिपत्ति, इस्, f. clear perception or ascertainment. —स्पष्ट-भा-षिन्, ई, इणी, इ, or स्पष्ट-वक्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, speak-ing clearly or distinctly, plain-spoken. —स्पष्टार्-थ (°ट-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, clear in meaning, obvious, perspicuous, intelligible. —स्पष्टी-करण, अम्, n. the act of making distinct or clear, elucidation. —स्पष्टी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to make dis-tinct or clear. —स्पष्टी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, made plain or clear, explained, expounded, elucidated, made manifest, revealed, exposed. —स्पष्टी-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, become plain or evident. —स्पष्टेतर (°ट-इत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, the reverse of clear, indistinct, un-intelligible.
स्पष्टय: स्पष्टय, Nom. P. स्पष्टयति, &c., to make clear, elucidate.
स्पाशित: स्पाशित, अस्, आ, अम्, caused to be stopped, hindered.
स्पार्ह: स्पार्ह स्पार्ह। See rt. स्पृह्, p. 1151.

स्पार्ह, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. स्पृहा), Ved. wished for, desirable, agreeable, enviable; (अम्), n., Ved. any-thing enviable or beautiful, (Sāy. स्पार्हा = स्पृह-णीयानि तेजांसि, Ṛg-veda I. 135, 2.) —स्पार्ह-रा-धस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. having or bestowing enviable wealth, (Sāy. = स्पृहणीय-धन, Ṛg-veda IV. 16, 16.) —स्पार्ह-वीर, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having enviable heroes or posterity.
स्पृ: स्पृ स्पृ (= rts. 3. स्तृ, 1. स्मृ), cl. 5. P. स्पृणोति, पस्पार, स्पर्तुम्, &c., Ved. to gratify, grant, confer; to extricate from, deliver from, preserve from, defend, (स्पर्तम् in निष्पर्तम् = न्यपारयतम्, ‘you rescued or extricated,’ Ṛg-veda VII. 71, 5); to live; to fill or bestow abun-dantly, (Sāy. स्पृणवाम = पूरयाम, Ṛg-veda V. 44, 10); to live.
स्पर्तृ: स्पर्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, delivering or protecting from, a deliverer; [cf. अव-स्प्°।]
स्पृत्: स्पृत्, त्, त्, त्, gratifying with, conferring; delivering from, (in किल्विष-स्°, delivering from guilt; लोक-स्°, [probably] conferring worlds; cf. धन-स्°।)
स्पृक्का: स्पृक्का स्पृक्का, f. the plant Trigonella Cor-niculata (= पृक्का).
स्पृध्: स्पृध् 1. स्पृध्, a Vedic form of rt. स्पर्ध्, col. 2 (e. g. अस्पृध्रन्, they strove toge-ther, Ṛg-veda VII. 56, 3; पस्पृध्रे = पस्पृ-धिरे; पस्पृधाते = मिथः स्पर्धेते, Ṛg-veda VII. 104, 12).
2. स्पृध्, त्, त्, त्, one who contends or fights; (त्), f. battle, fight (in Naigh. II. 17. स्पृधः is enume-rated among the सङ्ग्राम-नामानि).
स्पृधान: स्पृधान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. contending, vying, rivaling.
स्पृध्य: स्पृध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. vying, emulous, &c. (in मिथ-स्°, q. v.)
स्पृश्: स्पृश् 1. स्पृश् (cf. rt. स्पर्श्), cl. 6. P. (ep. also A.) स्पृशति (-ते), पस्पर्श (3rd pl. पस्पृशुः; ep. 3rd sing. A. पस्पृशे, 3rd pl. पस्पृशिरे), स्प्रक्ष्यति or स्पर्क्ष्यति, अस्प्रा-क्षीत् or अस्पार्क्षीत् or अस्पृक्षत्, Prec. स्पृश्यात्, स्प्रष्टुम् or स्पर्ष्टुम्, to touch, graze; to handle, take hold of, (अन्योन्यं हस्तौ स्पृश-तः, they mutually touch hands, i. e. they shake hands with each other); to cleave to, cling to, come in contact with; to act upon, affect; to take, re-ceive, accept (a sacrificial offering &c.); to reach, attain, obtain, undergo; to wash, sprinkle (e. g. अद्भिस्, with water, Manu II. 60): Pass. स्पृश्यते, Aor. अस्पर्शि, to be touched; to be seized or affected by: Caus. स्पर्शयति, -ते, -यितुम्, Aor. अपस्पर्-शत् or अपस्पृशत् (according to some अपिस्पृशत्), to cause to touch, make to touch (with two acc.); to offer, present, give: Desid. पिस्पृक्षति: Intens. परीस्पृश्यते, परीस्प्रष्टि, परीस्पर्ष्टि, &c.; [cf. Lat. spargo.]
2. स्पृश्, क्, क्, क्, a toucher, who or what touches, touching, piercing (generally in comps.; cf. मर्म-स्पृश्).
स्पर्शक: स्पर्शक, अस्, आ, अम्, touching, who or what touches or comes in contact with, a toucher.
स्पर्शन: स्पर्शन, अस्, ई, अम्, touching, handling; affect-ing, acting upon; (अस्), m. air, wind; (अम्), n. the act of touching, touch, contact; sensation, sense of touch, organ of sensation or feeling, sensitive nerve; gift, donation.
स्पर्शनक: स्पर्शनक, अम्, n. ‘that which touches,’ a term for the skin (in the Sāṅkhya phil.).
स्पर्शनीय: स्पर्शनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be touched, percepti-ble by touch, tangible, sensible, palpable, to be felt, to be handled.
स्पर्शिन्: स्पर्शिन्, ई, इनी, इ, touching, handling.
स्पर्ष्टव्य: स्पर्ष्टव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, tangible, to be felt, to be handled.
स्पर्ष्टृ: स्पर्ष्टृ, टा, ट्री, टृ, who or what touches or affects or acts upon; (टा), m. any agent or affection causing bodily pain or sickness, morbid heat, (the word स्परितृ given in Śabda-k. appears to be a corrupt form of this word; cf. स्परिश।)
स्पार्शनप्रत्यक्ष: स्पार्शनप्रत्यक्ष, अम्, n. (fr. स्पर्शन + प्रत्यक्ष), tactile perception, perception by touch or feel.
स्पृशत्: स्पृशत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत्, touching, handling, &c.
स्पृशा: स्पृशा, f. a kind of plant (= भुजङ्ग-घातिनी, commonly called Kankālikā).
स्पृशी: स्पृशी, f. the prickly nightshade, Solanum Jacquini.
स्पृश्य: स्पृश्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be touched or felt, tangi-ble, sensible.
स्पृश्यमान: स्पृश्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, being touched, being handled.
स्पृष्ट: स्पृष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, touched, felt with the hand, handled; formed by complete contact of the organs of utterance (as the consonants of the five classes of Gutturals, Palatals, Cerebrals, Dentals, and Labials, except the semivowels which are called ईषत्-स्पृ-ष्ट, formed by slight contact, and the sibilants and ह् which are called ईषद्-विवृत, formed by slight opening); defiled. —स्पृष्ट-मात्र, अस्, आ, अम्, merely touched. —स्पृष्ट-मैथुन, अस्, आ, अम्, defiled by sexual intercourse. —स्पृष्टा-स्पृष्टम् or स्पृष्टा-स्पृष्टि, ind. mutual touching, touching one another.
स्पृष्टि: स्पृष्टि, इस्, f. touch, touching, feeling, contact.
स्पृष्टिन्: स्पृष्टिन्, ई, इनी, इ (?) , one who has touched.
स्पृष्ट्वा: स्पृष्ट्वा, ind. having touched or felt or handled.
स्प्रष्टव्य: स्प्रष्टव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be touched, tangible, to be handled.
स्प्रष्टृ: स्प्रष्टृ, टा, ट्री, टृ, = स्पर्ष्टृ above.
स्पृह्: स्पृह् स्पृह् (connected with rts. 1. स्पृध्, स्पर्ध्), cl. 10. P. A. स्पृहयति, -ते, स्पृहयाम्-आस, स्पृहयाम्-बभूव, अपस्पृहत्, स्पृहयितुम्, to desire, wish for, long for (with dat. or gen., e. g. राज्याय न स्पृहये, I do not desire dominion); to envy (with dat. or gen., e. g. न तेषां स्पृहयामि, I do not envy them; कुवेराय स्पृहयति, he envies Kuvera): Pass. स्पृह्यते, to be desired, &c.; [cf. perhaps Gr. σκέρχομαι; Lat. spero; Old Germ. spulgen.]
स्पृहण: स्पृहण, अम्, n. the act of desiring or wishing for.
स्पृहणीय: स्पृहणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be wished or longed for, desirable, enviable. —स्पृहणीय-ता, f. or स्पृहणीय-त्व, अम्, n. desirableness, enviableness. —स्पृहणीय-शोभ, अस्, आ, अम्, having desirable beauty, of enviable beauty.
स्पृहयत्: स्पृहयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, longing for, desiring, envying. —स्पृहयद्-वर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. en-dowed with any form that may be desired, assuming all shapes, (Sāy. = यादृशं वर्णं यजमानः स्पृ-हयति तादृश-वर्णोपेतः, Ṛg-veda II. 10, 15.)
स्पृहयमाण: स्पृहयमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, desiring, wishing for, envying.
स्पृहयाय्य: स्पृहयाय्य, अस्, आ, अम्, desiring, desirable, en-viable, (Sāy. = स्पृहणीय); (अस्), m. epithet of a particular Nakṣatra, (Uṇādi-s. III. 96.)
स्पृहयालु: स्पृहयालु, उस्, उस्, उ, disposed to be desirous or envious of, wishful, desirous, eager for, covetous, cupidinous.
स्पृहयित्वा: स्पृहयित्वा, ind. having desired or wished for.
स्पृहा: स्पृहा, f. desire, eager desire, longing, wish, envy, covetousness.
स्पृहित: स्पृहित, अस्, आ, अम्, desired, wished for, longed for.
स्पृह्य: स्पृह्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be wished for or desired, desirable; (अस्), m. the wild citron tree (= मातु-लुङ्गक).
स्पृह्यमाण: स्पृह्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being desired or longed for.
स्पॄ: स्पॄ स्पॄ (also written स्वॄ, सॄ), cl. 9. P. स्पृणाति, to hurt, kill.
स्फट्: स्फट् स्फट् (thought to be for an original स्पर्त्; cf. Germ. spalten; Eng. split), cl. 1. P. स्फटति, &c., to burst, expand, &c. (= rt. स्फुट्, q. v.): Caus. or cl. 10. P. स्फाटयति, &c., to split open, cleave; to kill (= rt. स्फिट्).
स्फट: स्फट, अस्, आ, m. f. a snake's expanded hood; (ई), f. alum, (see स्फटिकारि below.)
स्फटिक: स्फटिक, अस्, m. crystal, quartz; (आ), f. sulphate of alumina or alum. —स्फटिक-प्रभ, अस्, आ, अम्, glittering like crystal, crystalline, transparent. —स्फ-टिक-मणि-गृह, अम्, n. a house of crystalline gems, crystal-abode. —स्फटिक-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made or consisting of crystal, crystalline. —स्फटिक-स्कम्भ, अस्, m. a crystal pillar. —स्फटिक-हर्-म्य, अम्, n. a crystal palace. —स्फटिकाचल (°क-अच्°), अस्, m. ‘crystal-mountain,’ mount Meru. —स्फटिकात्मन् (°क-आत्°), आ, m. crystal. —स्फ-टिकाद्रि (°क-अद्°), इस्, m. ‘crystal-mountain,’ the mountain Kailāsa. —स्फटिकाद्रि-भिद, अस्, m. ‘penetrating Kailāsa,’ camphor. —स्फटिकाभ्र (°क-अभ्°), अस्, m. ‘crystal-cloud,’ camphor. —स्फटि-काश्मन् (°क-अश्°), आ, m. ‘crystal-stone,’ crystal.
स्फटिकारि: स्फटिकारि, इस्, or स्फटिकारिका or स्फटिकारी, f. sulphate of alumina or alum (commonly corrupted into फट्-करी, फट्-कारी, फट्-किरि).
स्फाटक: स्फाटक, अस्, m. a drop of water; (अम्), n. crystal.
स्फाटिक: स्फाटिक, अस्, ई, अम्, made of crystal, crystalline; (अम्), n. crystal. —स्फाटिकोपल (°क-उप्°), अम्, n. ‘crystal-stone,’ crystal.
स्फाटित: स्फाटित, अस्, आ, अम्, split open, expanded, made to gape, cleft.
स्फण्ट्: स्फण्ट् स्फण्ट्, cl. 1. P. स्फण्टति, &c., to burst, open, expand, &c. (= rt. स्फुट्, q. v.), cl. 10. P. स्फण्टयति, to jest or joke with (= rt. स्फण्ड्).
स्फण्ड्: स्फण्ड् स्फण्ड्, cl. 1. P. स्फण्डति, &c., cl. 10. P. स्फण्डयति, to jest or joke with, to laugh at.
स्फर्: स्फर् स्फर् = rt. स्फुर्, and serving as the form of its Caus. स्फारयति, &c., see स्फुर्, वि-स्फुर्।
स्फरण: स्फरण, अम्, n. trembling, quivering, throbbing, vibration.
स्फार: 1. स्फार, अस्, m. (for 2. see p. 1152), throbbing, quivering, vibration; twanging (of a bow-string; cf. वि-स्फार).

2. स्फार, अस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. II. 13. fr. rt. स्फाय् above; perhaps also connected with rt. स्फर् and 1. स्फार), swelling, increase, enlargement (= वृद्धि); a bubble (in gold &c.); a protuber-ance [cf. Gr. σφαῖρα] (अस्, आ, अम्), large, increased, expanded, spreading, great; abundant; loud; (अम्), n. much, abundance. —स्फारी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भ-वति, &c., to become large or swollen, swell out, expand, spread out; to become manifest.
स्फार स्फार, स्फारण। See p. 1151, col. 3, and above.
स्फारण: स्फारण, अम्, n. the act of throbbing, shaking, trembling; causing to throb or vibrate (fr. the Caus.).
स्फारित: 1. स्फारित, अस्, आ, अम् (for 2. see p. 1152), made to quiver or vibrate [cf. वि-स्फारित]; throbbing; vibrating.
2. स्फारित, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. 2. स्फार above; but perhaps also connected with rt. स्फर्), swollen out, spread out, extended, large.
स्फल्: स्फल् स्फल्, cl. 1. P. स्फलति, पस्फाल, स्फलितुम्, to tremble, quiver, throb, palpitate, beat (= rt. स्फुल्, q. v.): Caus. स्फाल-यति, -यितुम्, to cause to tremble or shake, &c.; [cf. Gr. σφάλλ-ω, σφάλ-μα, ἀ-σφαλ-ής, σφαλ-ερός; Lat. fall-o, fal-sus, falla, fallax, fallac-ia; Old Germ. fallan; Lith. pula, pulti, ‘to fall.’]
स्फाल: स्फाल, अस्, m. throbbing, quivering, palpitation, beat, trembling, shaking.
स्फालन: स्फालन, अम्, n. the act of palpitating, shaking, quivering; causing to shake about or move; rubbing, friction; stroking or patting (a horse &c.).
स्फाय्: स्फाय् स्फाय् (thought by some to be derived from a Pass. of a lost rt. स्पन्, प् becoming फ् through the influence of initial स्; but apparently connected in some senses with rts. स्फर्, स्फुर्), cl. 1. A. स्फायते, पस्फाये, स्फा-यितुम्, to grow large or fat, become bulky, swell, expand, increase: Caus. स्फावयति (perhaps ori-ginally स्फापयति), -यितुम्, Aor. अपिस्फवत् (Pāṇ. VII. 3, 11), to cause to grow large, enlarge, augment, increase; [cf. Gr. σπά-ω, σπά-σ-μα, σπα-σ-μό-ς, ἀ-σπάζομαι, ἀγαπάω (i. e. ἀγαν-σπαω); Lat. spa-ti-um, patere; Old Germ. spannan, spa-nan; Angl. Sax. spanan, spinnan; Goth. spin-nan.]
स्फात: स्फात, अस्, आ, अम्, grown big, swollen, enlarged, increased.
स्फाति: स्फाति, इस्, f. swelling, intumescence, increase, growth.
स्फावयत्: स्फावयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, augmenting, increasing, enlarging.
स्फिर: स्फिर, अस्, आ, अम्, abundant, much, many, large; swollen, expanded; vast, capacious, (Sāy. = वृद्-ध।)
स्फीत: स्फीत, अस्, आ, अम्, swollen, enlarged, bulky, fat, big, large, thick; much, abundant, many, numerous; successful, prosperous; affected by hereditary disease. —स्फीत-ता, f. bulkiness, enlargement; prosperity, successful progress. —स्फीती-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to enlarge, augment.
स्फीति: स्फीति, इस्, f. increase, enlargement; prosperity.
स्फेयस्: स्फेयस्, आन्, असी, अस् (compar. of स्फिर), more abundant, very much or abundant.
स्फेष्ठ: स्फेष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम् (superl. of स्फिर), most abundant, very much or abundant.
स्फिच्: स्फिच् स्फिच्, क्, f. (by some connected with rt. स्फाय्, ‘to be fat’), a buttock, hip; (औ), f. du. the buttocks; [cf. Old Germ. spech; Angl. Sax. spic.] —स्फिक्-घातनक, अस्, m. a particular plant or small tree much used in medicine (= कट्-फल, p. 196, col. 1).
स्फिगी: स्फिगी, f., Ved. the buttock, hip; (this form स्फिगी seems necessary to account for स्फिग्या = कट्या, Ṛg-veda III. 32, 11; स्फिग्यम् = कटि-प्रदेशम्, Ṛg-veda VIII. 4, 8.)
स्फिट्: स्फिट् स्फिट्, cl. 10. P. स्फेटयति, &c., to hurt, injure, kill (= rt. स्फिट्ट्); to despise; to love (according to some); to cover (ac-cording to some).
स्फिट्ट्: स्फिट्ट् स्फिट्ट्, cl. 10. P. स्फिट्टयति, &c., to hurt, kill (= rts. स्फिट्, स्फट्).
स्फुट्: स्फुट् स्फुट् (connected with rts. स्फुर्, स्फुल्), cl. 6. P. स्फुटति, cl. 1. P. A. स्फोटति, -ते, पुस्फोट, पुस्फुटे, अस्फुटत्, अस्-फुटीत्, अस्फोटीत्, स्फुटितुम् (cl. 1. स्फोटितुम्), to burst or become suddenly rent asunder, burst open, split open, part asunder, break forth, expand; to blossom, blow (generally A.); to burst into view, be-come manifested or made public, to disperse, run away; cl. 10. P. स्फुटयति, to burst, crack, break open; to burst into view: Pass. स्फुट्यते, Aor. अस्फोटि: Caus. स्फोटयति, to burst or rend sud-denly, break, split, cleave, tear open, divide; to disclose, make clear; to hurt, destroy, kill; to winnow.
स्फुट: स्फुट, अस्, आ, अम्, burst, split open, broken, rent, torn, opened, expanded; open, blossomed, blown; clearly displayed, clear; plain, distinct, mani-fest, evident; well known or understood; bright; white; loud; spread, diffused; (in astronomy) ap-parent, true; corrected; (आ), f. the expanded hood of a serpent; (अम्), ind. distinctly, manifestly, evi-dently, certainly. —स्फुट-ता, f. openness, mani-festation; perspicuity; blossoming. —स्फुट-तार, अस्, आ, अम्, having stars clearly seen, bright with stars. —स्फुट-पौरुष, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has displayed valour or energy. —स्फुट-फल, अम्, n. (in geometry) clear or precise result (of any calculation); distinct or precise area (of a triangle &c.). —स्फुट-बन्धनी, f. a kind of plant, heart-pea (= पारावत-पदी). —स्फुट-वल्कली, f. the plant heart-pea. —स्फुट-सार, अस्, m. (probably) the true latitude of a star or planet. —स्फुट-सूर्य-गति, इस्, f. apparent or true motion of the sun. —स्फुटार्थ (°ट-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having a clear meaning, intelligible, obvious, significant. —स्फुटी-करण, अम्, n. the act of displaying clearly, making distinct; making true or correct, correction.
स्फुटत्: स्फुटत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत्, bursting open, part-ing or bursting asunder, splitting in two; blowing, blossoming; becoming manifest or clear; evolving.
स्फुटन: स्फुटन, अम्, n. the act of breaking or rending suddenly, bursting, tearing open, disruption, open-ing, expanding, blossoming.
स्फुटनीय: स्फुटनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be broken open or split.
स्फुटि: स्फुटि, इस्, or स्फुटी, f. cracking or chapping of the skin of the feet, sores or swelling of the feet; the fruit of the Karkaṭī or a sort of melon, Cucumis Momordica.
स्फुटिका: स्फुटिका, f. (probably) a small bit broken off, little bit or piece.
स्फुटित: स्फुटित, अस्, आ, अम्, burst, broken open, split, cracked; budded, blown, expanded (as a flower); made clear, manifested, spread out; torn, destroyed; laughed at (= परि-हसित; cf. rt. स्फुण्ट्). —स्फु-टित-चरण, अस्, आ, अम्, having wide feet, splay-footed.
स्फोट: स्फोट, अस्, m. breaking, splitting open, bursting, disclosure, (नर्म-स्फोट in dramatic action is ex-plained to mean भाव-लेशैः सूचितो ऽल्परसः, i. e. slight disclosures or glimpses of love); a swelling, boil, tumor; the idea or disclosure which bursts out or flashes on the mind when a sound is uttered; the eternal sound in the Pūrva-mīmāṃsā; (आ), f. the expanded hood of a snake. —स्फोट-वाद, अस्, m. a dissertation on the above philosophical Sphoṭa. —स्फोट-वीजक, अस्, m. ‘having bursting seeds,’ the marking-nut plant (= भल्लातक).
स्फोटक: स्फोटक, अस्, m. one who bursts or splits open; a swelling, boil, tumor.
स्फोटन: स्फोटन, अस्, ई, अम्, breaking or splitting asunder, opening, making clear, disclosing, manifesting; (अस्), m. (in Vedic grammar) = व्यञ्जक, separated utter-ance of a close combination of consonants; (अम्), n. the act of bursting or rending suddenly, splitting, cracking; tearing; winnowing grain, &c.; cracking the finger-joints, snapping the fingers; (in grammar) the separation of the letters of a double consonant; (ई), f. an instrument for splitting or cleaving, a gimlet, boring-tool, auger [cf. आ-स्फोटनी, लास्फो-टनी].
स्फोटायन: स्फोटायन, अस्, m., N. of an ancient gram-marian, (Pāṇ. VI. 1, 123; he is identified by some with Kakṣīvat.)
स्फोटिका: स्फोटिका, f. a kind of bird, a wagtail (= हापु-त्रिका).
स्फोटित: स्फोटित, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Caus.), made to burst open, rent or torn asunder, disclosed.
स्फुट्ट्: स्फुट्ट् स्फुट्ट्, cl. 10. P. स्फुट्टयति, &c., to despise, disrespect.
स्फुड्: स्फुड् स्फुड्, cl. 6. P. स्फुडति, &c., to cover.
स्फुण्ट्: स्फुण्ट् स्फुण्ट्, cl. 1. P. स्फुण्टति, &c., to open, expand, &c. (= rt. स्फुट्); cl. 10. P. स्फुण्टयति, &c., to jest, joke, laugh at (= rt. स्फण्ड्).
स्फुण्ड्: स्फुण्ड् स्फुण्ड्, cl. 1. A. स्फुण्डते, &c., to open, expand, &c. (= rt. स्फुट्); cl. 10. P. स्फुण्डयति, &c., to jest, &c. (= rt. स्फण्ड्).
स्फुत्: स्फुत् स्फुत्, an imitative sound; [cf. फुत्।] —स्फुत्-कर, अस्, m. ‘making a blowing or crackling sound,’ fire. —स्फुत्-कार, अस्, m. making the noise स्फुत्, crackling, burning.
स्फुर्: स्फुर् स्फुर् (= rt. स्फर्, which appears in the Caus. and is probably the older form, see स्फर्; the rt. स्फुर् is evidently con-nected with rts. स्फुट्, स्फुल्), cl. 6. P. स्फुरति, पुस्फोर, स्फुरिष्यति, अस्फुरीत्, Prec. स्फूर्-यात्, स्फुरितुम्, to tremble, palpitate, throb, vibrate, thrill, quiver, twitch, become agitated, struggle; to start, dart, spring, bound; to spring back, rebound; to spring up, shoot out, break forth, burst out plainly or visibly, start into view, be evident or manifest, appear clearly, become displayed or expanded; to flash, scintillate, twinkle, sparkle, shine, gleam, glitter; to flash on the mind, rush into the memory; to go tremulously; to bruise, destroy, (Sāy. स्फुरत् = स्फुरिष्यति = वाधिष्यति, Ṛg-veda I. 84, 8): Pass. स्फुर्यते, Aor. अस्फोरि: Caus. स्फोरयति, स्फारयति (see rt. स्फर्), -यितुम्, Aor. अपु-स्फुरत्, अपुस्फरत्, to cause to vibrate; to make to shine or glitter; to cast: Desid. पुस्फुरिषति: Intens. पोस्फुर्यते, पोस्फोर्ति; [cf. Zend śpar; Gr. σπαίρ-ω, ἀ-σπαίρ-ω, (probably also) σπείρω, σπέρμα, σποράς, σφυρόν; (probably) Lat. sperno; Angl. Sax. spurnan, spura; Lith. spir-ti, spar-dy-ti.]
स्फुर: स्फुर, अस्, m. trembling, throbbing; swelling; coruscating; a shield.
स्फुरण: स्फुरण, अम्, आ, n. f. the act of trembling, throbbing, pulsation, vibration; quivering or throb-bing of parts of the body (e. g. quivering of the lips, twitching of the eyes, &c., as indicating good or bad luck); springing or breaking forth, starting into view, expansion; flashing, coruscation, scintilla-tion, twinkling, glittering; flashing on the mind.
स्फुरत्: स्फुरत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत्, trembling, shaking, quivering, throbbing; starting, darting; springing up, breaking forth, bursting out plainly or visibly, becoming clear or manifest; flashing, glittering; flashing vividly on the mind; swelling, expanding [cf. स्फुटत्]; going, moving; going tremulously. —स्फुरद्-अधरोष्ठ (°र-ओष्°) or स्फुरद्-ओष्ठ, अस्, ई, अम्, having quivering lips, (स्फुरद्-अधरोष्ठम्, ind. with quivering or pouting lips.) —स्फुरद्-उल्का, f. a shooting meteor, aerolite. —स्फुरदुल्काकृति (°का-आक्°), इस्, इस्, इ, having the form of a shooting meteor.
स्फुरित: स्फुरित, अस्, आ, अम्, trembling, heaving, throb-bing, thrilling, palpitating; shaken, agitated; flash-ing, glittering, gleaming, playing, unsteady; swelled, swollen; (अम्), n. a throb, throbbing, tremor, quivering or twitching of the eyelids, &c., agitation or emotion of mind. —स्फुरित-शतह्रद, अस्, आ, अम्, having flashing lightning (said of a cloud). —स्फुरितोत्तराधर (°त-उत्°, °र-अध्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having trembling upper and under lips.
स्फूर्त: स्फूर्त, अस्, आ, अम्, (according to some) throbbed, throbbing; suddenly risen into remembrance.
स्फूर्ति: स्फूर्ति, इस्, f. throb, palpitation, tremor, trem-bling, shaking, vibration; spring, bound, start; breaking forth visibly, becoming evident or apparent, manifestation, expansion; flashing on the mind or memory. —स्फूर्ति-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, throbbing, thrilling (with joy or excitement), tremulous, agi-tated; tender-hearted; (आन्), m. a follower or wor-shipper of Śiva (= पाशुपत).
स्फोरण: स्फोरण, अम्, n. throbbing, quivering, &c. = स्फार (according to Vopa-deva).
स्फुर्छ्: स्फुर्छ् स्फुर्छ् (also written स्वुर्छ्), cl. 1. P. स्फूर्छति, पुस्फूर्छ, स्फूर्-छितुम्, to spread, extend; to forget.
स्फूर्छित: स्फूर्छित, अस्, आ, अम्, spread; forgotten.
स्फूर्ण: 1. स्फूर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, = स्फूर्छित above.
2. स्फूर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, (according to some) thun-dered.
स्फुर्ज्: स्फुर्ज् स्फुर्ज् (probably connected with rt. स्फुर्), cl. 1. P. स्फूर्जति, पु-स्फूर्ज, स्फूर्जितुम्, to thunder, make a sound like a thunder-clap, crash, explode: Pass. स्फूर्ज्-यते: Caus. स्फूर्जयति: Desid. पुस्फूर्जिषति: Intens. पोस्फूर्ज्यते, पोस्फूर्क्ति; [cf. Lat. spargo; Angl. Sax. sprecan, sprœncan, sprengan, sprin-can, springan.]
स्फूर्ज: स्फूर्ज, अस्, m. the crashing sound of a thunder-clap, thunder; Indra's thunderbolt; sudden burst, (नर्म-स्फूर्ज, sudden burst of love; in dramatic action defined to mean सुखारम्भो भयान्तो नव-सङ्गमः, first union of lovers characterized by joy in the beginning and some cause of fear in the end.) —स्फूर्जा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, thundering.
स्फूर्जक: स्फूर्जक, अस्, m. a sort of ebony tree, Diospyros Glutinosa (= तिन्दुक).
स्फूर्जथु: स्फूर्जथु, उस्, m. a clap of thunder, explosion.
स्फूर्जन: स्फूर्जन, अम्, n. the act of thundering; an explosion, crash.
स्फूर्जयत्: स्फूर्जयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, Ved. overwhelming, crushing, (Sāy. = निष्पिषत्।)
स्फूर्जित: स्फूर्जित, अस्, आ, अम्, thundered; [cf. वि-स्फूर्-जित।]
स्फुल्: स्फुल् स्फुल् (connected with rts. स्फुर्, स्फुट्, स्फल्), cl. 6. P. स्फुलति, पु-स्फोल, Aor. अस्फुलीत्, स्फुलितुम्, to tremble, throb, vibrate; to dart forth, appear; to collect; to slay, kill, (enumerated among the वध-कर्माणः in Naigh. II. 19): Pass. स्फुल्यते, Aor. अस्फोलि: Caus. स्फोलयति, &c. (For comparisons see rt. स्फल्।)
स्फुल: स्फुल, अम्, n. a tent (= वस्त्र-वेश्मन्).
स्फुलन: स्फुलन, अम्, n. trembling, throbbing, vibration, palpitation.
स्फुलिङ्ग: स्फुलिङ्ग, अस्, आ, अम्, m. f. n. (perhaps to be connected with स्फुत्, p. 1152), a spark of fire.
स्फुलिङ्गिन्: स्फुलिङ्गिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having sparks of fire, sparkling; (इनी), f., N. of one of the seven tongues of Agni or fire.
स्फोलन: स्फोलन, अम्, n. = स्फाल (according to Vopa-deva).
स्फ्य: स्फ्य स्फ्य, अम्, n. an implement used in sacrifices (described as a piece of wood shaped like a sword for stirring the boiled rice, or, according to some, for trimming the mound used as an altar). —स्फ्य-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, made or marked out by the स्फ्य. —स्फ्य-वर्तनि, इस्, m. the furrow or line made by the स्फ्य (in marking out the sacrificial ground).
स्फैयकृत: स्फैयकृत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. स्फ्य-कृत), re-lating to anything made by the स्फ्य।
स्बॄ: स्बॄ स्बॄ = rt. स्वॄ, q. v.
स्म: स्म स्म (probably for 2. समा, an old inst. of 1. सम, and meaning ‘wholly, entirely’), ind. a particle added to the present tense of verbs or to present participles (generally giving them a past signification, e. g. प्रविशन्ति स्म पुरीम्, they entered the city); a pleonastic particle (often used after मा, see मा स्म under 1. मा; also in the Veda preceded by अध, q. v., and other particles).
स्मत्: स्मत् स्मत्, ind. (probably connected with स्म; according to some an old neut. of 1. सम; but according to Sāy. a contraction of सुमत्), Ved. well, excellently, (Sāy. = सु, सुमत्); with, together with (= 2. सह; cf. Gr. μετά; Mod. Germ. mit); constantly, always, (Sāy. = नित्यम्।) —स्मत्-पुरन्-धि, इस्, m. = स्वर्ग-कुटुम्बी (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VIII. 34, 6). —स्मद्-अभीशु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. having beautiful reins, (Sāy. = शोभन-रज्जु-युक्त or शोभन-शरीर-कान्ति, Ṛg-veda VIII. 25, 24.) —स्मद्-इष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (according to Sāy.) going well or sent together (= प्रशस्त-गति or सह-प्रेषित, Ṛg-veda VII. 87, 3). —स्मद्-ऊध्नी, f. (see ऊधस्), Ved. (a cow) always giving milk, (Sāy. = नित्यम् उधसा युक्ता, सर्वदा पयसः प्रदात्री, Ṛg-veda I. 73, 6; cf. पी-नोध्नी।) —स्मद्-दिष्टि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. auspiciously speaking (said of Indra; Sāy. = भद्र-वाक्य, Ṛg-veda III. 45, 5); handsome-looking, (Sāy. = प्रशस्त-दर्शन, Ṛg-veda VI. 63, 9.)
स्मय: स्मय, अस्, m. smiling at anything, wonder, sur-prise, astonishment; Wonder (personified as a son of Dharma); pride, conceit, arrogance. —स्मय-नुत्ति, इस्, f. the driving away or pulling down of pride.
स्मर: स्मर, अस्, m. remembrance, recollection; loving recollection, love; Kāma-deva (god of love). —स्मर-कर्मन्, अ, n. amorous action or conduct, any wanton act, lasciviousness. —स्मर-कूपक, अस्, m. or स्मर-कूपिका, f. ‘well of love,’ the female organ. —स्मर-गुरु, उस्, m. ‘love-preceptor,’ epithet of Viṣṇu. —स्मर-गृह, अम्, n. ‘abode of love,’ the female organ. —स्मर-चक्र, अस्, m. a particular kind of sexual union. —स्मर-च्छत्र, अम्, n. the clitoris. —स्मर-दशा, f. a state of love, state of the body produced by being in love, (ten such states are enu-merated, e. g. anxious thought, sleeplessness, emacia-tion, loss of appetite, fainting, &c.) —स्मर-दायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, causing or exciting love (= कामोद्दीपक)। —स्मर-दीपिका, f., N. of a work. —स्मर-ध्व-ज, अस्, m. ‘love-sign,’ ‘love-emblem,’ the male organ; a fabulous fish (regarded as the emblem of Kāma-deva; cf. मकर-ध्वज); a musical in-strument; (आ), f. a bright moonlight night (accord-ing to some); (अम्), n. the female organ. —स्मर-प्रिया, f. ‘dear to Kāma,’ epithet of Rati (Kāma-deva's wife). —स्मर-भासित, अस्, आ, अम्, love-illuminated, inflamed by love. —स्मर-मन्दिर, अम्, n. ‘love-palace,’ the female organ. —स्मर-मोह, अस्, m. infatuation of love, passion, love. —स्मर-मोहित, अस्, आ, अम्, infatuated by love, overcome by passion. —स्मर-लेखनी, f. the Śārikā bird. —स्मर-वल्लभ, अस्, m. ‘love's fa-vourite,’ epithet of A-niruddha. —स्मर-वाण-पङ्क्ति, इस्, f. the five arrows of Kāma-deva collec-tively (see पञ्च-वाण). —स्मर-वीथिका, f. ‘love-shop,’ a prostitute, harlot. —स्मर-वृद्धि-सञ्-ज्ञ, अस्, m. a particular shrub (= काम-वृद्धि)। —स्मर-शवर, अस्, m. ‘love-barbarian,’ cruel love. —स्मर-शासन, अस्, m. ‘chastiser of Kāma-deva,’ epithet of Śiva (see अन्-अङ्ग). —स्मर-सख, अस्, m. ‘love's friend,’ the moon. —स्मर-स्तम्भ, अस्, m. ‘love-column,’ the male organ. —स्मर-स्मर्य, अस्, m. a donkey, ass (= गर्द-भ). —स्मर-हर, अस्, m. ‘love-destroyer,’ epi-thet of Śiva (see अन्-अङ्ग). —स्मराकुल or स्म-राकुलित (°र-आक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, agitated by love, love-sick. —स्मरागार (°र-आग्°), अम्, n. ‘love-abode,’ the female organ. —स्मराङ्कुश (°र-अङ्°), अस्, m. ‘love-hook,’ a finger-nail; a lover, lascivious person. —स्मरातुर (°र-आत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, love-sick, pining with love. —स्मरान्ध (°र-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, love-blinded, infatuated with passion. —स्मरारि (°र-अरि), इस्, m. ‘enemy of Kāma-deva,’ epithet of Śiva. —स्मरार्त (°र-आर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, love-sick. —स्मरासव (°र-आस्°), अस्, m. ‘love-liquid,’ saliva. —स्मरोत्सुक (°र-उत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, pining or languishing with love, love-sick.
स्मार्त: स्मार्त, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. स्मृति), relating to memory, memorial, remembered, coming within the range of memory; recorded in the Smṛtis, prescribed in the inspired codes of law, based on Smṛti, q. v.; sanc-tioned by law, canonical, legal; following the doc-trine of the law-books; domestic (applied to the domestic fire which every Brāhman is bound to keep up); (अस्), m. a Brāhman skilled in jurisprudence or traditional law (especially one belonging to a sect founded by Śaṅkarācārya, whose expositions of the principle of unity, according to the Vedānta doc-trine, they professedly follow, though holding Śiva in especial honour; their chief establishment is at Śṛṅga-giri, but they are said to be found throughout the south of India); (अम्), n. any act or rite enjoined by Smṛti or allowed by traditional usage, a legal act. —स्मार्त-कर्मन्, अ, n. a rite enjoined in the Smṛtis, one of the less important domestic rites. —स्मार्त-काल, अस्, m. the period to which memory may extend (i. e. a century, according to some lawyers). —स्मार्त-सूत्र, अम्, n. any Sūtra work based on Smṛti (opposed to श्रौत-सूत्र or Sūtras based on श्रुति, see सूत्र). —स्मार्त-होम-परि-शिष्ट, अम्, n., N. of a Pariśiṣṭa of the Sāma-veda.
स्मि: स्मि स्मि, cl. 1. A. स्मयते (ep. also P. -ति), सिष्मिये, स्मेष्यते, अस्मेष्ट, स्मेतुम्, to smile, laugh; to expand, bloom (as a flower): Pass. स्मीयते, Aor. अस्मायि: Caus. स्मा-ययति, -ते (also स्मापयते in वि-स्मि, q. v.), to cause to laugh, provoke or excite laughter; (A.) to laugh at, mock, despise: Desid. सिस्मयिषते: Intens. सेष्मीयते, (in Mālavikāgnimitra, Act IV, the Prākṛt सिमिसिमा-अन्ति [see s.v.] is incorrectly referred to the Intens. of rt. स्मि), सेष्मयीति, सेष्-मेति; [cf. Gr. μεῖ-δ-ος, μεί-δ-η-μα, μει-δ-ά-ω, μει-διάω, (perhaps also) σμοιός. μέμφομαι, μῶμος: Lat. mi-ru-s, ni-miru-m, mira-ri: Old Germ. smie-l-en, smie-r-en: Eng. smile: Angl. Sax. smœrc: Slav. sme-ja-ti, po-sme-chu: Lett. smee-t: Hib. smigeadh, magadh, ‘mocking;’ magamhuil, ‘jeering.’]
स्मयत्: स्मयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, smiling, laughing.
स्मयन: स्मयन, अम्, n. the act of smiling, a smile, gentle laughter.
स्मयनीय: स्मयनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be smiled (used im-personally).
स्मयमान: स्मयमान, अस्, आ, अम्, smiling, gently laugh-ing.
स्मयिन्: स्मयिन्, ई, इनी, इ, smiling, laughing.
स्मित: स्मित, अस्, आ, अम्, smiled, smiling; expanded, blown, blossomed; (अम्), n. a smile, gentle laugh. —स्मित-दृश्, क्, f. ‘having a smiling look,’ a hand-some woman. —स्मित-पूर्व, अस्, आ, अम्, preceded by a smile; (अम्), ind. with a smile, smilingly. —स्मित-पूर्वाभिभाषिन् (°व-अभ्°), ई, इणी, इ, addressing with a smile. —स्मित-शालिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having smiles, smiling, laughing. —स्मित-शोभिन्, ई, इनी, इ, smiling beautifully.
स्मिति: स्मिति, इस्, f. smiling, a smile, laughter.
स्मित्वा: स्मित्वा, ind. having smiled or laughed.
स्मेतव्य: स्मेतव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be smiled (used imper-sonally).
स्मेर: स्मेर, अस्, आ, अम्, smiling, laughing; blown, blooming, opened, expanded (as a flower); proud; evident, apparent; (अस्), m. (according to some) ap-pearance, manifestation. —स्मेर-मुख, अस्, ई, अम्, smiling-faced, having a smiling face. —स्मेर-विष्-किर, अस्, m. ‘proud bird,’ a peacock.
स्मिट्: स्मिट् स्मिट् (connected with rt. स्मि), cl. 10. P. स्मेटयति, &c., to slight, despise; to love; to go.
स्मील्: स्मील् स्मील् (= rt. श्मील्, p. 1023; cf. rt. मील्), cl. 1. P. स्मीलति, &c., to wink, blink.
स्मृ: स्मृ 1. स्मृ (= rt. स्पृ, q. v.), cl. 5. P. स्मृणोति, &c., to please, gratify; to protect, defend; to live.

स्मृ 2. स्मृ, cl. 1. P. (ep. also A.) स्मरति (-ते), सस्मार (2nd sing. सस्मर्थ, 1st du. सस्मरिव, 3rd pl. सस्मरुस्), स्मरिष्यति, अस्मार्षीत्, स्मर्तुम्, to remember (with acc. or gen., and when joined with 2nd Fut. of another rt. giving it a past signification, e. g. अमुं स्मरति ह-निष्यति, he remembers having killed him, Pāṇ. III. 2, 112); to recollect, call to mind, bear in mind, think of, think upon, be mindful of; to recite men-tally or call upon the name (of a deity &c.); to re-cord (in the Smṛti), declare (as Smṛti or law; स्मरन्ति, they declare in the Smṛti); to desire, long for (with gen.): Pass. स्मर्यते, Aor. अस्मारि, Prec. स्मृषीष्ट and स्मरिषीष्ट, to be remembered; to be recorded; to be mentioned; to be declared (as a law); to be mentioned in the Smṛti: Caus. स्मार-यति (or स्मरयति), -ते, -यितुम्, Aor. असस्मरत्, त, to cause to remember, call to mind, remind; to give information; to cause to regret, cause to desire or long for (in the latter sense only स्मरयति): Desid. सुस्मूर्षते, to wish to recollect: Intens. सास्मर्यते, सास्मर्ति; [cf. Gr. μέρ-μηρ-α, μέρ-ι-μνα, μερ-μαίζω, μερμηρ-ίζω, μέρ-μερ-ος, μάρ-τυρ, μάρ-τυρ-ο-ς, μάρ-τυ-ς, μαρ-τύρ-ιον, μαρτύρ-ο-μαι, (perhaps also) μέλειν, μέλ-ε-σθαι, μελ-έ-τη, &c.: Lat. me-mor, memor-ia, memor-ā-re, mor-a, mos, mor-is: Goth. mêr-j-an, ‘to proclaim;’ meritha, maurnan: Old Germ. smer-zo, m., smer-za, f. ‘pain;’ smerzan, mâriu, ‘to announce;’ māri, ‘memorable:’ Mod. Germ. Mährchen: Angl. Sax. mœlan, mal, ge-mœred, mœrdh, mœrsian, mel-dian, ameldian, murnan, smeortan, ‘to smart:’ Lith. uz-mirs-tu, ‘to forget:’ Hib. smuairean, ‘dejection;’ (perhaps) smalanach, ‘sorrowful;’ muirn, ‘natural affection.’]
स्मरण: स्मरण, अम्, n. the act of remembering, re-membrance, memory, recollecting, recollection, re-miniscence; tradition, traditional precept, (इति स्मर-णात्, ‘from its being so mentioned in the Smṛti,’ cf. स्मृति); mental recitation (of the name of a deity), calling upon the name of a god; regretting, remem-bering with regret; thinking upon, anxious thought. —स्मरण-पदवी, f. ‘road to mere memory,’ death. —स्मरणानुग्रह (°ण-अन्°), अस्, m. the favour of remembrance, kind remembrance. —स्मर-णापत्य-तर्पक (°ण-अप्°), अस्, m. ‘satisfying memory's offspring,’ a turtle, tortoise. —स्मरणा-यौगपद्य (°ण-अय्°), अम्, n. the non-simulta-neousness of recollections.
स्मरणीय: स्मरणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be remembered, memo-rable, to be borne in mind.
स्मरत्: स्मरत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, remembering, recollecting, considering.
स्मर्तव्य: स्मर्तव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be remembered, memo-rable.
स्मर्तृ: स्मर्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who remembers or re-collects. —स्मर्तृ-त्व, अम्, n. remembrance, recol-lection.
स्मर्यमाण: स्मर्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being remembered, being mentioned in the Smṛti.
स्मारक: स्मारक, अस्, इका, अम्, reminding, putting in mind, instructing.
स्मारण: स्मारण, अम्, n. (fr. the Caus.), the act of caus-ing to remember, reminding, calling to mind.
स्मारित: स्मारित, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Caus.), reminded, called to mind, recalled to recollection.
स्मारिन्: स्मारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, remembering; reminding.
स्मार्य: स्मार्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be remembered, memo-rable.
स्मृत: स्मृत, अस्, आ, अम्, remembered, recollected, called to mind; recorded, mentioned, said, declared, termed, styled, named; enjoined by Smṛti or traditional law, declared or propounded in the law-books. —स्मृत-मात्र, अस्, आ, अम्, only remembered or thought of.
स्मृति: स्मृति, इस्, f. remembrance, memory, reminiscence, recollection, thinking of or upon (any person or thing), calling to mind; Memory (personified as a daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Aṅgiras); what is remembered, that which is borne in mind from the beginning, tradition, law; the institutes or body of traditional or memorial law (as handed down ori-ginally by Manu, Yājñavalkya, and other great legis-lators who were supposed to have been inspired, and to have based their precepts on the Veda and divine revelation, though the laws they promulgated were called Smṛti, ‘what is remembered,’ in contradistinc-tion to Śruti, ‘what is heard or revealed,’ and to Ācāra, ‘established usage;’ the very essence of Smṛti being that it was delivered memoriter by human authors, and not directly revealed, as explained in Manu II. 10, see श्रुति; in its widest acceptation Smṛti is said to include the Vedāṅgas, the Sūtras or aphorisms both श्रौत and गृह्य, the institutes of Manu and other inspired law-givers, the Itihāsas, such as the Rāmāyaṇa and Mahā-bhārata, and the Purāṇas, but the term Smṛti is more usually re-stricted to the metrical codes of Manu, Yājñavalkya, Parāśara, &c., see स्मृति-शास्त्र below); any par-ticular law-book or code of laws; any particular law or rule of law, canon, legal text (e. g. अनुमिता स्मृतिः प्रत्यक्षया स्मृत्या बाध्यते, a Smṛti which is only inferred is set aside by a visibly exist-ing Smṛti; इति स्मृतेः, according to such a Smṛti or legal text, according to such a traditional law); a passage in a work treating of law; pensive or loving recollection, desire, wish [cf. स्मर]; under-standing. —स्मृति-कौमुदी, f. ‘light of law,’ N. of a legal work by Viśveśvara (composed under the patronage of king Madana-pāla). —स्मृति-कौस्तु-भ, ‘jewel of law,’ N. of a work by Ananta-deva. —स्मृति-चन्द्रिका, f., N. of a legal work. —स्मृ-ति-तत्त्व, अम्, n. ‘digest of legal truth,’ N. of a work by Raghu-nandana. —स्मृति-दर्पण, ‘mirror of law,’ N. of a work. —स्मृति-प्रत्यवमर्श, अस्, m. retentiveness of memory, accuracy of recollec-tion. —स्मृति-प्रबन्ध, अस्, m. a Smṛti com-position, legal work. —स्मृति-भ्रंश, अस्, m. loss or failure of memory. —स्मृति-मञ्जरी, f., N. of a legal work. —स्मृति-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a good memory, remembering, recollecting. —स्मृति-महार्णव (°हा-अर्°), अस्, m. ‘ocean of law,’ N. of a work. —स्मृति-रत्नाकर (°न-आक्°), अस्, m. ‘jewel-mine of law,’ N. of a work by Caṇḍeśvara. —स्मृतिरत्नावली (°न-आव्°), f. ‘string of jewels of law,’ N. of a work by Rāma-nātha. —स्मृति-रोध, अस्, m. temporary interruption or obstruction of memory, failure of memory. —स्मृति-विभ्रम, अस्, m. confusion of memory. —स्मृति-विरुद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, contrary to law, illegal, unjust. —स्मृति-विरोध, अस्, m. opposition to law, illegality, im-propriety;
