disagreement between two or more codes of law or legal texts. —स्मृति-शास्त्र, अम्, n. a law-book, a code, digest; legal science, (the most cele-brated law-books are those of Manu, Yājñavalkya with its commentary the Mitākṣarā, Parāśara, Hā-rīta, Vyāsa, Vasiṣṭha, Viṣṇu, Vṛhas-pati, Atri, Śaṅ-kha, Likhita, Uśanas, Aṅgiras, Yama, Āpastamba, Saṃvarta, Śātātapa, Kātyāyana, Dakṣa, Gautama; these authors are sometimes classed in three divisions, under the three heads of सात्त्विक, राजस, and तामस, according to the tendency of their writings.) —स्मृति-शील, ए, n. du. traditions and moral prac-tices. —स्मृति-शेष, अस्, आ, अम्, one of whom only remembrance remains, a deceased or defunct person; that of which nothing is left but remembrance. —स्मृति-शैथिल्य, अम्, n. temporary failure or loss of memory. —स्मृति-सङ्ग्रह or स्मृति-समुच्चय, अस्, m. ‘law-collection,’ N. of two legal works. —स्मृति-सम्मत, अस्, आ, अम्, approved by law. —स्मृति-सागर and स्मृति-सागर-सङ्-ग्रह and स्मृति-सागर-सार, N. of various legal works. —स्मृति-साध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, capable of being proved by law. —स्मृति-सार, अस्, m. ‘essence of law,’ N. of a work by Deva-yājñika; of another work by Yādavendra; of another by Hari-nātha. —स्मृति-सारावली (°र-आव्°), f. ‘line of es-sence of law,’ N. of a work. —स्मृति-सिद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, established by law. —स्मृति-हारिका, f. ‘memory-seizer,’ N. of a daughter of Duḥsahana (described in the fifty-first chapter of the Mārkaṇ-ḍeya-Purāṇa as exercising an evil influence on the memory). —स्मृति-हेतु, उस्, m. a cause of recollec-tion, any mental act stirring the memory, impression on the mind, reflection, association of ideas, recollec-tion. —स्मृत्य्-अन्तर, अम्, n. another law-book. —स्मृत्य्-अपेत, अस्, आ, अम्, departed from memory, forgotten; inconsistent with Smṛti; illegal, unjust. —स्मृत्य्-अर्थ-सागर, अस्, m., N. of a work by Nṛ-siṃha. —स्मृत्य्-अर्थ-सार, अस्, m. ‘essence of the meaning of Smṛti,’ N. of a work on Hindū cere-monies by Śrīdhara-svāmin. —स्मृत्य्-उक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, prescribed in the codes of law, enjoined by the Smṛtis, canonical.

स्य: स्य स्य, अम्, n., Ved. a winnowing basket (= शूर्प, q. v.).
स्यन्द्: स्यन्द् स्यन्द्, cl. 1. A. (in Fut., Aor., and Condit. also P., Ved. also P. in other tenses), स्यन्दते (-ति), सस्यन्दे (Ved. 3rd pl. Perf. स्यद: स्यद, अस्, m. rapid motion, speed, velocity, rush.
स्यन्तव्य: स्यन्तव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be flowed, &c.
स्यन्त्त्वा: स्यन्त्त्वा or स्यन्त्वा, ind. having flowed; having rushed on.
स्यन्द: स्यन्द, अस्, m. trickling; going, moving rapidly; a car, chariot.
स्यन्दत्: स्यन्दत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, moving on, rushing im-petuously.
स्यन्दन: स्यन्दन, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, flowing, going quickly; quick, expeditious, swift; (अस्), m. a war-chariot, chariot, car; air, wind; the tree Dalbergia Ougei-nensis (= तिनिश); a particular Arhat of the past era; (ई), f. saliva; (according to some) the urinary pas-sage; (अम्), n. the act of trickling, oozing, drop-ping; rushing, going or flowing swiftly; water. —स्यन्दन-द्रुम, अस्, m. the tree Dalbergia Ougeinensis (said to be so called because its wood is used to make chariot-wheels &c.). —स्यन्दनारू-ढ (°न-आर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, mounted on a chariot or car. —स्यन्दनारोह (°न-आर्°), अस्, m. a warrior who fights mounted on a war-chariot. —स्यन्दना-लोक-भीत (°न-आल्°), अस्, आ, अम्, terrified at the sight of a chariot.
स्यन्दनि: स्यन्दनि, इस्, m. the tree Dalbergia Ougeinensis.
स्यन्दनिका: स्यन्दनिका, f. a drop of saliva.
स्यन्दनीय: स्यन्दनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be flowed; to be run; to be gone.
स्यन्दमान: स्यन्दमान, अस्, आ, अम्, trickling, flowing, mov-ing rapidly.
स्यन्दितृ: स्यन्दितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who runs or rushes quickly.
स्यन्दित्वा: स्यन्दित्वा, ind. having flowed; having rushed.
स्यन्दिन्: स्यन्दिन्, ई, इनी, इ, trickling, oozing, dropping; flowing, rushing; going, moving; (इनी), f. saliva; a cow bearing two calves at once.

स्यन्न: स्यन्न, अस्, आ, अम्, flowed, trickled, dropped; dropping, trickling, flowing (as water &c.).
स्यम्: स्यम् स्यम्, cl. 1. P. स्यमति, सस्याम (3rd pl. सस्यमुस् or स्येमुस्), स्य-मिष्यति, अस्यमीत्, स्यमितुम्, (according to Vopa-deva also) cl. 10. स्यान्त: स्यान्त, अस्, आ, अम्, sounded; gone, &c.
स्यमन्तक: स्यमन्तक स्यमन्तक, अस्, m. the jewel worn by Kṛṣṇa (given to Satrā-jit by the Sun and transferred by him to his brother Prasena, from whom it was taken by Jāmbavat, and after much fighting and contention appropriated by Kṛṣṇa; the whole story is told in Viṣṇu-Purāṇa IV. 13; the jewel is described as yielding daily eight loads of gold and preserving from all dangers; it is said to have been worn by Kṛṣṇa on his wrist, that on his breast being called Kaustubha).

स्यात्: स्यात् स्यात्, ind. (properly 3rd sing. Pot. of rt. 1. अस्), it may be, perhaps, perchance, (स्याद् अस्ति, it may be, perhaps it is; स्यान् नास्ति, it may not be.) —स्याद्-वाद, अस्, m. (अस्), m. a proper N. —स्वाङ्गि, a patronymic from Svāṅga, (Vopa-deva VII. 1, 4.) —स्वाधिकार (स्व-अध्°), अस्, m. own office or function, peculiar station. —स्वा-धिपत्य (स्व-अध्°), अम्, n. own supremacy, su-preme sway, royalty, sovereignty. —स्वादिष्ठान (स्व-अध्°), अम्, n. one of the six Cakras or mys-tical circles of the body, (see चक्र।) —स्वाधीन (स्व-अध्°), अस्, आ, अम्, self-subject, self-dependent; independent, uncontrolled; in one's own power or subjection, dependent on or belonging to one's own side or party, one's own subject or dependent, faithful. —स्वाधीन-कुशल, अस्, आ, अम्, having prosperity in one's own power. —स्वाधीन-ता, f. or स्वाधीन-त्व, अम्, n. self-dependence, independ-ence; subjection to one's self. —स्वाधीन-पतिका or स्वाधीन-भर्तृका, f. a woman who has a hus-band subject to herself or dependent on herself, an independent woman. —स्वाध्याय (स्व-अध्°), अस्, m. ‘going over any subject to one's self,’ self-recit-ing, self-reading, repeating or rehearsing to one's self, inaudible reading or muttering of prayers, private prayer, (especially) repetition or study of the Vedas, sacred study; perusal of sacred books; the Veda; a day on which the resumption of sacred study is com-manded after a suspension of it. —स्वाध्याय-ब्राह्-मण, अम्, n., N. of a chapter in the Taittirīyāra-ṇyaka (ascribed to Kaṭha). —स्वाध्याय-वत्, आन्, m. a student of the Vedas. —स्वाध्यायार्थिन् (°य-अर्°), ई, m. one who seeks a maintenance for him-self during his studentship, (Manu XI. 1.) —स्वा-ध्यायिन्, ई, m. one who recites or repeats to himself, (especially) a repeater or student of the Vedas; a tradesman, dealer. —स्वानुभव (स्व-अन्°), अस्, m. one's own personal experience or observation. —स्वानुभूति (स्व-अन्°), इस्, f. one's own experi-ence; self-enjoyment. —स्वानुभूत्य्-एक-सार (स्व-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, whose only essence consists in self-enjoyment. —स्वानुरूप (स्व-अन्°), अस्, ई, अम्, ‘self-conformable,’ natural, innate. —१। स्वान्त (स्व-अन्°), अम्, n. (for 2. see s. v.), ‘having the end in itself,’ the mind (= मनस्); a cavern. —स्वान्यदीय-त्व (स्व-अन्°), अम्, n. the state of being one's own or some one else's. —स्वान्यदीयत्व-सन्देह, अस्, m. doubt about ‘meum’ and ‘tuum.’ —स्वायत्त (स्व-आय्°), अस्, आ, अम्, subject to one's self; uncontrolled by others, one's own master. —स्वायत्ती-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to make subject to one's self. —स्वा-रुह्, ट्, ट्, ट्, Ved. = स्व-रुह्. —स्वार्जित (स्व-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, self-acquired, acquired by one's own efforts. —स्वार्थ (स्व-अर्°), अस्, m. one's own ob-ject or aim or wish, own advantage or interest, self-interest; one's own property or substance; own meaning, inherent or real meaning, true interpreta-tion, similar meaning, a pleonasm; (according to Śabda-k.) = लिङ्गार्थ-विशेष; (अस्, आ, अम्), hav-ing one's own object or aim; having [its] own true and natural mean-ing, having a literal meaning; done with one's own wealth. —स्वार्थिन्, ई, इनी, इ, pursuing one's own objects, self-seeking. —स्वार्थोपपत्ति (°थ-उप्°), इस्, f. the gaining or accomplishing of one's own ob-ject. —स्वाश्रित (स्व-आश्°), अस्, आ, अम्, dependent on one's self. —स्वी-करण, &c., see col. 3. —स्वेच्-छा (स्व-इच्°), f. one's own wish or will, own inclina-tion, self-will, wilfulness. —स्वेच्छाचार (°छा-आच्°), अस्, m. acting as one likes, doing what is right in one's own eyes. —स्वेच्छा-तस्, ind. according to one's own will or inclination. —स्वेच्छाधीन (°छा-अध्°), अस्, आ, अम्, dependent on one's own will or inclination. —स्वेच्छा-मृत्यु, उस्, m. ‘dying at his own will,’ epithet of Bhīṣma (who had received from his father the power of fixing the time of his own death; see Mahā-bhārata, Bhīṣma-parvan 5674). —स्वेच्छाहार (°छा-आह्°), अस्, आ, अम्, eating any-thing at one's pleasure. —स्वेच्छाहार-विहार, अस्, m. feeding and roaming about according to one's in-clination. —स्वेदु-हव्य (स्व-इद्°), अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. probably = स्व-समृद्ध-हविष्क, (see Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 121, 6, where the word इदु is referred either to rt. इन्द् or rt. इन्ध्।) —स्वेष्ट (स्व-इष्°), अस्, आ, अम्, self-desired, wished for. —स्वोक्त (स्व-उक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, spoken by one's self, (स्वोक्तम् आक्षिपति, he corrects his own previous remark.) —स्वोदय (स्व-उद्°), अस्, m. the rising of a sign or any heavenly body at any particular place (de-termined by adding to or deducting from the लङ्को-दय or time of rising at Ceylon). —स्वोपधि (स्व-उप्°), इस्, m. self-support; (probably) a fixed star. —स्वोपार्जित (स्व-उप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, self-gained, self-acquired (as wealth &c.). —स्वौजस् (स्व-ओज्°), आस्, आस्, अस्, having natural or peculiar energy; (आस्), m. a proper N.
2. स्व, Nom. P. स्वति, according to Vopa-deva XXI. 7. = स्व इवाचरति, he acts like himself, he acts like his kindred.
स्वक: स्वक, अस्, आ, or इका, अम्, own, one's own, proper, peculiar.
स्वकीय: स्वकीय, अस्, आ, अम्, own, one's own; belonging to one's self, belonging to one's own family; (आ), f. one's own wife; [cf. स्वीया।] —स्वकीय-ता, f. owner-ship, one's own property.
स्वयम्: स्वयम्, ind. self, myself, himself, herself, itself, one's self, &c. (applicable to all persons and sometimes used emphatically with other pronouns, e. g. अहं स्वयम्, ‘I myself;’ sometimes used alone, e. g. स्वयं तत् कृतवान्, I or thou or he did that him-self; स्वयं तत् कृतवती, she did that herself; स्वयं तत् कुर्वन्ति, they do that themselves); by one's self, spontaneously, of one's own self, of one's own accord; [cf. Hib. feiñ, ‘own, self;’ sin, ‘that, there;’ siom, ‘they, them:’ Cambro-Brit. hun, ‘he himself.’] —स्वयं-वर, अस्, m. ‘self-choice,’ the election of a husband by a princess or daughter of a Kṣatriya at a public assembly of suitors held for the purpose; (आ), f. a maiden who thus chooses her own husband. —स्वयंवर-कथा, f. the de-claration of a Svayaṃ-vara. —स्वयंवर-कृत-क्षण, आ, f. a maiden who has fixed the moment for a Svayaṃ-vara (see above). —स्वयं-वृत, अस्, आ, अम्, self-chosen, selected by one's self. —स्वयं-शीर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, self-fallen, dropped spontaneously. —स्वयं-श्रेष्ठ, अस्, m. epithet of Śiva. —स्व-यं-हारिका, f. ‘self-seizing,’ N. of a daughter of Nir-mārṣṭi (who was wife of Duḥsaha; she is de-scribed in the fifty-first chapter of the Mārkaṇḍeya-Purāṇa as exercising an evil influence on certain sub-stances, by abstracting, for example, the colour from saffron and the thread from cotton). —स्वयङ्-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, self-formed, self-made, natural, sponta-neous; self-done, done by one's self; done to or under-taken for one's self. —स्वयङ्-गुप्ता, f. ‘self-pre-served,’ cowach, Carpopogon Pruriens. —स्वयङ्-ग्रह, अस्, m. the taking for one's self (without leave). —स्वयङ्-ग्राह, अस्, आ, अम्, self-choosing, volun-tary. —स्वयञ्-जात, अस्, आ, अम्, self-born. —स्वयन्-दत्त, अस्, आ, अम्, self-given; a child who has given himself to be adopted by adoptive parents (one of the twelve kinds of children recognised in law-books). —स्वयम्-अर्जित, अस्, आ, अम्, self-acquired, gained by one's own efforts. —स्वयम्-आगत, अस्, आ, अम्, come of one's own accord. —स्वयम्-उक्ति, इस्, f. voluntary declaration; (in law) information, de-position. —स्वयम्-उपस्थित, अस्, आ, अम्, come voluntarily or of one's own accord. —स्वयम्-उपाग-त, अस्, आ, अम्, come of one's own accord; (अस्), m. a child who comes and offers himself voluntarily to an adoptive parent. —स्वयम्-प्रभ, अस्, m. ‘self-shining,’ N. of the fourth Arhat of the future Utsarpiṇī; (आ), f., N. of an Apsaras. —स्वयम्-भु, उस्, m. ‘self-existent,’ Brahmā. —स्वयम्-भुव, अस्, m. ‘self-ex-isting,’ the first Manu; epithet of Brahmā; of Śiva; (आ), f. a kind of shrub (= धूम्र-पत्त्रा). —स्वयम्-भू, ऊस्, m. ‘self-existing,’ the Self-existent, Brahmā; Viṣṇu; Śiva; Kāla or time; Kāma-deva; a Jaina deified sage; N. of the third of the nine black Vāsu-devas; N. of certain plants (= माष-पर्णी; = लिङ्गिनी). —स्वयम्-भूत, अस्, m. ‘self-created,’ epithet of Śiva. —स्वयम्-भोज, अस्, m., N. of a Yādava chief. —स्वयम्-मूर्त, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. self-curdled, coagulated (said of दधि).
स्वयम् स्वयम्, स्वयं-वर, स्वयम्-भू, &c. See p. 1158.
स्वयु: स्वयु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. possessed of opulence, wealthy, (Sāy. = धन-वत्, Ṛg-veda III. 45, 5.)
स्वापय: स्वापय (fr. 1. स्व), Nom. P. स्वापयति, &c., (Vopa-deva XXI. 16.)
स्वामिक: स्वामिक = स्वामिन्, at the end of an adj. comp. (e. g. प्रनष्ट-स्वामिक, whose master or owner is lost or unknown, i. e. not known whether he be alive or dead).
स्वामिन्: स्वामिन्, ई, इनी, इ (fr. 1. स्व with affix मिन्), possess-ing proprietary rights, owning; (ई), m. a proprietor, owner; a master, lord; a sovereign, king, monarch; a husband, lover; a spiritual preceptor; a learned Brāhman, an ascetic or religious man of the highest order (used as a title at the end of names, e. g. श्रीधर-स्वामिन्); N. of Kārttikeya; of Viṣṇu; of Śiva; of the Muni Vātsyāyana; of Garuḍa; of an Arhat of the past era; of several other persons; (इनी), f. a mistress, proprietress; (स्वामिन् at the end of a comp. has frequently the meaning of ‘a temple or shrine built by,’ ‘a temple in honour of,’ e. g. धर्म-स्°, विष्णु-स्°।) —स्वामि-कार्त्तिक, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Rāga-mālā. —स्वामि-कार्त्ति-केयानुप्रेक्षा (°य-अन्°), f., N. of a Jaina work by Jaya-candra. —स्वामि-कार्य, अम्, n. the business of a king or master. —स्वामि-कार्यार्थिन् (°य-अर्°), ई, इनी, इ, desirous of or seeking a master's interests. —स्वामि-जङ्घिन्, ई, m., N. of Paraśu-rāma. —स्वामि-ता, f. or स्वामि-त्व, अम्, n. ownership, mastership; lordship, sovereignty, &c. —स्वामि-पाल, औ, m. du. the owner and the tender (of cattle, Manu VIII. 5). —स्वामि-पाल-विवाद, अस्, m. a dispute be-tween a master and the servant who tends his cattle. —स्वामि-भाव, अस्, m. the state or relation of a lord or owner. —स्वामि-मूल, अस्, आ, अम्, originat-ing in or derived from a master or lord, depending on a master or husband. —स्वामि-वात्सल्य, अम्, n. affection for a lord or husband. —स्वामि-सद्-भाव, अस्, m. existence of a master or owner; amiability of a master or lord. —स्वामि-सेवा, f. the service of a master, respect for a master; reverence for or atten-tion to a husband. —स्वाम्य्-अर्थम्, ind. for a master's sake. —स्वाम्य्-असम्मत, अस्, आ, अम्, un-permitted by a master; one who has not obtained an owner's permission. —स्वाम्य्-उपकारक, अस्, m. ‘serviceable to an owner, benefiting a master,’ a horse.
स्वाम्य: स्वाम्य, अम्, n. mastership, lordship, ownership; right or title to property; rule, supremacy, dominion. —स्वाम्य-कारण, अम्, n. the cause of supremacy or lordship.
स्वाय: स्वाय, Nom. A. स्वायते according to Vopa-deva XXI. 7. = स्व इवाचरति, he acts like himself, he acts like his own kindred.
स्विका: स्विका, f. See under स्वक, col. 1.
स्वीकरण: स्वी-करण, अम्, n. making one's own, appropria-tion, adopting, taking, accepting, assenting, agreeing, assent, promise. —स्वीकरण-कर्मन्, आ, आ, अ, Ved. whose function is to appropriate.
स्वीकरण स्वी-करण, स्वी-कृत, स्वीय, &c. See p. 1158, col. 3.
स्वीकरणीय: स्वी-करणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be appropriated; to be admitted or acknowledged or accepted; to be as-sumed; to be assented or agreed to; to be pro-mised.
स्वीकर्तृ: स्वी-कर्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who appropriates or accepts or admits, &c.
स्वीकार: स्वी-कार, अम्, n. making one's own, taking on one's self, appropriation, adopting, assuming, assump-tion, claiming, claim; assent, agreement, consent; promise. —स्वीकार-रहित, अस्, आ, अम्, devoid of assent, not agreed to. —स्वीकारान्त (°र-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, ended or concluded by assent; agreed to.
स्वीकार्य: स्वी-कार्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be admitted, to be as-sumed (in argument).
स्वीकृ: स्वी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to make one's own, own, win, appropriate, claim; to take upon one's self; to adopt, admit, assume (in argument); to as-sent, agree to.
स्वीकृत: स्वी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, appropriated, owned, ac-cepted, admitted, acknowledged, adopted, claimed, agreed, assented to, promised.
स्वीकृत्य: स्वी-कृत्य, ind. having agreed to or promised; having satisfied.
स्वीय: स्वीय, अस्, आ, अम्, own, relating or belonging to one's self, peculiar, characteristic; (आ), f. one's own wife, a faithful wife, one solely attached to her own husband; [cf. Gr. ἑός, αφέος, σφός.] —स्वीयाक्षर (°य-अक्°), अस्, m. one's own handwriting or signa-ture, autograph, (Śabda-k.)
स्वैर: स्वैर, अस्, ई, अम् (probably fr. स्व + ईर, going; see rts. इर्, ईर्), going where one likes, following one's own fancy, self-willed, wilful, wanton, unre-strained, refractory; slow, lazy; dependent on will, voluntary, optional, unimportant; (अम्), n. wilful-ness; (अम्), ind. with one's own will or assent; of one's own accord. —स्वैर-ता, f. wilfulness, inde-pendence. —स्वैर-वृत्त, अस्, आ, अम्, acting or liv-ing as one likes, following one's own inclinations.
स्वैरिन्: स्वैरिन्, ई, इणी, इ, going where one likes, self-willed, wanton, uncontrolled; (इणी), f. a loose or unchaste woman, an adultress, wanton woman. —स्वैरि-ता, f. wilfulness.
स्वक्क्: स्वक्क् स्वक्क्। See rt. ष्वक्क्, p. 1034, and Vopa-deva VIII. 43.
स्वक्ष: स्वक्ष स्व्-अक्ष, स्व्-अग्नि, स्व्-अङ्ग। See p. 1126, col. 2.
स्वगाकृ: स्वगाकृ स्वगा-कृ, cl. 8. P. A. -करोति, कु-रुते, &c., (said to mean) to put in its place, arrange (perhaps referrible to स्व-ग).
स्वङ्क्: स्वङ्क् स्वङ्क् (= rt. श्वङ्क्), cl. 1. A. स्वङ्-कते, &c., to go, move.
स्वङ्ग्: स्वङ्ग् स्वङ्ग्, cl. 1. P. स्वङ्गति, &c., to go, move (= rt. श्रङ्ग्, p. 1023).
स्वच्छ: स्वच्छ स्व्-अच्छ, स्वच्छ-ता, &c. See p. 1126, col. 2.
स्वञ्ज्: स्वञ्ज् स्वञ्ज् or स्वज् [cf. परि-ष्वञ्ज्], cl. 1. A. स्वजते, सस्वजे, सस्वञ्जे, स्वङ्-क्ष्यते, अस्वङ्क्त, स्वङ्क्तुम्, &c., to embrace, clasp, encircle, twist round: Pass. स्वज्यते, Aor. अस्वञ्जि: Caus. स्वञ्जयति, Aor. असिष्वञ्जत्: Desid. सिस्वङ्क्षते: Intens. सास्वज्यते, सास्वङ्क्ति; [cf. perhaps Germ. Schlange, ‘a snake.’]
स्वक्त: स्वक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, embraced; [cf. परि-ष्वक्त।]
स्वज्यमान: स्वज्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, being embraced.
स्वञ्जन: स्वञ्जन, अम्, n. the act of embracing.
स्वठ्: स्वठ् स्वठ् (= rt. 2. श्वठ्), cl. 10. P. स्वाठयति, &c., to finish, &c.; to go.
स्वद्: स्वद् स्वद् or स्वाद् (probably formed from 5. सु + rt. अद्), cl. 1. A. स्वादनीय: स्वादनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be tasted; tasty, savory.
स्वादित: स्वादित, अस्, आ, अम्, tasted, relished, liked, en-joyed; sweetened; pleased.
स्वादिन्: स्वादिन्, ई, इनी, इ, tasting, drinking.
स्वादिष्ठ: स्वादिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, sweetest, very sweet.
स्वादीयस्: स्वादीयस्, आन्, असी, अस्, sweeter, very sweet.

स्वाद्मन्: स्वाद्मन्, आ, अ, m. n., Ved. sweetness.
स्वधा: स्वधा स्व-धा or स्वधा, f. (fr. स्व + rt. 1. धा; but in Uṇādi-s. IV. 174. connected with rt. स्वद्; cf. स्वदित), Ved. one's own condition or nature, own peculiarity or individuality; innate or inherent power or strength, (स्वधया, by one's own power or strength; Sāy. = स्वकीयेन बलेन, by one's own nature or determination, spontaneously); ‘self-contained, self-sustained,’ N. of Māyā or Pra-kṛti (as the source of the phenomenal world; in this sense Svadhā is sometimes translated ‘Nature,’ as, for example, in the celebrated hymn Ṛg-veda X. 129. आनीद् अवातं स्वधया तद्, ‘that one, i. e. the supreme Being breathed calmly along with Na-ture;’ and in Naigh. III. 30. स्वधे, fem. du., is enumerated among the द्यावा-पृथिवी-नामधे-यानि); manner, habit, custom, usage, (अनु स्वधाम्, according to one's wont or custom, as usual; ac-cording to one's own determination, according to pleasure); one's own portion or share; the sacrificial offering due to each god; the food or oblation offered to the Pitṛs or spirits of deceased ancestors (in this sense especially in later Sanskrit); the Śrād-dha or funeral ceremony itself; the Food or Obla-tion to the Pitṛs &c. personified (as a daughter of Dakṣa and wife of the Pitṛs; also represented as a wife of Aṅgiras, of a Rudra, and of Agni); an ob-lation or offering or food (in general, = अन्न, Naigh. II. 7; = उदक, Naigh. I. 12); (स्वधा), ind. an exclamation or prayer used on presenting an oblation to the gods or Manes of departed ancestors and pro-genitors [cf. स्वाहा, श्रौषट्, वौषट्, वषट्], the highest form of blessing used at a Śrāddha, (स्व-धास्तु, ‘let there be Svadhā!’ this, according to Manu III. 252, is the highest benison at a Śrāddha); [cf. according to some Gr. ἔθ-ος, ἦθ-ος, ἠθεῖο-ς, εἴ-ωθ-α, ἐθ-ίζ-ω; Lat. suetus; Goth. sidus; Angl. Sax. sidu, siodo.] —स्वधा-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, offer-ing oblations to deceased ancestors or deified pro-genitors, performing funeral obsequies (Manu IX. 127); (अस्), m. = स्वधा-कार. —स्वधा-कार, अस्, m. pronouncing the exclamation or blessing स्व-धा; the formula स्वधा. —स्वधा-निनयन, अम्, n. ‘Svadhā-performing,’ a sacred text used in making the oblation to the Pitṛs, (Manu II. 172.) —स्वधा-पति, इस्, m., Ved. lord of the Svadhā. —स्वधा-प्रिय, अस्, m. ‘fond of the Svadhā,’ Agni or fire; black sesamum, (तिल or sesamum being offered to the Manes, Manu III. 267.) —स्वधा-भुज्, क्, m. ‘Svadhā-eating,’ a Pitṛ, deceased or deified ancestor; a deity. —स्वधा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having natural power, self-controlled, self-reliant, in-dependent, powerful, (Sāy. स्वधा-वान् = बल-वान्, Ṛg-veda II. 20, 6; in Ṛg-veda VII. 88, 5. स्व-धावः, voc. case masc. O self-sustaining one, O self-dependent God, Sāy. = अन्नवन्); having the Sva-dhā, rich in oblations; (आन्), m. epithet of Viśva-karman.
स्वधावन्: स्वधावन्, आ, अरी, अ, Ved. abounding in food, (Sāy. स्वधावरी = अन्नवत्यौ, Ṛg-veda VII. 31, 7); self-reliant, independent (perhaps in this sense for स्व-धावन्; cf. स्वधा-वत् above).
स्वधिति: स्वधिति स्वधिति, इस्, m. f. (sometimes writ-ten श्वधिति; fr. स्व + rt. 1. धा), an axe (in Naigh. II. 20. स्वधितिः is enumerated among the वज्र-नामानि). —स्वधिति-हेतिक, अस्, m. ‘axe-armed,’ a soldier armed with an axe.
स्वधिती: स्वधिती, f. an axe. —स्वधिती-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. possessing or holding an axe, having a weapon.

P. स्वनति, सस्वान (3rd pl. सस्वनुस् or स्वेनुस्), स्वनिष्यति, अस्वनीत् or अस्वानीत्, स्वनितुम्, to sound, make a noise; to sing: Caus. स्वनयति, -यितुम्, Aor. असि-स्वनत्, to cause to sound, make to resound; to sound; to adorn (in this sense also स्वानयति, &c.): Desid. सिस्वनिषति: Intens. संस्वन्यते, सं-स्वन्ति; [cf. स्वन: स्वन, अस्, m. sound, noise; voice, speech (in Naigh. स्वनत्: स्वनत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, sounding, resounding.
स्वनिक: स्वनिक, अस्, आ, अम्, sounding (at the end of a comp., e. g. पाणि-स्°, one who claps with the hands).
स्वनित: स्वनित, अस्, आ, अम्, sounded, sounding, making a noise; (अम्), n. the noise of thunder, a thunder-clap. —स्वनिताह्वय (°त-आह्°), अस्, m. a kind of pot-herb (= तण्डुलीय).
स्वानिन्: स्वानिन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. noisy, turbulent.
स्वान्त: 2. स्वान्त, अस्, आ, अम् (for 1. स्वान्त see p. 1158, col. 1), sounded, making a noise.
स्वनय: स्वनय स्वनय, अस्, m., N. of a king (said to have given his ten daughters in marriage to the Ṛṣi Kakṣivat).
स्वप्: स्वप् 2. स्वप् (for 1. स्व्-अप् see p. 1126), cl. 2. P. स्वपिति (2nd sing. स्वपिषि, 1st sing. स्वपिमि, ep. also A. and sometimes even cl. 1. P. सुप्त्वा: सुप्त्वा, ind. having slept, having gone to sleep.
सुषुपाण: सुषुपाण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. sleeping, (Sāy. = सुप्त।)
सुषुप्सु: सुषुप्सु, उस्, उस्, उ, wishing to sleep, sleepy, drowsy.
स्वपत्: स्वपत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, sleeping, asleep, reposing.
स्वपन: स्वपन, अम्, n. the act of sleeping, dreaming, sleep.
स्वपनीय: स्वपनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be slept, &c.
स्वपितिकर्मन्: स्वपिति-कर्मन्, आ, m. one who lies down to sleep (= शयन-कर्तृ).
स्वप्तव्य: स्वप्तव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be slept.
स्वप्तुकाम: स्वप्तु-काम, अस्, आ, अम्, wishing to sleep.
स्वप्तृ: स्वप्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, a sleeper, one who sleeps.

स्वप्नज्: स्वप्नज्, क्, क्, क्, sleepy, drowsy, sleeping, asleep.
स्वाप: स्वाप, अस्, m. sleep, sleeping; dreaming, a dream; sleepiness, sloth; paralysis, palsy, loss of sensation, ignorance; temporary or partial loss of sensation from pressure on a nerve, numbness, the sleep of a limb.
स्वापिन्: स्वापिन्, ई, इनी, इ, causing sleep, lulling to sleep.
स्वपू: स्वपू स्वपू (thought by some to be fr. an old rt. स्वप्, ‘to tear, pull’), Ved. (according to some) a beak, bill of a bird, (in Ṛg-veda VII. 56, 3, Sāy. explains स्व-पूभिस् by स्वकीयैः पव-नैः सञ्चरणैः, by their own pure paths); [cf. Old Germ. snabul, ‘beak;’ Mod. Germ. स्वब्दिन्: स्वब्दिन् स्वब्दिन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. (perhaps) roaring, (Sāy. = शब्दं कुर्वत्, Ṛg-veda VIII. 33, 2.)
स्वमेक: स्वमेक स्वमेक, अस्, m. (etymology doubt-ful), a year (= संवत्सर, according to Śabda-k.).
स्वर्: स्वर् 1. स्वर्, cl. 10. P. स्वरयति, &c., to find fault, blame, censure, reprove (= rt. सुर्).

स्वर् 2. स्वर्, ind. (probably connected with rt. 4. सु or 3. सू, and apparently originally written सुवर्, cf. सूर, सूर्य; but according to some fr. a lost rt. स्वर् = सुर्, ‘to shine,’ cf. सुर), the sun (Ved.; according to Sāy. = स्वरण-शील आदित्य, Ṛg-veda V. 45, 1); heaven, paradise, the world of the gods, abode of the deities; the heaven of Indra and temporary abode of the virtuous after death; the sky, ether; the space above the sun or between the sun and the polar star, the region of the planets and constellations; a mystical word pronounced after ॐ and before the Gāyatrī by every Brāhman in commencing his daily prayers, (it is the third of the three Vyāhṛtis, भूर्, भुवः, स्वर्, and denotes the space of the sky above de-scribed as distinguished from the earth and atmo-sphere, see Manu II. 76. and cf. भुवस्, व्य्-आहृति; the mystical word स्वर् is represented as produced from the Sāma-veda, just as भूर् and भुवः are supposed to come from the Ṛg-veda and Yajur-veda respectively); radiance, splendor; water, (in Naigh. P. -काम्यति, &c., to wish for heaven. —स्वः-पति, इस्, m., Ved. the lord of heaven. —स्वर्-आपगा, f. the river of heaven, the celestial Ganges. —स्वर्-आरूढ, अस्, आ, अम्, ascended to heaven. —स्वर्-आलु, उस्, m. a kind of root (= वचा). —स्वर्-गङ्गा, f. the celestial Ganges; the galaxy. —स्वर्-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, gone to heaven, dead. —स्वर्-गति, इस्, f. or स्वर्-गमन, अम्, n. going to heaven, future felicity; death. —स्वर्-गिरि, इस्, m. ‘the heavenly mountain,’ Su-meru. —स्वर्-जित्, त्, त्, त्, conquering heaven; (त्), m. a proper N.; N. of a kind of sacrifice, (Manu XI. 74; cf. स्वर्ग-जित्।) —स्वर्-णदी, f. the river of heaven, the celestial Ganges; a kind of shrub (= वृश्चिकाली)। —स्वर्-णर, अस्, m., Ved. the lord of heaven; one who leads or is led to heaven, a pious or de-votional man; all-leading, (Sāy. = स्वर्गम् प्रति नेतृ or नेतव्य or सर्वस्य नेतृ); a sacrifice (as leading the offerer to heaven). —स्वर्-दृश्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. looking heavenwards; (क्), m. epithet of Indra; of Agni; of Soma. —स्वर्-नदी, f. = स्वर्-णदी. —स्वर्-पति, इस्, m., Ved. the lord of heaven. —स्वर्-भानव, अस्, m. a kind of precious stone (= गो-मेदक). —स्वर्-भानु, उस्, m., N. of Rāhu or the personified ascending node (repre-sented in Ṛg-veda V. 40, 9. as of the Asura race and as concealing or piercing the sun); N. of a Dānava (regarded as a son of Kaśyapa or, according to other authorities, a son of Vipracitti). —स्वर्-भानु-सूदन, अस्, m. ‘destroyer of Rāhu,’ the sun. —स्वर्-मध्य, अम्, n. the central point of the sky, zenith. —स्वर्-मीऌह, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. happiness-bestowing, (Sāy. = सुख-सेक्तृ); con-ferring heaven, (Sāy. स्वर्-मीऌहेषु = स्वर्ग-दे-शेषु सुखस्य सेचयत्सु, Ṛg-veda I. 130, 8.) —स्वर्-यात, अस्, आ, अम्, gone to heaven, deceased, dead. —स्वर्-यातृ, ता, त्री, तृ, going to heaven, dying. —स्वर्-लोक, अस्, m. the celestial region, heaven. —स्वर्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. full of splen-dor or happiness, heavenly, celestial, (Sāy. = सुख-युक्त, Ṛg-veda VI. 22, 3.) —स्वर्-वधू, ऊस्, f. ‘celestial wife,’ an Apsaras. —स्वर्-वापी, f. ‘heavenly lake,’ the Ganges. —स्वर्-विद्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. obtaining heaven, possessing heaven (said of the Pitṛs, of Indra, &c.). —स्वर्-वेश्या, f. a courtezan of heaven, nymph, Apsaras (such as Urvaśī &c.). —स्वर्-वैद्य, अस्, m. ‘physician of heaven,’ either of the two Aśvins, (see अश्विन्।) —स्वर्-षा, आस्, आस्, अम्, Ved. granting heaven; (आस्), m. epithet of Soma; of the thunderbolt. —स्वर्-षाति, इस्, f., Ved. the granting or gaining of heaven, anything which gains heaven; (इस्, इस्, इ), bestowing or procuring heaven (and hence applied to ‘war, battle;’ according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda X. 99, 3. स्वर्-षाता = स्वर्-षातौ = स्वर्ग-लाभोपेते; in IX. 88, 2 = स्वर्ग-लाभ-युक्ते सङ्ग्रामे, cf. वाज-साति). —स्वस्-तरु, उस्, m. the tree of paradise.
स्वर्ग: स्वर्ग, अस्, m. (according to some for सु-वर्ग), heaven, Indra's paradise, the residence of beatified mortals and of the inferior gods (supposed to be situated on the mountain Meru); N. of a son of Bhīma. —स्वर्ग-काम, अस्, आ, अम्, desirous of heaven. —स्वर्ग-खण्ड, N. of the third book of the Padma-Purāṇa. —स्वर्ग-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, gone to heaven. —स्वर्ग-गमन, अम्, n. going to heaven. —स्वर्ग-गामिन्, ई, इनी, इ, going to heaven. —स्वर्ग-गिरि, इस्, m. ‘the heavenly moun-tain,’ Su-meru. —स्वर्ग-जित्, त्, त्, त्, winning or obtaining paradise. —स्वर्ग-द, अस्, आ, अम्, heaven-giving, procuring paradise. —स्वर्ग-द्वार, अम्, n. heaven's gate, the door of paradise, entrance into heaven; epithet of Śiva. —स्वर्ग-पति, इस्, m. the lord of heaven, Indra. —स्वर्ग-पर, अस्, आ, अम्, intent on heaven, desirous of heaven. —स्वर्ग-भर्तृ, ता, m. the lord of heaven, Indra. —स्वर्ग-मार्ग-दिदृक्षु, उस्, उस्, उ, wishing to see the road to heaven. —स्वर्ग-लोक, अस्, m. the ce-lestial region, (see स्वर्ग); Indra's heaven, para-dise. —स्वर्गलोकेश (°क-ईश), अस्, m. ‘lord of the celestial world,’ Indra; the body (as enjoying felicity in the paradise of Indra). —स्वर्ग-वधू, ऊस्, f. a woman or nymph of Indra's heaven, Apsaras. —स्वर्ग-वास, अस्, m. residence in heaven. —स्वर्ग-वासिन्, ई, इनी, इ, inhabiting heaven. —स्वर्ग-श्री, ईस्, f. the glory of heaven. —स्वर्ग-सम्पादन, अस्, ई, अम्, effecting or procuring heaven, gaining heaven. —स्वर्ग-सरित्, त्, f. the river of heaven. —स्वर्गसरिद्-वरा, f. ‘best of heavenly rivers,’ the Ganges. —स्वर्ग-साधन, अम्, n. a means of attaining heaven. —स्वर्ग-सु-ख, अम्, n. the joy of heaven. —स्वर्ग-स्त्री, f. a woman of paradise, Apsaras. —स्वर्गापगा (°ग-आप्°), f. the celestial river, the Ganges. —स्वर्गा-पवर्ग (°ग-अप्°), अस्, m. heaven-like emanci-pation. —स्वर्गारूढ (°ग-आर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, ascended to heaven. —स्वर्गारोहण (°ग-आर्°), अम्, n. the act of ascending to heaven; N. of certain funeral ceremonies. —स्वर्गारोहण-पर्वन् or स्वर्गारोहणिक-पर्वन्, अ, n., N. of the eighteenth book of the Mahā-bhārata (in which is described the journey of the five Pāṇḍava princes towards Indra's heaven in mount Meru). —स्वर्गेप्सु (°ग-ईप्°), उस्, उस्, उ, desirous of obtaining heaven. —स्वर्-गौकस् (°ग-ओक्°), आस्, m. ‘having an abode in heaven,’ a god, deity.
स्वर्गिन्: स्वर्गिन्, ई, इणी, इ, belonging to heaven, being in heaven, heavenly; (ई), m. an inhabitant of heaven, a god, deity, celestial; (in law) ‘in heaven,’ a dead person. —स्वर्गि-गिरि, इस्, m. the celestial moun-tain, Su-meru. —स्वर्गि-वधू, ऊस्, f. a celestial woman, Apsaras.
स्वर्गीय: स्वर्गीय, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging or relating to Svarga, heavenly, celestial; conducive to heaven, leading to heaven.
स्वर्ग्य: स्वर्ग्य, अस्, आ, अम्, = स्वर्गीय above.
स्वर्य: स्वर्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. heavenly, celestial.
स्वर्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. to be praised.
स्वर्यु: स्वर्यु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. wishing for heaven; de-siring happiness.
स्वर: स्वर स्वर, स्वरित, स्वरितृ। See rt. स्वृ।

स्वर, अस्, m. sound, noise; voice; tone, tune, music, a primary musical sound, note of the musical scale or gamut (of which there are seven, commonly thus arranged, 1. निषाद, 2. ऋषभ, 3. गान्-धार, 4. षड्ज, 5. मध्यम, 6. धैवत, 7. पञ्चम; these notes are described as resem-bling respectively the notes of an elephant, bull, goat, peacock, curlew or heron, horse, and Koil; they are designated by their initial letters or syllables thus, नि, ऋ, ग, ष, म, ध, प, and the order is some-times changed, षड्ज being placed first, पञ्चम fifth, and निषाद last); a symbolical expression for the number seven; a vowel (either ह्रस्व short, दीर्घ long, or प्लुत prolated); an accent, tone (of which there are three, viz. उदात्त, अनुदात्त, and स्वरित, see below); air breathed through the nostrils, nasal sound; snoring; (आ), f., N. of the chief wife of Brahmā (Gāyatrī being the other). —स्वर-गता-ध्यय (°त-अध्°), अस्, m., N. of the first book of the Saṅgīta-darpaṇa; of the first book of the Saṅ-gīta-ratnākara. —स्वर-ग्राम, अस्, m. the musical scale, gamut. —स्वर-तत्त्वोदय (°व-उद्°), अम्, n., N. of treatise on astrology by Jīva-nātha. —स्वर-पत्तन, अम्, n. ‘abode of accents,’ N. of the Sāma-veda (this Veda being chanted with a peculiar rhythm, and the efficacy of its prayers depending on their proper accentuation). —स्वर-बद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, composed in musical measure (said of a song &c.). —स्वर-भक्ति, इस्, f. ‘vowel-fracture,’ (in Vedic phonetics) a vowel-sound phonetically inserted in the pronunciation of र् or ल् when these letters are fol-lowed by a sibilant or other consonant without the intervention of a vowel (e. g. वर्ष pronounced वरिष). —स्वर-भङ्ग, अस्, m. interruption or indistinctness of utterance, broken articulation, crack-ing of the voice, hoarseness, fluttering of the voice, any defect in speaking (caused by emotion or morbid affections of the chest). —स्वर-भङ्गिन्, ई, m. ‘note-separating,’ a kind of bird. —स्वर-भेद, अस्, m. = स्वर-भङ्ग above. —स्वर-मण्ड-लिका, f. a kind of Vīṇā or stringed musical instru-ment (also read सुर-खण्डलिका). —स्वर-लासिका, f. a flute, pipe. —स्वर-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having sound, sonorous; having a voice, vocal; having an accent, accentuated. —स्वर-शास्त्र, अम्, n. a trea-tise on the modulations of sound or on the passage of the air through the nostrils. —स्वर-शुद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, correct in musical measure. —स्वर-शून्य, अस्, आ, अम्, devoid of sound, without musical notes, unmelodious, unmusical. —स्वर-संयोग, अस्, m. the junction of vowels. —स्वर-सङ्क्रम, अस्, m. a transition or succession of sounds or notes; the musical scale, gamut. —स्वर-सन्धि, इस्, m. the junction or coalition of vowels. —स्वर-सामन्, आनस्, m. pl. epithet of particular days in a Sattra or sacrificial session. —स्वरांश (°र-अं°), अस्, m. a half or quarter tone in music. —स्वरान्तर (°र-अन्°), अम्, n. ‘vowel-interval,’ the interval between two vowels, hiatus, = विवृत्ति; (ए), ind. in the middle of vowels, between two vowels. —स्वरोदय (°र-उद्°), अस्, m. the arising or production of sound (thought to be connected with certain tubular vessels of the body); (अस्, अम्), m. n., N. of a work on that subject; an astro-logical dissertation on the indications which the human breath affords under particular circumstances and astral conjunctions of the duration of life and future events; (अस्, आ, अम्), followed by a vowel. —स्वरोदय-विवरण, N. of a work on the tubular vessels of the body (regarded as passages of air and channels of sound). —स्वरोपध (°र-उप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, preceded by a vowel.
स्वरु: स्वरु, उस्, m. sunshine; a sacrifice; part of a sacrificial post (or a slip of wood from it); the sacri-ficial post, (Sāy. = यूप); a thunderbolt; an arrow; a kind of scorpion; (उस्, उस्, उ), Ved. (perhaps) per-fect, entire, (Sāy. = स्वरवः = स्व-शकलवन्तः, Ṛg-veda III. 8, 6.)
स्वरेणु: स्वरेणु स्वरेणु, उस्, f. (etymology doubt-ful), N. of a wife of the Sun (= 2. सञ्-ज्ञा).
स्वर्जिक: स्वर्जिक स्वर्जिक, अस्, m. (= सर्जि, सर्जिका), natron, nitrate of potash.
स्वर्ण: स्वर्ण स्वर्ण, अम्, n. (contracted fr. सु-वर्ण, q. v.), gold; a gold coin. —स्वर्ण-कण, अस्, m. a grain of gold; ‘having golden grains or seeds,’ a kind of plant (= कण-गुग्गुलु). —स्वर्-ण-कणिका, f. a particle of gold, grain of gold. —स्वर्ण-कदली, f. = सुवर्ण-कदली. —स्वर्-ण-काय, अस्, आ, अम्, golden-bodied; (अस्), m. Garuḍa. —स्वर्ण-कार, अस्, or स्वर्ण-कृत्, त्, m. a gold-worker, goldsmith (forming a particular caste). —स्वर्ण-केतकी, f. a sort of Ketakī tree with golden-coloured or yellow blossoms. —स्वर्ण-क्षीरी, f. ‘having gold-like milk or sap,’ a kind of Soma or moon-plant with yellow juice (used for medicinal purposes and said to be brought from the Himālaya mountains; cf. हिमा-वती). —स्वर्ण-गैरिक, अम्, n. a kind of yellow ochre or red chalk. —स्वर्ण-ग्राम, N. of a country situated to the east of Dacca. —स्वर्ण-ग्रीवा, f. ‘golden-necked,’ N. of a river issuing from the eastern side of the Nāṭaka mountain. —स्वर्ण-चूड, अस्, m. ‘golden-crested,’ the blue jay; a cock. —स्वर्ण-ज, अम्, n. ‘gold-produced,’ the metal tin. —स्वर्ण-जीवन्ती, f. a kind of plant (= तृण-ग्रन्थि)। —स्वर्ण-दीधिति, इस्, m. ‘golden-rayed,’ fire. —स्वर्ण-द्रु, उस्, m. a kind of tree with yellow blossoms (= आरग्-बध). —स्वर्ण-पक्ष, अस्, m. ‘golden-winged,’ Garuḍa. —स्वर्ण-पद्मा, f. ‘bearing golden lotuses,’ the celestial Ganges. —स्वर्-ण-पाठक, अस्, m. borax (= टङ्कण). —स्वर्ण-पारेवत, अम्, n. a kind of tree (= महा-पारे-वत). —स्वर्ण-पुष्प, अस्, ई, अम्, having golden-coloured flowers or yellow blossoms; (अस्), m. the tree Ārag-badha; the Campaka tree; (आ), f. the gum-arabic tree and other plants, = कलि-कारी; = स्वर्णुली; = सातला; (ई), f. the tree Ārag-badha; the golden Ketakī tree; a sort of moon-plant. —स्वर्ण-प्रस्थ, N. of an island. —स्वर्ण-फला, f. ‘having golden fruit,’ a kind of plant. —स्वर्ण-बणिज्, क्, m. a gold-merchant, money-changer. —स्वर्ण-बन्ध or स्वर्ण-बन्धक, अस्, m. a deposit of gold. —स्वर्ण-भृङ्गार, अस्, m. a golden vase; a kind of plant (= स्वर्ण-भृङ्गराज). —स्वर्ण-महा, f. a particular river (mentioned in the eighty-second chapter of the Kālikā-Purāṇa). —स्वर्ण-माक्षिक, अम्, n. a mineral substance (= सुवर्ण-म्°, q. v.). —स्वर्ण-यूथी or स्वर्ण-यूथिका, f. yellow jasmine. —स्वर्-ण-रेखा, f. a streak of gold; N. of a woman. —स्वर्ण-लता, f. ‘golden creeper,’ a kind of plant (= ज्योतिष्मती). —स्वर्ण-वर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, gold-coloured; (आ), f. turmeric. —स्वर्ण-वल्कल, अस्, m. ‘having golden bark,’ the plant Bignonia Indica. —स्वर्ण-वल्ली, f. a kind of plant (= रक्त-फला). —स्वर्ण-विन्दु, उस्, m. a spot of yellow or gold; ‘having a gold mark or dot,’ epithet of Viṣṇu. —स्वर्णविन्दु-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —स्वर्ण-शृङ्ग, अस्, ई, अम्, golden-horned. —स्वर्ण-शेफालिका, f. a kind of yellow Śephā-likā; the tree Cassia Fistula (= आरग्-बध)। —स्वर्णाङ्ग (°ण-अङ्°), अस्, m. ‘golden-bodied,’ the Ārag-badha tree. —स्वर्णारि (°ण-अरि), इस्, m. ‘enemy to gold,’ sulphur.
स्वर्णक: स्वर्णक, अस्, आ, अम्, golden, made of gold.
स्वर्णकूठ: स्वर्णकूठ स्वर्णकूठ, N. of a sacred place.
स्वर्णुली: स्वर्णुली स्वर्णुली, f. a kind of shrub (= स्वर्ण-पुष्पा).
स्वर्त्: स्वर्त् स्वर्त् = rt. श्वर्त्, p. 1030, col. 3.
स्वर्द्: स्वर्द् स्वर्द्, cl. 1. A. स्वर्दते, सस्वर्दे, स्वर्दितुम्, to taste; to be pleasing.
स्वल्: स्वल् स्वल्, cl. 1. P. स्वलति, सस्वाल, &c., to go (?) .
स्वल्प: स्वल्प स्व्-अल्प, अस्, आ, अम्, very small or little, minute, trifling, insignificant; very few; (एन), ind. for a very short time. —स्वल्प-कङ्क, अस्, m. a species of heron (= भू-काक). —स्वल्प-केशरिन्, ई, m. ‘having minute filaments,’ the Kovidāra tree. —स्वल्प-केशिन्, ई, m. ‘having small fibres,’ the root of sweet flag. —स्वल्प-जातक, अम्, n., N. of a work by Varāha-mihira; [cf. वृहज्-जातक।] —स्वल्प-पत्त्रक, अस्, m. ‘small-leaved,’ a kind of Madhūka or Bassia Latifolia. —स्वल्प-फला, f. ‘having small fruit,’ a kind of plant (= कच्छु-घ्नी, अ-पराजिता). —स्वल्प-बल, अस्, आ, अम्, having very little strength, extremely weak or feeble; attended by a very small force. —स्वल्प-विषय, अस्, m. a very small matter, insignificant object; a small part. —स्वल्प-व्यय, अस्, m. very little expenditure, great stinginess; (अस्, आ, अम्), spending very little, very niggardly. —स्वल्प-व्रीड, अस्, आ, अम्, having little shame, shameless, impudent. —स्वल्प-शरीर, अस्, आ, अम्, having a very dimi-nutive body, small in stature. —स्वल्प-शिला, f. a very small stone. —स्वल्प-शिलाय, Nom. A. -शिला-यते, &c., to act like a very small stone, to become a very small stone. —स्वल्पाहार (°प-आह्°), अस्, आ, अम्, eating very little, most abstemious.
स्वल्पक: स्वल्पक, अस्, आ, अम्, very little, very small, very few.
स्वल्पीयस्: स्वल्पीयस्, आन्, असी, अस्, much less, (Manu XI. 8.)
स्वसर: स्वसर स्व-सर (see p. 1157), अम्, n. (pro-bably fr. स्व + सर), Ved. ‘self-moving, self-revolv-ing,’ epithet of the sun, (Sāy. = स्वसरस्य = स्व-यं सर्तुर् आदित्यस्य, Ṛg-veda V. 62, 2); a day, (Sāy. = अहन्, Ṛg-veda I. 34, 4, Naigh. I. 9); a house, abode, nest, (Sāy. स्वसराणि = स्वकीयानि निवास-स्थानानि, Ṛg-veda II. 34, 5; in Naigh. II. 4. enumerated among the गृह-नामानि); one's own place of going.
स्वसृ: स्वसृ स्वसृ, सा, f. (according to Uṇādi-s. स्वरित: स्वरित, अस्, आ, अम्, sounded; sounded as a note, pitched; articulated; accented; having the mixed or circumflex accent, circumflexed; (अस्), m. the third or mixed tone between high and low, which is thought to correspond with the circumflex accent, (the other two tones being called Ud-ātta and An-udātta, q.q. v.v.; the Ud-ātta sound of a vowel is said to result from the employing the upper half of the organs of utterance, and the An-udātta from em-ploying the lower half, while the Svarita represents a sustained mixed intonation neither high nor low, which is well illustrated by the expression तिर्यग्-गमन, i. e. a horizontal or wavy movement of the hand as distinguished from a direct upward and downward motion; Pāṇini, however, applies the term अन्-उदात्त, ‘non-elevated,’ to the neutral accent-less tone, and uses the term सन्न-तर or अन्-उदात्त-तर for ‘the very or proper An-udātta,’ i. e. the true grave accent which precedes the Udātta; in I. 2, 31. he calls the Svarita सम्-आहार, i. e. ‘a combination’ of the elevated and non-elevated tones; the Svarita accent is denoted in the Ṛg-veda by a small upright stroke above the syllable, the Anudātta-tara by a horizontal mark underneath, and the Udātta is left unmarked; but the Svarita mark may denote either a dependent or an independent Svarita, i. e. one produced by an Udātta immediately preceding or a real Svarita belonging to the word itself, and commonly produced by the suppression of an Udātta syllable; again, as a word is supposed to have only one real accent, so words which have real Svaritas of their own do not have Udātta accents; they are called आदि-स्वरित, मध्य-स्वरित, अन्त-स्वरित, according as they have Svaritas on the first, middle, or last syllable; it must also be borne in mind that when a dependent Svarita is immediately followed by an Udātta, the Svarita becomes a kind of Anudātta-tara, and is so marked, see ताथाभाव्य; there were, doubtless, different kinds of Svarita pronunciation.) —स्वरित-त्व, अम्, n. the state of having the Svarita accent. —स्वरितोपध (°त-उप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, pre-ceded by the Svarita; having the penultimate marked with the Svarita.
